The body that is corrupted overloads the soul, and the earthly habitation depresses the mind that thinks about many things. Who will I talk to? Who is to hear? Who will understand where we must be after this life if we ascend with our hearts? Then, since no one will understand it, wait then for some ineffable place of bliss established for you by the one who also ordained ascensions in your heart. But where? In the valley of tears. The valley symbolizes humility; the mountain, the greatness. There is a mountain to climb: a certain spiritual greatness. And what is this mountain that we climb? Our Lord Jesus Christ. He who made for you, while suffering, the valley of weeping, made, while remaining, the mountain of ascent. What is this valley of tears?: The Word became flesh and lived among us. What is this valley of tears?: He offered his cheek to the one who hurt him and was saturated with reproaches. What is this valley of tears?: He was buffeted, spit upon, crowned with thorns and crucified: this is the valley of tears from which he must ascend for you. But where should it go up? In the beginning there was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. But the Word became flesh and lived among us. He came down to you, remaining in himself; He came down to you to become a valley of tears for you; It remained in itself, being for you a mountain of ascent. Verbum caro factum est, et babitavit in nobis. Quid est vallis plorationis? Praebuit percutienti se maxillam; saturatus est opprobiis (Thren 3,30). Quid est vallis plorationis? Colaphizatus est, sputis illinitus, spinis coronatus, crucifixus est. Haec est vallis plorationis unde tibi ascendendum est. Sed in quo ascendendum est? In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum et Deus erat Verbum. Ipsum enim Verbum caro jactum est, et babitavit in nobis (lo 1,1.14). Sic descendit ad te, ut maneret in se: descendit ad te, ut ieront tibi convallis plorationis; mansit in se, ut esset tibi mons ascensionis. Those who did not want to climb through the valley of tears were forced by Him. They hurriedly wanted to climb up; They thought of high honors, but not of the path of humility. The Lord saw that they thought hastily and disorderly about honors, when above all they should learn to humble themselves in order to be exalted; and therefore he says to them: Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink? Therefore, brothers, let us sing this psalm of ascent, those of us who are to ascend in our hearts, since in order for us to ascend he came down to us (Christ). We can assume that those who he saw rising symbolized those who profit, and those who he saw falling, those who faint, because, without a doubt, we find this in the people of God, for some profit and others Sed noli aliquid terrenum cogitare, nec quia montem audisti, alta quaedam cogites terrae: nec cum saxum audis aut petram, duritia a te intelligatur; nec cum audis leonem, cogites feritatem; nec cum audis agnum, cogites pecus. Nihil horum est in se, et omnia factus est prote te. Hinc ergo ascendendum est, iiluc ascendendum; ab exemplo ipsius, ad divinitatem ipsius. Exemplum enim tibí fecit humiliando se. However, not only He comes down. From heaven certainly only He comes down; But many saints, imitating him, come down and come down to us, because the Apostle lived at a certain height of the heart when he said: Let us go out with our minds to God. What he had surpassed with his mind, he had done for God. Overcoming with his mind all human frailty, all the temporal things of the century, all things that in whatever way disappear by being born and dying, passing over all these passing things, he dwelt with his heart, as far as he could, in a certain ineffable contemplation, of which he says he heard ineffable words that it is not possible for man to express. He certainly couldn't express them to you; However, he could still see the things he couldn't express to you. This existed in the beginning in God. All things were made by Him, and without Him nothing was made. Understand it if you can; take hold of it; It is food. Perhaps you must tell me: "He is food, I am a child; I must be breastfed to make myself able to eat the food." As you must be fed with milk and He is a solid delicacy, that is why this delicacy passed into your mouth through meat. Just as the mother eats the delicacy to give it to the infant made into milk through the flesh, so the Lord, the bread of angels, made into flesh, became milk. Hence the Apostle says: I gave you milk to drink, not food, because you were not yet capable, nor are you even now. Then, giving milk, she went down to the children; and because it descended, it descended. And thus he says: Did I intend to know anything among you other than knowing Christ, and him crucified? Longitudo illa dierum, aeternitas est. Hoc enim proprio moda dicit Scriptura longum, quod aeternum est: nam quidquid finem habet, brief est. Alio loco: Longitudine, inquit, dierum replebo eum

Would it be a great thing to say: Honor your father and mother so that you may enjoy a long life on earth? On what land? About the one that says: You are my hope, my portion in the land of the living. What does it mean that life is long there? That one lives eternally, since being long-lived here is nothing more than reaching old age; And no matter how long life may seem, when it comes to an end, one knows that it is short, since it ends. Furthermore, many who curse their parents grow old in the earth, and others who obey them soon turn to the Lord. So, is it true that one lives long according to this life? Therefore, "long-lived" was written for "eternity." Longevity is assigned to the right, but glory and riches to the left; that is, what is sufficient for this life, the things that are considered good by men. An individual approaches and tries to hurt your right, that is, take away your faith. You received the slap on the right; You offer him the left, that is, let him take what is temporary and not what you have eternal. Hear the apostle Saint Paul act in this way. The men persecuted him because he was a Christian; He was wounded on the right, he offers the left: I am, he says, a Roman citizen. They despised the right, he terrified the left. Since they did not yet believe Christ, they could not fear his right. Then what will we say? That, if the right embraces, the left is under the head. Well, what does it mean: Your left does not know what your right is doing? That, when you do good, work for eternal life. Because, if you do good in (Ps 90,16). Et numquid aliter pro magno diceretur, Honora patrem tuum et matrem tuam, ut longaevus sis super terram? (Ex 20:12). Super quam enim terram, nisi de qua dicit: Spes mea es tu, portio mea in tena vivostium? (Ps 141.6). Ibi esse longaevum est, nisi ibi vivere in aeternum? Nam hic esse longaevum quid est, nisi ad senectutem pervenire? Etsi longa videtur aetas, cum pervenerit, brevis convincitur; quia finitur. Et multi maledicentes parentibus, senescunt in hac terra; multi autem obsequentes parentibus, I quote eunt ad Dominum. Numquid ergo impletur, ut longaevus sit secundum hanc vitam? Sed longaevum pro aeternitate illa positum est. Longaevitas est in dextera eius; at vero divitiae et gloria, id est sufficientia vitae huius, ea quae bona existimantur ab hominibus, sinistra est.

Nescio quis venit, et vult tibi percutere dexteram, id est, tollere tibi fidem tuam: tu accepisti alapam in dexteram, praebe sinistram (Mt 5,39), id est, ut illud tollat quod temporale est, et non ea quae aeterna habes. Audite Paulum apostolum hoc facientem, Homines persequebantur in eo quod christianus erat; percutitur lili dextera, ille sinistram opponebat: Civis Romanus sum, ait (Act 22,25). Dexteram contemnebant illi, et de sinistra terrebat ille: quia illi dexteram eius timere non poterant; nondum enim Christo crediderant. Quid ergo, si dextera amplectitur, sinistra sub capite est; quid est, Nesciat sinistra tua quid facial dextera tua? Id est, quando facis bonum opus, propter vitam aeternam fac. Nam si opus bonum in terra proptetea feceris, ut terrena tibi abundent; scit sinistra tua quid faciat dextera tua, miscuisti

the earth, so that earthly things may multiply for you, then your left will know what your right is doing. Work only for eternal life. Do it like this and you will work safely; God ordered this. If what you do you do only for earthly goods and for the life of the world, only the left acts. But if you work for eternal life, work only the right one. If you direct your intention toward eternal life, and yet, when you perform the good work, the greed of temporal life interferes with you so that you look for it so that something is granted to you here, the left is mixed in the works of the right; God forbids this. 11. Let's go back to what the psalm says: The Lord is your protection on the hand of your right. Call power a hand. How do I test it? Because the power of God was called the hand of God. The devil, who tempted Job, says this to God: Stretch out your hand and touch everything he has, and you will see if he truly blesses you. What does it mean extend your hand? Gives power. Hear it more clearly, brother, do not perhaps happen that you still judge with carnal sense that God consists of members; He clearly hears how power is called a hand. The Scripture says in a certain place: Death and life, in the hands of the tongue. We know that the tongue is a small member of flesh; It moves in the mouth, hurting the palate and teeth, thus forming the sounds with which we speak. The hands of the tongue are shown to me. The tongue has no hands and it has hands. What are your hands? His power. What does it mean: Death and life are in the hands of the tongue? Through your mouth you will be justified and through your mouth you will be condemned. Then dexteram sinistrae. Noli faceré nisi propter vitam aeternam. Ideo fac, et securus facies: hoc enim mandavit Deus. Si propter solas res humanoes et solam vitam istam facis quod facis, sinistra sola operatur; si autem propter vitam aeternam operaris, dextera sola operatur: si autem habes intentionem ad vitam aeternam, sed subrepit tibi cupiditas vitae temporalis, ut attendas etiam istam quando facis opus bonum, ut hic tibi aliquid retribuatur, miscet se sinistra operibus dexterae: hoc vetat Deus. 11. Veniamus nunc ad illud quod ait Psalmus: Dominus tegumentum tuum super manum dexterae tuae. Manum potestatem dicit. Unde probamus? Quia et manus Dei, potestas Dei dicta est. Nam diabolus, qui tentavit Iob, hoc ait Deo: Mitte manum tuam, et tange omnia quae habet; et vide, si in faciem benedicet tibi (Iob 1,11). Quid est, Mitte manum tuam, nisi, da potestatem?

Evidentius audi, frater, ne forte carnali sensu adhuc cogites quia membris distinctus est Deus; audi evidenter quomodo dicatur manus potestas. Ait quodam loco Scriptura: Mors et vita in manibus linguae (Prov 18:21). Ñovimus linguas frusta quaedam carnis; in ore moventur, et percutiendo palatum et dentes, distinguishing sons quibus loquimur: ostendantur mihi manus linguae. Lingua ergo non habet manus, et habet manus. Quae sunt manus linguae? Potestas linguae. Quid est, Mors et vita in manibus linguae? Ex ore tuo iustificaberis, et ex ore tuo condemnaberis (Mt 12:37). If the hands are the power, what does right hand mean? I believe that nothing else is more aptly understood by hand than the power that God gave you so that, if you wish, He granting it to you, you may stand on the right, since all the wicked will be on the left, and all the good children, to whom it will be said: Come, you blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom that was prepared for you from the beginning of the world, at the right hand; That is, so that you could become a child of God you received the power. What power? The one about whom Saint John says: He gave them the power to become children of God. How did you receive this power? Believing in his name. Then, if you believe, you were given the power to be among the children of God. Being counted among the children of God is the same as belonging to the right. Therefore your faith is your right hand; that is, the power that was given to you to be among the children of God is the hand of your right. But what is the power that man received worth if the Lord does not protect him? See what he believes; He already walks in faith; but it is weak, it stirs between temptations, between restlessness, between carnal corruption, between the suggestions of greed, between the snares and snares of the enemy. So what is the point of having power and believing in Christ to find yourself among the children of God? Woe to the man whose faith the Lord does not protect! This means that God does not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear, as the Apostle says: God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear. Even when we are already faithful, even when the hand on our right is already

In us, the same God, who does not allow us to be tempted more than we can, protects us with the hand of our right. It is not enough for us to have the right hand if He does not also protect the same right hand. 12 [v.6]. Notice I said this about temptations. Pay attention to what follows: May the Lord protect you on the hand of your right. I explained it, and I think you understood it. Well, if you had not understood what I said and what the Scripture said, you would not have shown me with your acclamations that you understood it. Then, because you understood it, pay attention to what follows: why the Lord also protects the right hand, that is, faith, by which we have received the power to be children of God and to be on the right hand, and why it is appropriate that the Lord protect. Because of scandals or setbacks. Where do the scandals come from? Two things are to be feared, since there are two precepts on which all the law and the prophets hang: the love of God and neighbor. The Church is loved out of concern for one's neighbor; to God, for God's sake. God, figuratively, is called the sun, and the Church, the moon. Anyone who can err by believing that God is something other than what is appropriate to believe and does not believe that the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit are a single substance, was deceived by the malice of the heretics, and mainly of the Arians. If you believe that there is something less in the Son or in the Holy Spirit than in the Father, you have stumbled over God and are burned by the sun. He who, on the other hand, believes that the Church is found in one place only and does not recognize it as spread throughout the world, and, therefore, believes those who

If manus potestas, what is manus dexterae? Nihil arbitrar intelligi congruentius, nisi ut intelligamus manum dexterae, potestatem quam tibí dedit Deus, ut si velis, donor Deo, ad dexteram sis. Erunt enim impii omnes ad sinistram; erunt autem omnes filii boni ad dexteram, quibus dicetur: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi (ib. 25,34). Ut autem sis ad dexteram, id est, ut possis Dei filius fieri, potestatem accepisti. What potestatem? De qua dicit Ioannes, Dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri. Unde accepisti hanc potestatem? Credentibus, inquit, in nomine eius (lo 1,12). Si ergo credis, ipsa tibi potestas data est, ut sis inter filos Dei. Esse autem inter filos Dei, hoc est ad dexteram pertinete. Ergo fides tua, manus dexterae tuae; id est, potestas quae tibi data est, ut sis inter filios Dei, manus est dexterae tuae. Sed quid valet ipsa potestas quam accepit homo, nisi Dominus protegat? Ecce credidit, iam ambulat in fide: iníirmus est, inter temptationes agitatur, inter inconveniences, inter carnales corruptiones, intet suggestiones cupiditatis, inter versutias et laquees inimici. Quid valet ergo, quia habet potestatem, et credidit in Christum, ut sit inter filios Dei? Vae homini illi, nisi et ipsius fidem Dominus protegat: id est, ut non te permittat tentari supra quam potes ferré; sicut dicit Apostolus, Fidelis Deus, qui non vos permittet tentari supra quam potestis ferré (1 Cor 10:13). Ule ergo qui non sinit tentari supra quam possumus ferré, quanvis iam fideles simus, quamvis iam manus dexterae nostrae sit in nobis, protegit nos Deus super manum

dexterae nostrae. Non nobis sufficit habere manum dexterae, nisi ille et ipsam manum dexterae protegat. 12 [v.6]. Ecce hoc de tentationibus dixi: intendite quid sequatur: Protegat te Dominus super manum dexterae tuae. Dixi, et, quod arbitrar, recognovistis. Si enim non recognovissetis, et de Scripturis non recognovissetis, non vocibus vestris intellectum vestrum mihi significaretis. Ergo quia intellexistis, fratres, videte quid sequitur; quare protegat Dominus et super manum dexterae, id est, super ipsam fidem, in qua potestatem accepimus esse filios Dei, et esse ad dexteram: quare oportet ut protegat Dominus? Ptopter scandala. Unde sunt scandala? De duobus timenda sunt scandala, quia et duo sunt praecepta in quibus tota Lex pendet et Prophetae, dilectio Dei et proximi (Mt 22,37-40). Ecclesia propter proximum diligitur, Deus autem propter Deum. In Deo, intelligitur figurate dictus sol: in Ecclesia, intelligitur figurate dicta luna. Quisquis potest errare, ut aliud de Deo credat quam oportet, non credat Patrem et Filium et Spiritum sanctum unius esse substantiae, deceptus est versutia haeteticorum, especially Arianorum. Yes aliquid minus in Filio, aut minus in Spiritu sancto quam in Patre crediderit, passus est scandalum in Deo; a sole uritur. Quisquis rursus putaverit Ecclesiam in una parte esse, et non eam cognoverit diffusam toto orbe terrarum, et crediderit eis qui dicunt, Ecce hic est Christus, et ecce illie (ib. 24,23), sicut moda audistis cum Evangelium legeretur; cum ille totum orbem

They say: See, here is Christ; See, there it is, as you heard when the gospel was read recently, since He bought the whole earth, giving an immense price, stumbles on his neighbor and is burned by the moon. He who errs in the substance of truth is burned by the sun and during the day, because he errs in the same wisdom, of which it was said: The day announces the word to the day. Hence the Apostle says: We provide the spiritual to the spiritual. The day announces the day the word (means): We provide the spiritual to the spiritual. The day announces the day the word means: We speak wisdom among the perfect. And what does it mean and the night announces the night science? That the humility of Christ is preached to the little ones, because this is milk, which is sufficient for the little ones. However, infants are not left abandoned at night, because at night the moon also shines, that is, the Church is announced through the flesh of Christ, since this flesh is the Head of the Church. Whoever does not stumble here, that is, in the Church and in the flesh of Christ, is not burned by the moon. Whoever has not stumbled in the Immutable and Uncontaminated Truth is not burned by the sun. I am not saying that it is not burned by the sun that animals and flies see with us, but by that sun of which the wicked will finally say: What did pride profit us? And what did boasting of riches bring us? All these things passed away like shadows; and, having said this, they will add: Then we turned away from the path of truth and the light of righteousness did not shine on us, nor was the sun born for us. Does this material sun not rise for all the wicked, having been ordained by Him from whom

It is said that he makes his sun rise on the good and the bad? Then Oíos made a sun that makes it rise on the good and the bad, this sun that the good and the bad see. But there is another sun, not made, but begotten, and by which all things were created, and in it is found the immutable wisdom of truth. Of this the wicked say: The sun was not born for us. Whoever does not err in wisdom is not burned by the sun. Anyone who does not err in the Church, in the flesh of the Lord, in the things that were temporarily done for us, is not burned by the moon. However, any man, even if he had already believed in Christ, errs here or there, that is, in one way or another, if what was said does not take place in him: The Lord is your protector on the hand of your right. Therefore, when he said: The Lord is your protector on the hand of your right, as if the same psalmist asked and said: "Behold the hand of my right, behold, I have already chosen to believe in Christ, that I received the power to be a son of God; why then is God still my protector above, that is, on the hand of my right?" He then explains it, saying: Because the sun will not burn you during the day, nor the moon during the night. It is your protector over the hand of your right so that the sun does not burn you during the day, nor the moon during the night. Understand, brothers, that it was spoken here figuratively. In fact, if we think about the visible sun, (we see) that it burns during the day. But does the moon burn at night? What is usrion? The scandal or setback. Listen to the Apostle, who says: Who gets sick that I don't get sick? Who is scandalized or stumbles that I am not burned?

Quisquís ergo errat in ipsa substantia veritatis, a sole uritur, et per diem uritur; quia in ipsa sapientia errat, de qua dictum est, Dies diei eructat verbum: unde dicit et Apostolus, Spiritualibus spiritualia comparantes. Dies diei eructat verbum; Spiritualibus spiritualia comparadores. Dies diei eructat verbum; Sapientiam loquimur interperfects (1 Cor 2,13:6). Quid est nox nocti annuntiat scientiam? (Ps 18,3). Parvulis praedicatur humilitas Christi, et caro Christi, et crucifixio Christi; quia ipsum est lac quod sufficit parvulis. Et ideo non relinquuntur in nocte parvuli, quia luzet et luna etiam in nocte; id est, per carnem Christi praedicatur Ecclesia, quia ipsa caro Christi caput Ecclesiae est. Quisquis ibi non scandalizatur, in ipsa Ecclesia et carne Christi, a luna non uritur. Quisquis scandalizatus non fuerit in veritate illa incommutabili et incontaminabili, a sole non uritur: non isto solé non uritur, quem nobiscum vident musmae et pécora; sed iUo sole de quo dicunt impii in fine, Quid nobis profuit superbia? et divitiarum iactatio quid contulit nobis? Transierunt omnia tanquam umbra. Et cum ista dixissent: Ergo, inquiunt, erravimus a via veritatis et iustitiae lumen non luxit nobis, et sol non ortus est nobis (Wis 5,6-9). est: Qui facit solem suum oriri super bonds et malo? (Mt 5,45). Ergo alium solem fecit Deus, qui oritur super bonds et malo, istum quem vident et boni et mali; alius est autem ille sol, non factus, sed genitus, per quem facta sunt omnia, ubi est intelligentia incommutabilis veritatis: de ipso dicunt impii, Et sol non ortus est nobis. Quisquis in ipsa sapientia non errat, non uritur a sole. Quisquis in Ecclesia, et in carne Domini, et in bis quae pro nobis temporaliter gesta sunt, non errat, non uritur a luna. Qmnis autem homo quamvis iam crediderit in Christum, aut ibi errat, aut ibi, si non in illo fit quod dictum est, Domínus tegumentum tuum super manum dexterae tuae. Ideo enim cum dixisset, Dominus tegumentum tuum super manum dexterae tuae; quasi quaesisset ille et dixisset, Iam ecce est manus dexterae meae, iam elegi credere in Christum, accepi potestatem Inter filios Dei esse, quid est quod Deus tegumentum meum est adhuc supra, id est, super manum dexterae meae? sequitur, Per diem sol non uret te, ñeque luna per noctem. Ad hoc igitur tegumentum tuum est super manum dexterae tuae, ut non te urat sol per diem, ñeque luna per noctem. Nam bine intelligite, fratres, quia figurate dictum est. Etenim revera, solem visibilem si cogitemus, urit per diem: numquid luna urit per noctem? Who are you? Scandalum. Audi Apostolum dicentem, Quis injirmatur, et ego non infirmar? quis scandalizatur, et ego non uror? (2 Cor 11:29).

13 [v.7}. Then the sun will not burn you during the day, nor the moon during the night. Because? Because the Lord will keep you from all evil. Because we are among temptations; Therefore, the Lord will keep you from all evil. May the Lord preserve your soul, that is, your soul too. Save your entry and your exit from now and forever. Not as your body, because the martyrs perished as to the body; but may the Lord preserve your soul, because the martyrs did not die as regards their soul. The persecutors attacked Santa Crispina, whose feast day we celebrate today; They were cruel to the weak and rich woman, but she was strong, because the Lord, who protected her, was her protector on the hand of her right. By chance, brothers, is there anyone in Africa who does not know who this woman was? She was eminent, of noble lineage, rich; but all these things were the left, they were under the head. The enemy approaches to wound the head, and the left hand, which was under the head, is offered to him. The head was up, the right one narrowed it above. What could the pursuer do even when it was a weak woman? He was weak because of sex, perhaps more lacking in vigor because of riches, and even weaker because of bodily life. But what could the enemy do in the face of so many defenses? What about the Bridegroom, who extended his left hand under her head and embraced her with his right? When, being thus defended, could 13 [v.7]. See diem ergo sol non uret te, ñeque luna per night. Quare? Quia Dominus custodiet te ab omni malo. Will the enemy hurt her? And yet, he wounded her, but in the body. Well, what does the psalm say? The Lord keep your soul. The soul did not die, the body died; but he died temporarily, because at last he will rise again. For also the one who deigned to be Head of the Church temporarily offered his body to death, but resurrected it on the third day. He will resurrect ours at the end of the world. He resurrected the Head in attention to the Body so that it would not faint. The Lord keep your soul. Noceda; do not be broken by stumbling; do not give in by fainting in persecutions, in work, because, as the Lord says, do not fear those who kill the body and cannot kill the soul; rather fear Him who can kill the body and throw the soul into the fires of hell. The Lord keep your soul so that you do not give in to the wicked persecutor, to the lying promiser, to the threater of temporal things: The Lord keep your soul. 14 [v. 8]. Then he says: May the Lord guard your coming and going from now on and forever. Temporarily attend to your entrance: May the Lord guard your entrance and your exit from now and forever. Also save your output. What does "entrance" mean? What "exit"? When we are tempted, we enter; When we overcome temptation, we come out. See the entrance, see the exit: The fiery furnace tests the potter's vessels, and the temptation of tribulation, the righteous men. If righteous men are like the potter's vessels, it is necessary that the potter's vessels enter the oven. However, the potter is not sure when they enter, but rather when they leave. However, the Lord is seanimam tuam Dominus. Anima non cessit, corpus percussum est. Et corpus ad tempus percussum est: nam in fine resurrectum est. Quia et ipse qui dignitatus est esse caput Ecclesiae, praebuit corpus suum ad tempus percutiendum: sed carnem suam ille triduo resuscitavit; carnem nostram in fine resuscitaturus est. Ideo suscitatum est caput, quod attenderet corpus, ut non deficeret. Custodiat animam tuam Dominus.

Instantly gressus, lapsu ad ruinam a Deo, quia intuitus est et inspexit felicitatem peccatorum, et vidit eos habere pacem, se autem laborem. Narravit autem hoc cum iam evasisset, cum iam correct corde Deo inhaesisset, narravit praeterita pericula sua. Ergo, Bonus Deus Israel: sed quibus? Rectis corde. Who was straight? Qui non reprehendunt Deum. Who was straight? Qui voluntatem suam ad voluntatem Dei dirigunt; non voluntatem Dei ad voluntatem suam curvare conantur. Breve praeceptum est, ut homo dirigat cor suum. Vis habere rectum cor? Your fac quod vult Deus; noli Deum velle faceré quod vis tu. Pravicordes ergo sunt, id est, qui rectum cor non habent, qui sedent et disputant quomodo debuit faceré Deus; non laudando quod fecit, sed reprehende.

Corrigere illum volunt: parum est quia corrigi ab eo nolunt; et dicunt, Non debuit Deus faceré pauperes, sed soli divites esse debuerunt; et ipsi soli viverent. Utquid factus est pauper? utquid vivit? Reprehendit Deum pauperum. Quanto melius esset pauper Dei, et dives esset de Deo; hoc est, sequeretur voluntatem Dei, et videret paupertatem suam temporalern esse, et transituram, divitias autem sibi spirituales ita venturas, ut nullo pact possent praeterire; et haberet in divitiis cordis fidem, si ei non contingit aurum habere in arca? Quia si aurum haberet in arca, furern timeret, et aurum de arca etiam nolens loseet; fidem autem de corde non loseet, si ipse illam inde non expelleret. I quote autem I will respond

It can be answered: Dearest, God made the poor to test man, and he made the rich to test him through the poor; and all things that God made, he did well. 3. Who are these? Those who live in Jerusalem. Those who live in Jerusalem will not be moved forever. If we understood Jerusalem to be the earthly city, you will observe that all those who lived there were thrown out by wars and the destruction of the city itself. Now you are looking for the Jew in the city of Jerusalem and you cannot find him. Then how will those who live in Jerusalem not be moved eternally? Because there is another Jerusalem, about which you are used to hearing many things. She is our mother, for her we sigh and groan on this pilgrimage in order to return to her again. We had turned away from it and had no way; The King came from her, and our way was made so that we could return to her. She is the city where our feet stood firm in the courts of Jerusalem, as you heard in a previous psalm of gradual song already expounded and commented on, for which he who sang sighed: Jerusalem, which

it is built as a city; her participation in the Same, that is, in the Permanence. Therefore those who live there will not be moved forever. Those who lived in earthly Jerusalem were moved, first in their hearts, then in exile. When they were moved to the heart and collapsed, they crucified the King of the heavenly Jerusalem itself. Spiritually they were outside and they were throwing out the King himself. They took him out of his city and crucified him outside. He also cast them out of their city, that is, from eternal Jerusalem, the mother of us all, which is in heaven. 4. What is this Jerusalem? He concisely describes it: Mountains around it. Is it something great that we are in that city that the mountains surrounded? Does all our happiness consist in the fact that we will possess the city that the mountains surround? But there are other mountains worth loving; lofty mountains: the preachers of the truth, whether angels, apostles or prophets. These are found around Jerusalem; They surround it and form like a wall. Scripture speaks frequently of these lovely and delightful mountains. Notice, when you hear or read, that you find these delightful mountains in more passages than I can cite. However, as soon as the Lord inspires me, I delight in speaking at length about these mountains, and above all because many divine testimonies from the Holy Scripture came to my memory. They are the mountains that are illuminated by God; and first they are illuminated so that from them

Think, brothers, that some timid souls could have become heretics. Only great men made heretics; but insofar as they were great insofar as they were bad mountains. For they were not such mountains that could receive peace so that the hills could receive justice, but they received discord from their father the devil. I called all of these mountains, but shipwrecked ones. You see that some little light of words emanates from them and some momentary fire ignites from them. If you sail on the log and the night falls on you, that is, the darkness of this life, do not be deceived; do not go to that ship; There are rocks there, there are great shipwrecks. When these mountains are praised to you and you begin to be persuaded to approach these mountains as a place of refuge so that you can rest here, respond: I trust in the Lord. Why do you say to my soul: "Transmigrate to the mountain like a bird"? It is good for you to raise your eyes to the mountains from where help comes to you from the Lord. So that you avoid falling like a bird into the hunters' trap, do not transmigrate to these mountains. The bird is fickle; at all times it moves; instantly flies from one side to the other. Trust in the Lord, and you will be like Mount Zion; You will not be moved forever and you will not transmigrate to the mountains like the bird. Those who desired to be mountains by their own righteousness, like some Jews or their princes the Pharisees, are censured in this way: Not knowing the justice of God and trying to establish their own, they did not submit to the justice of God. In such a way those who submitted are exalted, that at the same time they are humble. Because they are exalted they are called mountains, because they submit to God they are valleys; but since they possess the capacity for piety, they receive the abundance of peace and transmit its overflow to the hills. This power is found in almost all families. There are lords and servants; The names are diverse, but men and men are the same names. What does the Apostle say teaching servants to submit to their masters? Servants, obey your carnal masters; and he says it this way because there is another Lord regarding the

spirit. He is the true and eternal Lord; but these of the flesh are temporary. As for you, walking on the path, living in this life, Christ does not want to make you proud. any misfortune. Why does it say as consoled and not, simply, "consoled"? This word sicut, like, does not always mean similarity. The word sicut sometimes refers to nature or quality, other times to similarity; here it refers to quality. But examples of the common way of speaking must be offered to us so that we can easily understand it. When we say: Sicut vixit pater (as the father lives, so lives the son), we express it denoting similarity. Likewise, sicut pecus moritur (as the animal dies), in the same way man dies, indicates similarity. However, when we say: Fecit sicut vir bonus (he acted as a good man), is he not a good man, but rather the likeness of a good man? Likewise: Fecit tanquam tustús (he did it as just), this tanquam does not deny that it is just, but rather demonstrates the quality or property of the name. You acted sicut (like) a senator. Let this one say: "I am not a senator"; precisely because you are, you acted like a senator; so also, because you are just, you acted as just, and, because you are good, you acted as good. Then as these were truly consoled sicut consolati, as consoled they rejoiced, that is, their joy was great, as if they were consoled, the one who died consoling those who were to die. A man is unclean when he eats and yes when he vomits, for the Lord says: What goes into the mouth is not defiled, but what comes out is not defiled. Next, in the same place, another evangelist declared what are the things that come out of the mouth, so that we would understand that it is not the mouth of the body, but that of the heart, for he writes: From the heart come evil thoughts, fornications, murders, blasphemies; These are the things that defile man; But eating without washing your hands does not defile a man. But, if because he had fallen the things that were said through him had no value, it would be judged that he said them and not that they were said through him. Optime igitur etiam hoc egit mercy Dei et Spiritus eius, ut quidquid boni per Salomonem dictum est, Deo tribueretur; peccatum autem hominis homini. Quid mirum quia in populo Dei cecidit Solomon? to expect Solomon to fall among the people of God. Didn't Adam fall in Paradise? Didn't the angel fall from heaven and become a demon? From here let us learn that we should not put hope in any man. Solomon built the temple to the Lord, figuratively symbolizing the Church and the body of the Lord; That is why the Lord said in the Gospel: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then as he had built the temple, so the true Solomon, the true Pacific, our Lord Jesus Christ, built the temple. Solomon means peaceful. This is that true Peace of which the Apostle says: Our peace is He who made both things one. The true Pacific is the One who united within himself the two walls that met on opposite sides, for which he was made the cornerstone. When the believing people of circumcision and the believing people of the foreskin of the Gentiles, made for them a cornerstone, came to him, he constituted a Church of both peoples, and for this reason it is the true Pacific. He is the true Solomon, since Solomon, son of David, born to the wife Bathsheba, king of Israel, prefigured the Pacific when he built the temple. Therefore, lest you think that Solomon, the son of Bathsheba, built the house of God, the Scripture, making known to you another Solomon, begins to say in the psalm: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it will labor in vain. Then the Lord builds the house, our Lord builds his house. Many work in construction; But if He does not build, those who build it will work in vain. Who are those who work in construction? All those in the Church who preach the word of God, the ministers of the sacraments of God. We all run, factus est? ideo docemur in millo hominum spem esse ponedam. Quia et iste Salomón aedificaverat templum Domino (ib. 6), in typo quidem et in figura fugae Ecclesiae et corporis Domini; unde dictit in Gospel, Solvite templum hoc, et in triduo excitabo illud (lo 2,19): quia ergo ipse aedificaverat illud templum, aedificavit sibi templum verus Solomon Dominus noster Iesus Christus, verus pacificus. Nomen enim Salomonis interpretatur Pacificus: est autem ille verus pacificus, de quo dicit Apostolus, Ipse est enim pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum.

Ipse est verus pacificus, qui duos parietes e diverse venientes in se copulavit, quibus factus est lapis angularis, venienti populo ex circumcisione credentium, et venienti populo ex praeputio Gentium et ipsorum credentium; fecit unam Ecclesiam de duobus populis, factus est illis lapis angularis (Eph 2, 14-22), et ideo veré pacificus. Quia ergo ille verus Solomon; Solomon autem ille filius David de muliere Bethsabee (2 Reg 12:24), rex Israel, figuram gestabat huius pacific, quando templum aedificavit: ideo ne illum putes Salomonem qui aedificavit domum Deo, alium Salomonem tibi ostendens Scriptura sic coepit in Psalm: Nisi Dominus aedificaverit domum, in vanum laboraverunt aedificantes eam. Dominus ergo aedificat domum, Dominus Iesus Christus aedificat domum suam. Laborant multi in aedificando; sed si non ille aedificet, in vanum laboraverunt aedifican-

We all work, we all build now; and also before us others ran, worked, built; But if the Lord does not build the house, the builders will work in vain. Therefore, seeing the apostles fall some, they say, and especially Saint Paul: You observe days, years, months and seasons. I fear for you, lest I have labored for you in vain. As he knew that he had been built up internally by the Lord, he wept for them, lest it should happen that he had worked on them in vain. Then we build externally, He internally. We notice how you hear; What you think is only noticed by those who see your thoughts. He edifies, admonishes, frightens, gives understanding, subjects our assent to faith. However, we also work as workers; But if the Lord does not build the house, the builders will labor in vain. 3. The house of God is the city itself. The house of God is the people of God, since the house of God is the temple of God. What does the Apostle say? The temple of God, which is you, is holy. All the faithful saints, who are the house of God, not only those who now exist, but also those who previously existed and have already died and those who after us will exist, who are yet to be born to be in the midst of human things until the end of the world, gathered in one, are innumerable faithful, but numbered by God, for of them the Apostle says: The Lord knew those who are his. These grains that now groan among the straws and that will form a single heap when the heap is finally forked; all this bunch of faithful saints formed with the men who are to be transmutes eam. Who sunt who laborant aedificantes? Omnes qui in Ecclesia praedicant verbum Dei, ministri Sacramentorum Dei. Omnes currimus, omnes laboramus, omnes aedificamus moda; et ante nos cucurrerunt, laboraverunt, aedificaverunt: sed nisi Dominus aedificaverit domum, in vanum laboraverunt, aedificantes eam. Ideo quosdam videntes ruere Apostoli, et proprie Paulus ait: Dies observatis, et annos, et menses, et tempora; timeo vos, ne forte sine causa laboraverim in vos (Gal 4,10.11). Quia novetat se intus a Domino aedificari, plangebat istos, quia sine causa laboraverat in eis. Nos ergo loquimur foris, Ule aedificat intus. Quomodo auditatis, nos advertimus; quid cogitetis, ille solus novit qui cogitationes vestras videt.

Ipse aedificat, ipse monet, ipse terret, ipse intellectum aperit, ipse ad fidem applicat sensum vestrum: et tamen laboramus et nos tanquam operanii; sed nisi Dominus aedificaverit domum, in vanum laboraverunt aedificantes eam. 3. Quae autem domus Dei, et ipsa civitas. Domus enim Dei, populus Dei; quia domus Dei, templum Dei. Et quid dicit Apostolus? Templum enim Dei sanctum est, quod estis vos (1 Cor 3:17). Omnes autem fideles, quae est domus Dei, non solum qui moda sunt, sed et qui ante nos fuerunt et iam dormierunt, et qui post nos futuri sunt, adhuc qui nascí habent in rebus humanis usque in finem saeculi, congregati in unum fideles innumerabiles, sed Domino numerati, de quibus dicit Apostolus,

ted to become equal to the angels of God, united to the same angels, who now do not pilgrimage, but wait for us to return from the pilgrimage, they all form together one house of God and one city. This is Jerusalem, which has guards, because as it has builders who work to build it, it also has guards. For what the Apostle says belongs to the guard: I fear lest, as the serpent deceived Eve, so your minds become depraved, losing simplicity towards Christ. The Apostle guarded, was a guardian; He watched as much as he could over those in front. The bishops also do this, since they are placed in a higher place to supervise and guard the people, since what is said in Greek episkopous, bishop, is translated into Latin as superintendent, inspector or superintendent, because he inspects, because he contemplates from above. As the winegrower occupies a high position to guard the vineyard, the bishop is in a high position to guard the flock. From this vantage point there must be a risky and detailed account if we do not remain here with our hearts humbled at your feet and praying for you so that he who knows your thoughts will keep them. Well, I can see those who enter and leave the temple, but to such an extent I cannot see what you think in your hearts, that I cannot even see what you do in your houses. So how do we guard? As men, as much as we can, as much as is granted to us. And, since we guard like men and cannot make it perfectNovit Dominus qui sunt eius (2 Tim 2,19); grana illa quae moda gemunt Inter paleas, quae massam unam invoice sunt, quando area in fine fuerit ventilata (Mt 3:12): omnis ergo numeras fidelium sanctorum, ex hominibus commutandorum ut fiant aequales Angelis Dei, adiuncti etiam ipsi Angelis, qui moda non peregrinantur, sed exspectant nos quando a peregrinatione redeamus; omnes simul unam domum Dei faciunt, et unam civitatem. Ipsa est Jerusalem. Habet custodes: quomodo habet aedificantes, laborantes ut aedificetur; sic habet et custodians. Nam ad custodiam pertinet quod dicit Apostolus: Timaeus ne sicut serpens Evam seduxit astutia sua, sic et vestrae minds corruptantur a castitate quae est in Christo (2 Cor 11,3). Custodiebat, custos erat; vigilabat, quantum poterat, supet eos quibus praeerat. Et episcopi hoc faciunt.

Nam ideo altior locus positus est episcopis, ut ipsi superintendant, et tanquam custodiant populum. Nam et graece quod dicitur episcopus, hoc latine superintentor interpretatur; quia superintendit, quia desuper videt. Quomodo enim vinitori altior fit locus ad custodiendam vineam, sic et episcopis altior locus factus est. Et de isto alto loco periculosa redditur ratío, nisi eo corde stemus hic, ut humilitate sub pedibus vestris simus, et pro vobis oremus, ut qui novit mentes vestras ipse custodiat. Quia nos intrantes vos et exeuntes possumus videre; usque adeo autem non videmus quid cogitetis in cordibus vestris, ut ñeque quid agatis in domibus vestris videre possimus. Quomodo ergo custodimus? We work guarding, but our work will be useless if the one who sees our thoughts does not guard. He guards when you watch, He guards when you sleep, for He once slept on the cross, and He sleeps no more. Be Israel, for he who guards Israel neither sleeps nor slumbers. Come, brothers: if we want to be kept under the shadow or protection of the wings of God, let us be Israel. I guard you because of the government's office, but I want to be guarded with you. I am a shepherd to you, but I am a sheep with you under that Shepherd. From this place I am like a doctor to you, but I am your fellow student in this school under that one Master. 4 [v.2]. If we want to be guarded by Him who humbled Himself for us and who exalted Himself to keep us, let us be humble. Nobody assumes anything. No one has anything good unless he has received it from Him who alone is good. He who wants to claim wisdom is foolish. Be humble so that wisdom comes upon you and enlightens you. If before wisdom comes upon him he thinks he is wise, he rises before dawn and walks in darkness. What do you hear in this psalm? It is useless for you to get up before the light. If you arise before the light appears, you will necessarily remain in vanity, because you will be in darkness. Our light has risen, Christ. It is better for you to arise after Christ, not before Christ. Who rise before Christ? Those who try to overcome Christ. And who are these? Those who quia nos sicut nomines custodimus, et perfecte custodire non possumus, ideo sine custode remanebitis? absit. Nam ubi est Ule de quo dicitur, Nisi Dominus custodierit civitatem, in vanum laboravit qui custodit eam? Laboramus in custodiendo, sed vanus est labor noster, nisi ille custodiat qui videt cogitationes vestras. Custodit ille cum vigilatis, custodit et cum dormieritis. Ule enim dormivit in crossing semel, et surrexit; iam not asleep. Estote Israel; quia non dormit, ñeque dormitabit, qui custodit Israel (Ps 120,4). Eia, fratres, si volumus sub umbra alarum Dei custodiri, simus Israel. Custodimus enim vos ex officio dispensationis; sed custodiri volumus vobiscum. Tanquam vobis pastores sumus, sed sub illo Pastore vobiscum oves sumus.

Si volumus custodiri ab illo qui humiliatus est propter nos, et exaltatus est ad custodiendos nos, humiles simus. Nemo sibi arroget aliquid. They want to exalt themselves here where Christ humbled himself. Then humble yourselves here if you want to exalt yourself there where Christ exalted himself. For of those who adhered to Him by faith, among whom we are if we also believe in Him with a right heart, He says: Father, I want those whom you gave me to be with me where I am. Great gift, immense grace, excellent promise, my brothers! Who doesn't want to be with Christ where He is? Christ is already in the exalted. Do you want to be there where He is? Be humble where He was. Therefore, the same light tells them: The disciple is not more than the Master, nor the servant more than the Lord. The disciples who longed to be more than the Master and the servants who wanted to be more than their Lord wanted to rise above the light; They walked in vain, since they did not walk after the light. This psalm says to these; It is useless for you to get up before the light. Such were the sons of Zebedee, who, before being humiliated according to the passion of the Lord, chose places to sit in: one on the right and the other on the left. They wanted to get up before the light; That's why they walked in vain. The Lord, upon hearing this, directed them to humility, saying to them: "Can you drink the cup that I must drink? I came to humble myself, and you want to be exalted before me? Where I go, follow me; because, if you want to go a different way than I go, it is useless for you to rise before the light." Peter also rose before the light when he tried to give advice to the Lord not to suffer from noseritis. Surrexit lux nostra Christus; bonum est tibi ut surgas post Christum, non surgas ante Christum. What arose before Christum? Qui se volunt praeponere Christo. And who is who volunt praeponere Christo? Qui volunt hic excelsi esse, ubi humilis ille Fuit. Sint ergo hic humiles, si volunt ibi esse excelsi, ubi Christus excelsus est. Ait enim de iis qui illi adhaeserant fide, in quibus et nos sumus, si et nos in illum pure corde credimus: Pater, inquit, quos mihi dedisti, voló ut ubi ego sum, et ipsi sint mecum (lo 17,24). Magnum donum, magna gratia, magna promissio, fratres mei! Et quis non vult esse cum Christo, ubi est Christus? Be iam excelsus Christus: vis ibi esse ubi est excelsus? This humilis, ubi et ille humilis Fuit. Propterea illis dicit ipsa lux: Non est discipulus super magistrum, nec servus super dominum suum (Mt 10,24).

Qui volebant discipuli esse super magistrum; et servi volebant esse super dominum suum, ante luzem volebant arisere; in vanum ibat, quia non post luzem ibat. lilis ergo dicit iste psalmus, In vanum est vobis ante luzem surgere. Such weret filii Zebedaei, qui antequam humiliarentur secundum passionem Domini, iam sibi loca choosebant, ubi sederent, unus ad dexteram, alter ad sinistram: ante luzem volebant surgere; ideo in vanum ibat. Revocavit illos Dominus ad humilitatem, cum hoc audiret, et ait illis: Potestis bibere calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? (ib. 20,21.22). Ego veni humilis esse, et vos ante me vultis esse excelsi? others. The Lord spoke of his passion, of his humiliation, by which we were to be saved, since he suffered humbly. Having thus announced his future passion, Peter, who had shortly before confessed him as the Son of God, was filled with fear; He feared that he would die, and said to him: Far be it from you, Lord; God will be kind to you, this will not happen. He intended to get up before the light and give advice to the light. But what did the Lord do? He made him rise after the light: "Stand behind me, satan," he told him. "You are satan, because you want to rise before the light. Stand behind me so that I precede you and you follow me. Where I go you must go, but you must not want to take me where you want to go." 5. The psalm says to those who wanted to rise before the light: It is useless for you to rise before the light. When will we get up? After we have humiliated ourselves. Get up after you've sat down. The resurrection means exaltation; the session, humility. In some places, a session is understood as the honor of judging, and in others, humility. How is the session the honor of judging? You will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel. What does humility mean? At the sixth hour, the Lord being tired, sat down by the well. The Lord's fatigue symbolized his weakness; the weakness of power, the weakness of wisdom; but this weakness is humility. Then if he sat down out of weakness, the sitting symbolizes humility. But his session, that is, his humility, saved us, because the weakness of God is stronger if he does vultis iré, qua ego non eo, In vanum est vobis ante luzem surgere. Et Petrus ante lucem surrexerat, quando consilium Domino will give volebat, ut non pateretur pro nobis. Dixerat enim ille de passione sua, in qua salvi futuri eramus, de ipsa humilitate; humilis enim passus est: cum ergo de passione sua future diceret, expavit Petrus, qui illum paulo ante dixerat Filium Dei; timuit ne moreretur, et ait illi, Absit a te, Domine; propitius this lukewarm; non fie' istud. Ante Lucem volebat surgere, et luci consilium daré. Sed quid fecit Dominus? Fecit illum ut post luzem surgeret: Redi post me, satan (ib. 16,21-23). Ideo enim satanás, quia ante luzem vis emergere, Redi post me, ut ego praecedam, tu sequaris: qua ego eo, illac eas; non qua tu vis iré, illac me velis ducere. 5. Ergo illis qui volebant ante luzem surgere dicit Psalmus, In vanum est vobis ante luzem surgere. And when does it arise?

Cum fuerimus humiliati: Surgete posteaquam sedistis. Surrectio exaltationem significat, session humilitatem significat. Aliis locis intelligitur session in honore iudicandi, aliis locis humilitatem otendit. Quomodo in honore iudicandi session? Sedebitis super duodecim sedes, indicative duodecim tribes Israel (Mt 19:28). How do I sign humilitatis session? Sixth hour Dominus fatiguetus sedit ad puteum (lo 4,6). Fatigatio Domini, infirmitas Domini Fuit, infirmitas virtutis, infirmitas sapientiae: sed ipsa infirmitas, humilitas. Ergo si sedi ex infirmatate, session illa humilitatem significat. than men. That is why it says in a psalm: Lord, you knew my session and my resurrection, that is, my humility and my exaltation. Why do you want, children of Zebedee, to exalt yourselves before the light? We speak like this and preferably name these because they will not be angry with us, since this was written about them so that others would avoid the pride, into which they fell. Why do you want to get up before the light? It is useless to you. Do you want to get up before you humiliate yourself? Your Lord himself, who is your light, humbled himself to be exalted. Hear Saint Paul, who says: He who subsisted in the form of God did not consider it a shame to be equal with God. Why wasn't it a robbery for Him? Because he was so by nature, because he was born like this being equal to Him by whom he was begotten. But what did he do? He emptied himself for us, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of man and found in a man's habit. He humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross. This is your session. But hear the resurrection: Therefore God exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name. You are already running towards this name; get up But after you have sat down, do you want to get up? Sit down first; and thus, rising from humility, you will reach the kingdom. Because, if you rush into taking the kingdom, you will fall from the kingdom before you rise. Can you drink, said the Lord, the cup that I am to drink? They answered: We can. He replies to them: You will drink my cup; but to sit on my right and on my left, it is not mine to give it to you; for others it was prepared by my Father. What does it mean it doesn't belong to me to give it to you? It is not said in quodam psalmo: Domine, tu cognovisti sessionem meam, et resurrectionem meam (Ps 138,2); id est humilitatem meam, et exaltionem meam. Quid ergo vos ante luzem vultis exaltari, o filii Zebedaei? Sic enim loquamm', et ipsos potius nominemus, qui non nobis irascuntur; quia ideo de illis ista conscripta sunt, ut alii caverent superbiam in qua ipsi correpti sunt. Quid ergo vultis ante luzem surgere? In vanum est vobis. Exaltari vultis, antequam, humiliemini? Dominus ipse vester, qui est lux vestra, humiliatus est ut exaltaretur. Audite Paulum dicentem: Qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo. Quare illi non erat rapine? Quia natura erat, quia hoc natus erat, ut esset aequalis illi a quo genitus est. Sed quid fecit?

Propter nos semetipsum exinanivit, formam servi accipiens, in similarityine hominum factus, et habitu inventus ut homo. Humiliavit semetipsum factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Haec est sessio ipsius. Sed audi resurrectionem: Propter quod et Deus illum exaltavit, et donavit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen (Phil 2,6-9). Iam vos ad illud nomen festinatis; arise, sed posteaquam sedistis. Surgere vultis, sed primo sedete: et arises ab humilitate, pervenis ad regnum. Nam si praeripis regnum, cadis a regno antequam surgas. Potestis bibere, inquit, calicem quem ego bibiturus sum? Et illi: Possumus. Et ille: Calicem, inquit, meum bibetis; Sedere autem ad dexteram, vel ad sinistram meam,

Then let us also hear this, since the psalm says: Take yourselves up after you have sat down. 6. So that no one thinks that he feels to be honored, he declares that for the session he wanted to recommend humility; so that no one would believe that he was commanded to sit down either to judge, or to eat, or to rejoice, and hence try to become more arrogant, he adds, declaring and emphasizing the type of humility: Those who eat the bread of sorrow. Those who groan in this pilgrimage feed on the bread of pain, since they are in the valley of tears. But God commands the rises in the heart. Where do you order them? In his heart—he says—he ordered the rises. Who? God. If he ordered the rises in the heart, this is why they sing the song of degree. Let us humble ourselves in the century and rise. As? With the heart, for the rise of the heart arises from the valley of tears: In the valley of tears, says the psalm. As the mountains were erected, so were the valleys settled. Depressions in the earth are called "valleys"; hills, portions of land somewhat higher, but less than those of mountains, since the highest places on earth are called mountains. It is a small thing that is commanded, for it is not said: "Get up from the hill," nor "from the field or plain," but from the valley, so that from this

way be something more humble and lower than the field or plain. Then if in the valley of tears you eat the bread of sorrow and say: My tears were my bread day and night while I am told every day: "Where is your God?", you get up well, because you had sat down. 7. And as if you were asking when we will rise, since we are now ordered to sit down, you are answered: "Our resurrection will take place when the Lord's." Pay attention to the one who preceded you, because if you do not pay attention to Him, it is useless for you to rise before the light. When was He exalted? After death. Then wait for your exaltation after death; wait for it at the resurrection of the dead, because He rose from the dead and ascended to heaven. But where did he sleep? On the cross. When he slept on the cross he symbolized, what am I saying?, he fulfilled what was executed in Adam; Well, while he was asleep, a rib was torn out of him, and Eve was made of it; Likewise, when the Lord's side was wounded with the spear while he was sleeping on the cross, the sacraments gushed forth and the Church was born. The Church, wife of the Lord, was made from the side, like Eve. As this one was made from the side of the one who slept, so was that one from the side of the dead man. Therefore if He was not resurrected except after He had died, expect exaltation after this life. Teaching this psalm to you, who seems to ask him: "When will I get up? Maybe before I sit down?", he tells you: When he gives sleep to his loved ones. God will give this after his loved ones sleep. Then his loved ones will arise, that is, those of Christ. Omnes enim surgent, sed non quomodo dilecti eius. Omnium est resurrectio mortuorum; sed quid ait Apostolus? Omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur (1 Cor 15:51). Si autem membra eius sumus, tune sumus dilecti eius, tune ad nos pertinet illa resurrectio quae praecessit in Domino, ut lux surrexerit ante nos, nos post luzem: quia in vanum est nobis ante luzem surgere, id est, altitudinem quaerere antequam moriamur; cum Christus lux nostra non sit exaltatus in carne, nisi posteaquam mortuus est. Constituti ergo membra eius, et in membris eius dilecti eius, cum somnum acceperimus, tune surgemus in resurrectionem mortuorum. Unus resurrectexit, iam non moriturus. He dusted himself off. What do you say about the dress? She brushed off her dress. If what came out by shaking and that from which came what had adhered is called shaken, the dust was shaken, and so were the apostles. Then why should the children of the apostles not be called children of the shaken? 11. But there is another opinion that I must not ignore. Perhaps this was recorded obscurely so that it would give rise to many meanings, and thus, by discovering what was hidden in many ways, men would be enriched in this way more than if it were made evident in only one way. We also say that something is shaken so that what is hidden comes out. In one way we say that he shakes his dress, so that the dust comes out of it, and in another way that he shakes his jacket, so that what was hidden inside it comes out. Therefore, I understand as much as I can, brothers, that perhaps the apostles themselves were called children of the shaken; that is, children of the prophets, since the prophets contained hermetic and hidden sacraments, but they were shaken so that they appeared clearly. Believe then that the prophet said, as he certainly did, that the ox knew its owner, and the donkey its master's manger, but Israel did not know me. Now at the moment this occurred to me that could

say of the prophet; If something else had occurred to me, I would have said it. Well, if upon hearing this the man thinks of the donkey, the ox, the animals and the donkeys that he sees, since he perceives externally what is internally enclosed as in a wrapper, he will nevertheless not know what is there. The prophet covered it up with I don't know what disguises of names. Which donkey and ox are you referring to? The donkey, symbolizing the people of God, is the donkey of God, who carries the Lord as a knight so that he does not go astray, and the ox is the one about which the Apostle says: You shall not muzzle the ox that threshes. Does God take care of the oxen? And he added: This is what the Scripture says for us. Everyone who preaches the word of God, admonishes, rebukes, frightens, threshes the harvest and fulfills the office of an ox. The ox came from the Jews; the preaching apostles came from there; the donkey, from the part of the foreskin, that is, from the Gentiles; He approached to carry the Lord, and so the Lord rode on the donkey, which had never been carried on anyone's shoulders, since neither the law nor the prophets had been sent to the Gentiles. Then, since our Lord Jesus Christ wanted to be our food, and, for the same reason, at birth he was placed in the manger, the ox knew its owner, and the donkey its master's manger. Would these things have come to light if the sack had not been shaken? If the hidden prophecy had not been diligently shaken, would it perchance appear clear to us? 13. He will not be ashamed when he speaks to his enemies at the door. Brothers, let's talk at the door, that is, let everyone know what we're talking about. Those who do not want to speak at the door try to hide what they speak; and maybe he wants to hide it because it is a bad thing. If you trust, speak at the gate, as it is said of wisdom: Speak boldly at the gates of the city. As long as the innocent retain justice, they will not be ashamed; and this is precisely preaching at the door. And who preaches at the door? He who preaches in Christ, because Christ is the door through which we enter the city. I would be lying if He had not said: I am the door. If it is a door, it is an entrance. He is called the door of the house; The gate of the city is the entrance, the gate of the house is the entrance. But perhaps it is not rightly called an entrance if what is called a house is not rightly called a city. Shortly before, both things were said: If the Lord does not build the house, the builders will work in vain; And so that you would not think that, upon hearing the word house, it was a trivial thing, he added: Unless the Lord keeps the city, he who keeps it watched in vain. Therefore the house is the city. It has a door, like a house, and an entrance, like a city. He who is the door of the house is the entrance to the city. Therefore if Christ is the entrance to the city, he who establishes himself in Christ is not ashamed, and thus he preaches. But whoever preaches against Christ closes the entrance. Who are those who preach against Christ? Those who deny that arrows were shot from the hand of the Mighty One and reached to the ends of the earth, and that this is the inheritance of the Lord, of which it was said: Ask of me,

Id est, divine desires; non potes implere ex eis desiderium tuum: desideras honores in terra, desideras ea quae etiam iumentis donavit Deus, hoc est voluptatem temporalem, et salutem corporis, et talia; non ex eis implebis desiderium tuum. 13. Non confundetur, cum loquetur inimicis suis in porta. Fratres, in porta loquamur, id est, omnes noverint quid loquamur. Qui enim non vult loqui in porta, latere vult quod loquitur; et forte ideo vult latere, quia malum est. Si fidit, in porta loquatur; sicut dicitur of Sapientia: In portis autem civitatum audenter dicit (Prov 8,3). Quanto tempore iustitiam innocentes tenuerint, non erubescent: hoc est in porta praedicare. Et quis est qui praedicat in porta? Qui praedicat in Christo; quia Christus is portal qua intramus ad illam civitatem. Mentior, si non ipse dixit, Ego sum ianua (lo 10,9). Si ianua est, et porta est. Ianua enim dicitur domus; ianua civitatis porta est, porta domus ianua est. Sed forte non bene dicitur porta, si non bene dicitur civitas quae dicta est domus. Utrumque enim paulo ante dictum est: Nisi Dominus aedificaverit domum, in vanum laboraverunt aedificantes eam; et ne istam domum audiendo parvum aliquid putares, Nisi Dominus, inquit, custodierit civitatem, in vanum laboravit qui custodit eam. Illa est ergo domus quae est civitas. Ipsa ergo habet ianuam tanquam domus, et habet portam tanquam civitas. Qui est ergo ianua domus, ipse est porta civitatis. Ergo si Christus porta civitatis, ille non erubescit qui in Christo stat, et sic praedicat. Qui autem contra Christum praedicat, clauditur contra illum porta. Qui sunt illi qui contra Christum praedicant? Qui negant quia missae sunt sagittae de manu potentis, et pervenerunt usque in fines

Our husband is absent; Ask your conscience: "Do you want him to come or to delay his coming?" See, brothers, I knocked at the door of your hearts, but He heard the voice of the inhabitants. I, since I am a man, cannot perceive what each one's conscience has said now; but he who is absent with the body, but present with the virtue of majesty, has heard you. How many, if it were said to them: "Behold, Christ is coming; tomorrow will be the day of judgment," would not exclaim: "I hope he comes"! Those who say it love a lot; and if it is said to them: "It will be late," they fear its delay, because they possess chaste love. As now they fear that he will be late, so when he comes they will fear that he will turn away. This fear will be chaste, because it is safe and peaceful. He will not abandon us when he had come, since he looked for us before we looked for him. Therefore chaste fear, my brothers, carries with it the origin of love. However, unchaste fear fears presence and punishment; everything good he does, he does out of fear; but not for the fear of losing the good, but for the fear of suffering the evil; He is not afraid because he will lose the embrace of his sweet husband, but because he will be sent to the fire. Nevertheless, this fear is useful, but it will not remain forever and ever, for it is not yet the chaste fear that remains forever and ever. 9. In whom is chaste fear found? carnal? To the Jews, who were outside. The synagogue is also outside. Because Mary is next to her house; and his relatives, coming from the consanguinity of the Virgin Mary, who believed in Him, were at the side of his house; not insofar as they were united to Him by blood of the flesh, but insofar as they heard and executed the word of God. Well the Lord replied and said this: Who is my mother and who are my brothers? For this reason, some dared to say that Christ had no mother, since he said: Who is my mother? And why? So Saint Peter, Saint John, James and the other Apostles did not have fathers on earth? Well, what did he also tell them? Do not call anyone on earth your father, for there is only one Father who is in heaven. What he taught the disciples regarding the father, this he declared in relation to the mother. The Lord wants us to put God before earthly blood relations; Honor the father, because he is a father, but put God first, because he is God. The father begot you by giving you his flesh, God created you by manifesting his power. Let the father not be angry when God is put before him; On the contrary, he should rejoice, all the more because He who must be put before Him has been found. Then what will I say? What does the Lord say? Who is my mother and who are my brothers? And stretching out his hand over the disciples, he said, Behold my mother and my brothers. They were certainly brothers; but how were they mother? For, continuing, he said: He who does the will of my Father is my brother, and my sister, and my mother. Have him as a brother when

to the virile sex that the Church contains; for sister, for the women that Christ counts in his members; and for mother, in what way? Because Christ himself is found in Christians, whom the Church engenders every day through baptism. Then in the same ones you understand that she is a wife, she is a mother and she is a son. 13- Tell what children should be like. As? Peaceful. Why peaceful? For blessed are the peaceful, for they will be called children of God. The fruit of peace is enclosed in the olive. The oil symbolizes peace, because it symbolizes charity, and without charity there is no peace. It is evident that those who broke the peace had no charity. Hence, I have already explained to your charity why the dove brought the olive branch with fruit to the ark: to signify that those who were baptized outside, as those branches were baptized outside the ark, if they did not have only leaves, that is, only words, but also fruit, which is charity, the same dove takes them to the ark and they come together in unity. Such should be the children around the Lord's table, like olive buds. This is a perfect reality, a great happiness. Who doesn't long to be there? When you see a blasphemer who has a wife, children, grandchildren, if perhaps you do not have them, do not envy, because this is fulfilled in you, but spiritually. Don't you belong to the members? If you are not in them, cry, because you will not have them here nor there. If you are in the members, be sure, because, if you have them there and not here, it will be more fruitful to have them there in the members than here in the flesh.

quem habet Ecclesia; soror, propter feminas quas hic in membris habet Christus: mater quomodo, nisi quia ipse Christus est in Christianis, quos Christianos per Baptismum quotidie parit Ecclesia? Ergo in quibus intelligis coniugem, in illis matrem, in illis filios. 13. Dicatur ergo quales debent esse filii. Which ones? Pacifici. Quare pacific? Quia, Beati pacifici, quia ipsi filii Dei vocabuntur (ib. 5,9). Quia ergo in oliva fructus est pacis: oleum enim pacem significat, qua charitatem significat; sine charitate mile pax est: et manifestum est quia qui diviserunt pacem, non habebant charitatem. Unde iam exposui Charitati vestrae quare columba folia cum fructu portavit ad arcam (Gen 8,11); ut significaret quia et illi qui foris baptizati sunt, sicut ligna illa extra arcam baptizata sunt, si non sola folia habuerint, id est verba sola, sed habuerint et fructum, quod est charitas, ipsa columba illos reportat ad arcam, et veniunt ad unitatem. Such ergo filii debent esse in circuitu mensae Domini, velut novellatio olivarum. Perfecta res est, magna beatitudo: iam quis ibi nolit esse? Cum videris aliquem blasphemum habere uxorem, filios, nepotes, et te forte non habere, noli zelare; vide quia et in te completum est, sed spiritualiter. An forte is not in membris? Si non ibi es, plange quia nec hic, nec ibi. Si autem ibi, securus this; quia etsi ibi et non hic, fructuosius ibi quam hic.

I have often warned your charity tates suas: tantummodo accessat plena corde, et desinat iam faceré quae antea faciebat, et non dicat, Illa iniquitas non mihi dimittitur. Si enim hoc dixerit, propter ipsam quam putat sibi non dimitti, non se convertit, et fazando caetera, non illi dimittitur et illud quod non timebat. Quia feci, inquit, scelus magnum, et non mihi potest dimitti; iam faciam et caetera: hoc enim perdo quod non fació. Noli timere: in profound it is, noli contemnere de profundis clamare ad Dominum, et dicere, Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine; Domine, quis sustinebit? Observa illum, et exspecta illum, et sustine propter íegem ipsius. Quam legem tibí dedit? Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris. Spera te resurrecturum, et tune futurum omni moda sine peccato, quoniam ille resurrexit qui primus Fuit sine peccato. A harsh morning vigil. Noli dicere: Ego non sum dignus propter peccata. that the voice was not to be taken as if it were that of a single man who sings, but that of all those who are in the Body of Christ. And since in His Body there are all men, that is why He speaks as one man, since the same one is also many. They are many in themselves, but they are one in Him who is unique. He is also the temple of God, of which the Apostle says: The temple of God that you are is holy, that is, all those who believe in Christ, and so believe that they love, are the temple of God. To believe in Christ is to love Christ. But not as the demons believed, who did not love; and, for the same reason, although they believed, they said, What do we have with you, Son of God? We, on the contrary, believe, so that, believing in Him, we love Him; and not say: What have we to do with you?, but rather: "We belong to you, for you redeemed us." All those who believe thus are like living stones, with which the temple of God is built, and like incorruptible wood, with which the ark was made, which could not be submerged in the flood. This, then, is the temple, that is, men themselves are the temple where God is supplicated and heard. Everyone who prays to God outside of his temple is not heard with regard to the peace of eternal Jerusalem, although he is heard with regard to certain temporal goods, which God also granted to the pagans, since the same demons were also heard to enter the swine. Being heard regarding eternal life is a different thing, and is only granted to him who prays in the temple of God. He who prays in the peace of the Church prays in the temple of God.

The Lord expelled from the temple, under a certain symbolism, the men who sought their interests, that is, those who went to the temple to sell and buy. Therefore, if that temple was a symbolism, it is evident that also the Body of Christ, which is the true temple, of which it was the image, has mixed sellers and buyers, that is, men who seek their interests, but not those of Jesus Christ. But they will be thrown from there with the rope woven into the shape of a whip. The rope or rope symbolizes sin; Thus it is said by the prophet: Woe to those who drag sins like a long rope! Those who add sins to sins drag sins like a long rope; who, when committing one sin, commit another to cover it up. Just as to make a rope, esparto is added to esparto, but not by joining one fiber to another, but by twisting them, so all vicious acts, by adding sins to them and emanating one sin from another, linking sins to sins, form a long string. Their ways are vicious, and their steps are tortuous. What is this rope for? So that with it his feet and hands are tied and he is thrown into the outer darkness. You will remember that it was said of a certain sinner in the Gospel: Bind his feet and hands and throw him into the outer darkness; There will be crying and gnashing of teeth. The voice of this temple is heard in the psalm. In this temple, not in the material, one prays, as I said, to God and hears in spirit and in truth. That one was a shadow or figure of this one, in which the one who was to come was made known; That's why that one was already destroyed. Then did the house of our prayer collapse? Not by the way. The temple that was destroyed could not be called a house of prayer, of which it was said: My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations. So you heard what our Lord Jesus Christ said: It is written: "My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations; you have made it a den of thieves." Did those who tried to make the house of God a den of thieves manage to destroy the temple? Likewise, those who live badly within the Catholic Church, as far as it depends on them, try to make the house of God a den of thieves; but that does not mean they destroy the temple. The time will come when they will be cast out by the rope of their sins. However, this temple of God, this Body of Christ, this congregation of faithful, has one voice and as one man sings in the psalm. We have already heard his voice in many other psalms; Let's hear it in this one. If we want, it is our voice; If we want, we hear with the ear that

sing and we sing with our hearts. If we do not want to (sing or hear), we will be in the temple as buyers and sellers, that is, seeking our interest, since we enter the church, but not to execute what pleases the eyes of God. Then let each one see, as he can, how he hears: if he hears and mocks; if he hears and throws it behind his back; if he hears and agrees, that is, if he perceives his voice here and unites the voice of his heart to the voice of this psalm. However, the voice of this psalm is not silent; Learn those who can. What do I say? Those who want; Those who do not want to, do not prevent it. 5. Lord, my heart has not been proud, nor have my eyes been haughty, nor have I walked in greatness, nor in things more admirable, than I. Let this be said more clearly and heard. I was not arrogant, I did not want to show myself to men in wonderful things, nor did I seek something about my strength to boast before the unlearned. Take care of your charity. A great thing is recommended. Simon Magus wanted to walk in greatness greater than himself; That is why the power of the apostles pleased him more than the justice of the Christians. He saw that the Holy Spirit was given to the faithful by the laying on of the hands of the apostles and by their prayers; and it is noteworthy that then the reception of the Holy Spirit was made known by miracles, speaking languages that had not been learned.
