Then in our members you see, my brothers, how each one of them has his own office: the eye sees and does not hear; the ear hears and does not see; The hand works and does not hear or see; The foot walks and does not hear, nor see, nor do what the hand does. But in the same body, if it is healthy and the members do not dispute among themselves, the ear sees through the eye, the eye hears through the ear, and the ear cannot be reproached for not seeing, so that it is said: "You are of no use, you are a scouring pad; can you perhaps see and distinguish colors, as the eye does?" For the ear will respond by the peace of the body, and will say: "I am where the eye is, in the same body I am; I do not see for myself, but I see for him with whom I am." Thus, when the ear says: "The eye sees for me," the eye also says: "The ear hears for me"; The eyes and ears say: "The hands work for us"; and the hands say: "The eyes and ears see and hear for us"; The eyes, ears and hands say: "The feet walk for us." In short, when all the members act in the same body and are in agreement, they all rejoice and congratulate each other. And, if any member suffers any discomfort, the others do not abandon him, they all suffer with him. Perhaps, because the foot is in the body distant from the eyes, since these are placed at the highest and those at the lowest, when the foot is stuck by a thorn, the eyes leave it, and rather, as we experience it, the whole body trembles or contracts, and the man sits down, hunches over, to look for the thorn that stuck in the foot? All members do everything they can to ensure that the

and weak place the thorn that was stuck be removed. Therefore, brothers, he who cannot raise the dead in the Body of Christ, let him not try; Just try not to disagree in the Body so that what happens to your ear does not happen, which, if you wanted to see, would be discordant, since what you did not receive you cannot do. Perhaps he is blamed and told: "If you were just, you would raise a dead man, as Peter raised him." In the life of Christ it seems that the apostles did greater things than the Lord himself. But how can it happen that the branches have more power than the root? How is it that they appear to have done greater things than Him? At the voice of the Lord the dead are resurrected and before the passing shadow of Peter a dead person is resurrected. This fact seems greater than that. But Christ could work without Peter, but Peter without Christ would not have done anything. Because without me—says the Lord—you can do nothing. Then, when the man who takes advantage hears this, as if a slander was thrown in his face by the ignorant pagans, by men who do not know what they are talking about, while he is in the connection of the Body of Christ, he responds and says: "You who say: 'You are not righteous, because you do not perform miracles', you could also say in the ear: 'You are not in the body, because you do not see.'" But he insists and says: "You would do it, as Peter did"; Well, Peter did it for me, because I am in the same Body in which Peter did it; and in him from whom I am not separated, what he can, I can do. For what I can do less, he pities me, and for what he can do more, I rejoice with him. The Lord Himself cried from above for His Body, saying: Saul, Saul, why do you allow me?

Then, brothers, if each one does exactly what he can and does not envy that another can do more, but congratulates himself as established in the same Body, then this voice of the psalm belongs to him: Lord, my heart has not been lifted up, nor have my eyes been haughty, nor have I walked in greatness, nor in things more admirable than I. 12. Those who dealt with these things before me had another opinion, and gave these words of the psalm another meaning, which I will not hide from your charity. But there are certain men who, upon hearing that they should be humble, abandon themselves and do not want to learn anything, thinking that if they learn something, they will be arrogant, and they remain mere babies. The Scripture rebukes these, saying: You have needed milk again, not solid food. God wants to feed us with milk; but in such a way that we do not remain in it, but, growing through it, we arrive at solid food. Therefore, man should not channel his heart toward pride, but rather elevate it toward the teaching of the word of God. If the soul should not be elevated, it would not be said in another passage of the psalm: To you, Lord, I elevated my soul. Let us investigate what Ephrathah means, where I heard it was, and what it means in the jungle fields, where I found it. Ephrathah is a Hebrew word that is translated into Latin by speculum, mirror, as it was bequeathed by those who declared in other languages ​​the meaning of the Hebrew words recorded in Scripture so that their knowledge could reach us. First, the Scripture was translated from the Hebrew language to the Greek language, and for us from this to the Latin language. There were those who studied the Scripture. Then if Ephrath means mirror, that house that was found in the fields of the jungle was heard to be in the mirror. The mirror forms the image in itself, and all prophecy is an image of future things. Then the future house of God was announced in the image of prophecy. We heard that she was in the mirror, that is, we heard that she was in Ephrathah. Here the word saltus is not recorded in a vulgar sense, as when the people say, for example: "Ule saltus, that platoon, that troop or forest of people, consists of so many centuries." The word saltus properly means a place that is still uncultivated and wild. This is why some codices wrote in campis silvae, in the fields of the jungle. Who were the wild fields? Sometimes, as I must not overlook it, you will find a poor person who is arrogant and a rich person who is humble. We frequently encounter these. You hear a poor man groaning under the rule of the rich; When the rich oppresses him powerfully, you usually see him humble. Other times he is not even humble on this occasion, but rather arrogant. From this you understand who I would be if I had something. Therefore the poor of God is poor in the soul, not in the purse. It happens from time to time that a man has a full house, fertile lands, many possessions, much gold and silver, but he knows that he should not boast of all this, and, therefore, he humbles himself before God, and does good with these goods; His heart is so lifted up towards God that he knows that not only are these riches of no use to him, but they also hinder his feet if the Lord does not govern him and help him. Well, this one is counted among the poor who are satisfied with bread. On the contrary, you find a poor beggar who is conceited or not conceited, because he has nothing, but who is looking for a way to become conceited; God does not pay attention to assets, but to covetousness, and judges him according to the desire for which he longed for what is temporal, not according to the goods that he did not achieve. Everyone who is born is born from Adam; condemned of condemned, and, living evil, adds sins to Adam. What good then did Adam deserve? Yet the Merciful loved; Did the Bridegroom love, not the beautiful one, but Quomodo, fratres mei, intelligimus, quam oram dicat, quo potuit descendé unguentum? Non puto quod oram vestimenti in lateribus voluit intelligi. Sunt enim orae in lateribus. Sed a barba I will descend unguentum ad oram potuit, quae in capite est, ubi aperitur capitium. Such sunt qui habitant in unum: ut quomodo per oras istas intrat caput hominis, ut vestiat se; sic per concordiam fraternam Christus intrat, qui est caput nostrum, ut vestiatur, ut Ecclesia illi haereat. 10 [v.3]. Quid aliud dicit? Sicut ros Hermon, who descended super mountains Zion. Hoc voluit intelligi, fratres mei, gratiam Dei esse quod fratres inhabitant in unum; non ex suis viribus, non ex suis meritis, sed ex illius dono, sed ex illius gratia, sicut ros de cáelo.

Non enim terra sibi pluit, aut non quidquid genuerit arescit, nisi pluvia desuper descendat. Dicit quodam loco in psalmo: Pluviam voluntaryam segregabis, Deus, haereditati tuae (Ps 67,10). Quare dixit voluntarily? Quia non meritis nostris, sed illius volúntate. Quid enim boni meruimus peccatores? quid boni meruimus iniqui? Ex Adam Adam, et super Adam fines peccata nascuntur. to make it beautiful. Then he called the grace of God the dew of Hermon. 11. You must know what Hermon is. It is a mountain distant from Jarusalem, that is, from Zion. That is why it is surprising that the psalmist says this: As the dew of Hermon descends on the mountains of Zion, since Mount Hermon is far from Jerusalem, since it is said to be on the other side of the Jordan. Then let's investigate what Hermon means. It is a Hebrew name; and we know its meaning because of those who know that language. Hermon is said to mean lofty light. From Christ comes the dew, because no light was exalted apart from Christ. How was he exalted? First on the cross, then in heaven. He was exalted on the cross by humbling himself, but his humiliation could only be elevated. The stewardship or administration of man diminished more and more every day; This was symbolized in Saint John the Baptist. The stewardship of God grew day by day in our Lord Jesus Christ, which is also made known by the days of his birth, since John was born, according to the tradition of the Church, on June 24, when the days begin to decrease, and the Lord was born on December 25, when the days begin to grow. Listen to John himself, who says: It is good for Him to increase, but for me to decrease. Their passions also demonstrate this. The Lord was lifted up on the cross, John was reduced by cutting off his head. Therefore the exalted light is Christ, whence comes the dew of Hermon. All of you who desire to dwell in union, long for this dew; it will rain on you from here.

Otherwise you will not be able to fulfill what you profess, nor will you be able to dare to promise, unless He has let His voice be heard; nor will you be able to remain if you lack their food or help, for their food comes down on the mountains of Zion. 12. The mountains of Zion are great in Zion. What is Zion? The Church. And what mountains are there? Big. Those who symbolize the mountains, the beard symbolizes the same, the gorget of the dress symbolizes the same. Beard is only understood as those who are perfect, since only those in whom the charity of Christ is found live in union. Because in those who do not have the charity of Christ, even when they live in one, they hate, annoy, torment, and disturb others with their bad mood and are looking for what to say about them. What happens to them is what happens to the restless donkey that is harnessed to the team, which not only does not pull, but breaks with its kicks what is harnessed to it. But if he possesses the dew of Hermon, which descends on the mountains of Zion, he is meek, calm, humble, tolerant, and prays instead of murmuring, for murmurers were wonderfully described in a certain place of Scripture: The bowels of the foolish are like the wheels of a chariot. What does it mean: The guts or the heart of the fool are like the wheels of the cart? That is loaded with hay and creaks. The wheel of the cart cannot help but squeak. Thus there are many brothers; They only dwell in union regarding the body. But who are those who live in union? Those of whom it is said: There was only one soul in them and one heart in God; and no one had anything of his own, but all the

tamen misericors amavit, et sponsus dilexít, non pluchram, sed ut faceret pulchram. Ergo gratiam Dei dixit rorem Hermon. 11. Sed Hermón quid sit, nosse debentis. Mons est quidam longe disiunctus ab Ierusalem, id est a Sion. Itaque mirum est quod sic ait, Sicut ros Hermon, who descended super mountains Zion; cum mons Hermon longe sit disiunctus ab Jerusalem; nam trans Iordanem esse dicitur. Ergo aliquid interpretatione Hermon quaeramus. Nomen enim hebraeum est, et habemus interpretationem ab eis qui illam linguam noverunt. Hermon interpret dicitur, Lumen exaltatum. To Christo enim ros: nam nullum lumen exaltatum, nisi Christus. What exaltatum is this? Cousin in crossing; post in cáelo. Exaltatus in intersection, cum humiliaretur; sed humíliatio illius non potuit nisi alta esse. Hominis dispensatio minus minusque fiebat, quae significatur in Ioanne; Dei dispensatio in Domino nostro Iesu Christo crescebat: quod et natalibus eorum ostenditur. Nam Ule natus est, sicut tradit Ecclesia, eighth iulias calends, cum iam incipiunt minui dies: Dominus autem natus eighth iunuary calends, quando iam dies incipiunt crescere. Audi ipsum Ioannem confitentem: Illum oportet crescere, me autem minui (lo 3.30). Et passiones ipsorum hoc indicat. Dominus in cruz exaltatus est; ille caeso capite deminutus. Ergo lumen exaltatum, Christus: inde est ros Hermon. Sed quicumque vultis habitare

in unum, optate rorem istum, compluimini inde. Alioquin non poteritis tenere quod profitemini, nec profiteri audere poteritis, nisi ille intonuerit; nec permanere poteritis, nisi eius sagina non desit vobis: ipsa enim sagina descendit super mountains Zion. 12. Iam mountains Zion, magni in Sion. Who is Zion? Ecclesia. Et qui ibi sunt montes? Magni. Quos signifier montes, hos significat beard, hos significat ora attire. Barba non intelligitur nisi in perfectis. Non ergo habitant in unum, nisi in quibus perfection fuerit charitas Christi. Nam in quibus non est perfection charitas Christi, et eum in uno sint, odiosi sunt, molesti sunt, turbulenti sunt, anxietate sua turbant caeteros, et quaerunt quid de illis dicant; quomodo in iunctura inquietum iumentum non solum non trahit, sed et frangit calcibus quod iunctum est. Si autem habet rorem Hermón, qui descendit super montes Sion, quietus, platatus, himilis, tolerans, pro murmure precem fundit. Nam murmuratores omnes magnifice descripti sunt quodam loco Scripturarum: Praecordia fatui sicut rota carri (Eccl 33,5). What is it, Praecordia fatui sicut rota carri? Fenum portat, et murmurat: non enim potest rota carri quiescere a murmure. Sic sunt multi fratres; non inhabitant in unum nisi corpore. Among the brothers who live in union. There he prescribed the blessing, there those who dwell in harmony bless the Lord. Because in discord you do not bless the Lord. Without reason you say that your tongue praises God if your heart is silent; With your mouth you bless and with your heart you curse. With their mouth they blessed and with their heart they cursed, says a psalm. Are they my words? Some were pointed out here. You bless God when you pray, and, continuing in your prayer, you curse your enemy. But pay attention; This is what you heard from the Lord: Love your enemies. If you work and love your enemy so that you pray for him, God has ordered his blessing there, and you will have life there for the ages, that is, eternally. Many, loving this life, curse their enemies. And why? For this life, for worldly interests. How did your enemy oppress you that you are forced to curse him? Did it afflict you on earth? Emigrate from her; lives in heaven. "How," you say, "will I dwell in heaven, being flesh, given to the flesh?" Precede with the heart so that you may continue with the body. Don't listen while pretending to be deaf: Hearts up! Keep your heart up, and no one will grieve you in heaven. Hence the following psalm continues admirably. suum esse, sed erant Mis omnia communia (Acts 4:32). Designati sunt, descripti sunt, qui pertineant ad barbam, qui pertineant ad oram vestimenti, qui numerentur inter montes Sion. Et si ibi alii numeratores, meminerint dicti Domini: Unus assumetur, et unus relinquetur (Mt 24,40). 13. Quoniam ibi mandavit T)ominus benedictionem. Ubi mandavit? In fratribus qui inhabitant in unum. Ibi praecepit benedictionem, ibi benedicunt Dominum qui habitant concorditer. Nam in discordia non benedicis Dominum. Sine causa dicis quia lingua tua sonat benedictionem Domini, si corde non sones: ore benedicis, et corde maledicis. Pray suo benedicebat, et corde suo maledicebat (Ps 61,5). Numquid verba nostra sunt? Meaning sunt quidam. Benedicis Dominum, cum oras; et sequeris in prece tua, et maledicis inimico tuo. Hoc est quod audisti ab ipso Domino, Diligite inimicos vestros?

Si autem facias, et diligas inimicum tuum, et ores pro eo, ibi mandavit Dominus benedictionem suam; ibi habebis vitam in saeculum, id est in aeternum. Multi enim lovers vitam istam, maledicunt inimicis suis: pro qua re, nisi pro ista vita, nisi pro commodis saecularibus? Ubi te angustavit inimicus tuus, ut cogaris maledicere? In tena angustatus is; migrate, live in cáelo. Quomodo, inquies, habito in cáelo, homo carne indutus, carni deditus? Corde praecede, quo sequaris corpore. Noli surdus audire, Sursum corda. Sursum cor habe, et nemo te angustabit in cáelo. Et ideo bene sequitur alius psalmus:

1 [v.l]. Hey, now is the time to bless the Lord, all the servants of the Lord, those who are in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God. Why did he add in the courts? The atriums are the largest rooms in the house. The one who is in the atriums or in the hallways is not narrowed or oppressed, in a certain way it is dilated. Remain in breadth, and you will be able to love your enemy, because you do not love the things for which you can suffer hardship from your enemies. How will you know you are in the courts? Remain in charity, and you will be in the courts. In charity there is ease, and in hatred there is narrowness. Hear the Apostle: Anger, indignation, tribulation and anguish (will be) in every soul of the man who does evil. And what does it say about the breadth of charity? That the charity of God was spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. When you hear diffusion, you understand width; When you hear breadth, think of the courts of the Lord, and you will have the true blessing of the Lord by not cursing your enemies. The Holy Spirit speaks here to those who suffer tribulation; and, exhorting them to glory in it, he says to them: Come, now is the time to bless the Lord, all the servants of the Lord. What does it mean: Hey, now? In this time. Because, after the tribulations, it is evident that we will dedicate ourselves to blessing the Lord, as it was said: Well-

1 [v.l]. Ecce nunc benedicite Dominum, omnes serví Domini, qui statis in domo Domini, in atriis domus Dei nostri. Quare addidit, in atriis? Atria amplificara spatia domus intelliguntur. Qui stat in atriis non angustatur, non premitur; quodam mode dilatatur. In latitudine mane, et potes diligere inimicum tuum; quia non ea diligis, ubi ab inimico anguishes patiaris. Quomodo intelligeris stare in atriis? Sta in charitate, et stas in atriis. In charitate latitudo est, in hatred anguish. Audi Apostolum: Ira et indignatio, tribulatio et anguish in omnem animam hominis operantis malum (Rom 2,8.9). De latitudine autem charitatis quid dicit? Quoniam charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis (ib. 5,5). Ubi audis diffusionem, intellige latitudinem; ubi audis latitudinem, intellige atria Domini; et habebis veram benedictionem Domini, quando non maledicis inimicis. Alloquitur enim Spiritus eos qui patiuntur tribulationem, ut glorientur in tribulationibus; et dicit eis, Ecce nunc benedicite Dominum, omnes serví Domini. Quid est, Ecce nunc? In hoc tempore. This is Ea, now is the time to bless the Lord, all the servants of the Lord who are in the house of the Lord, what does it mean for those who are there? Those of you who persevere. For it was said of one who was an archangel: He did not remain in the truth; and likewise it was said of the bridegroom's friend: The bridegroom's friend stands and hears him, and is glad when he hears the bridegroom's voice. 2 [v.2]. Then those who are in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our Lord, at night raise your hands towards the sanctuary and bless the Lord. It is easy to bless during the day. What does "during the day" mean? In prosperous events. The night is the sad event, and the day is the happy one. When things go well for you, you bless the Lord. When you want a child and it is born to you, you bless the Lord. Your wife is freed from the danger of childbirth, you bless the Lord. Your son was sick, heal, bless the Lord. But your son is sick, perhaps you consulted the fortune teller, the exhauster; perhaps you burst into some curse against the Lord, not verbal, but of action, curse of customs, curse of bad living; Do not boast because you bless with your tongue if you curse with your way of living. "How—you say—do I curse with my life?" Because you look at your life and say: "See what a Christian, see what Christians are." For you it is blasest: Beati qui habitant in domo tua; in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). Qui tune benedicturi sunt sine defectu, hic incipiunt benedicere Dominum; hic in tribulationibus, in temptationibus, in molestiis, Inter adversitates saeculi, Inter insidias inimici, Inter frauds et Ímpetus diaboli. Hoc est, Ecce nunc benedicite Dominum, omnes serví Domini, qui statis in domo Domini. Quid est, qui statis? Qui persevere. Quia dictum est de quodam, qui archangelus Fuit, Et in veritate non stetit (lo 8,44): et dictum est de amico sponsi, Amicus autem sponsi stat, et audit eum, et gaudio gaudet propter vocem sponsi (ib 3,29). 2 [v.2]. Ergo, Qui statis in domo Domini, in atriis domus Dei nostri, in noctibus extollite manus vestras in sancta, et benedicite Dominum. Facile est benedicere in diebus. Quid est, in diebus?

In rebus prosperis. Nox enim tristis res est; dies res es laeta. When tibi bene est, you bless Dominum. When filium desideras et nascitur, benedicis Dominum. Liberata est uxor tua a periculo parthias; benedicis Dominum. Aegrotabat filius, liberatur; benedicis Dominum. Aegrotabat filius; forte quaesisti mathematicum, sortilegum: forte non de lingua, sed de moribus tuis exiít maledictio in Dominum; exit de moribus et vita tua. Noli gloriari quia lingua benedicis, si vita maledicis. Quomodo, inquis, vita maledico? Quia attenditur vita tua, et dicitar: Ecce christianus, ecce quales sunt

fema against Christ. What good is it if you bless with your tongue, if you curse with your life? Then bless the Lord. When? In the nights. When did Job bless? In the gloomy night. They took everything he owned from him; They took away his children, for whom he kept him. What a gloomy night! But let us see if, nevertheless, he does not bless in the night: The Lord gave him to me, the Lord took him away from me; As it pleased the Lord, so it was done. Blessed be the name of the Lord. What a sad night! Ulcerated from head to toe, it was rotting away. Then Eve dared to tempt him, saying: Say something against God and die. Hear him who blesses in the night: You spoke like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the hand of the Lord, will we not endure evil? See there what it means: At night raise your hands towards the sanctuary and bless the Lord. What did Job say? You spoke like one of the foolish women. Adam, rotten, rejected Eve, as if he had told her: "It is enough that for you I became mortal. You were stronger in paradise, but you are defeated in the dunghill." Sublime grace of God! But where did this come from? That the dew of Hernon had rained on his soul and the Lord had given him the softness so that our land could produce its fruit. At night, raise your hands towards the sanctuary and bless the Lord. 3 [v.3]. May the Lord, who made heaven and earth, bless you from Zion. 1 [v.l]. It should be extremely sweet to us and it should rejoice us in what this psalm exhorts us to do. It begins like this: Praise the name of the Lord. He then explains why it is right for us to praise the name of the Lord, saying: Praise the Lord, servants. What is more just, what is more worthy, what is more pleasant? In fact, if the servants did not praise the Lord, they would be proud, ungrateful, impious. And what do they achieve by not praising the Lord? Perceive him terrible. The ungrateful servant cannot, because he does not want to praise the Lord, not be a servant. Whether you praise or not, you are a servant; but if you praise him, you will have favor with him; If you do not praise him, you will offend him. Therefore exhortation is good and useful; hence we should put more effort into seeing how God should be praised than into hesitating to praise Him. Then praise the name of the Lord. The psalm, the prophet, the Spirit of God and, finally, the Lord himself, us (Ps 132,1). Pluralis numerus, fratres; sed singularis habitare in unum: ideo, Benedícat te Dominus ex Síon, qui jecit caelum et terram. Nemo vestrum dicat: Ad me non pervenit. Putas quis est quem dixit, Benedicat te Dominus ex Sion? Unum benedixit: esto unum, et pervenit ad te benedictio.

They exhort us to praise God. God does not grow with our praise, but we do. God does not become better because you praise Him nor worse because you revile Him; but you, praising the good, will be better; reviling him, worse. However, He remains good as He is. If He teaches His servants, those who serve Him well or deserve good from Him, the preachers of His word, the rectors of His Church, those who reverence His name, those who fulfill His precepts, to retain in their conscience the sweetness of their good life so that they may not be corrupted by the praises or broken by the reproaches of men, how much more does the Immutable One, who is above all things and who teaches everything? Will this not become greater because you praise him or lesser because you revile him? But since it is our business to praise the Lord, he mercifully commands that we praise him without arrogance. Let us hear what he says: Praise the name of the Lord; Praise, servants, the Lord. You servants do nothing extraordinary by praising the Lord, for if you should praise the Lord even if you were always servants, how much more should you, being servants, praise the Lord so that you also deserve to be sons? 2 [v.2]. But as it was written in another psalm: Praise belongs to the upright; and also in another place: Praise is not beautiful in the mouths of sinners; and likewise it is said in another psalm: The sacrifice of praise will glorify me; and there is the way in which I will show you the health of God; and, consequently, it is also recorded: God said to the sinner: "Why do you count my righteousnesses and take my praise into your mouth? You hated enim laudibus nostris ille crescit, sed nos. Deus nec melior fit, si laudaverís; nec deterior, si vituperaveris: sed tu laudando bonum, melior eris; vituperando, deterior: bonus autem ille manet, ut est. Si enim servos suos ipsos bene de se merits, praedicatores verbi sui, rectores Ecclesiae suae, veneratores nominis sui, obtemperatores mandati sui id docet, ut in conscientia sua habeant dulcedinem bonae vitae suae, ne corrumpantur laudibus, ne frangantur vituperationibus hominum; quanto magis ipse incommutabilis super omnia qui haecdocet, non utique maior fit si laudaveris, nec minor si vituperaveris? Sed quoniam nobis expedit laudare Dominum, misericordíter íubet ut laudemus eum, non arroganter. served, Dominum.

Nom enim aliquid incongruum facitis, laudando servi Dominum: etsi semper tantummodo servi essetis, beretis laudare Dominum; How many magis should you laudare Dominum servi, ut esse mereamini et filii? 2 [v.2]. Sed quoniam scriptum est in alio psalmo, Rectos decet laudanum (Ps 32,1); et item alibi scriptum est, Non est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris (Eccl 15,9); itemque alibi dicitur, Sacrificium laudis glorificabit me, et ibi via est in qua ostendam Mi salutare Dei; et consequenter, Peccatori autem dixit Deus, Utquid tu enanas iustitias meas, et assumis testamentum meum per os tuum? due to the rational soul, by which he is man; in the cattle, the unlearned, but who have faith, because, if not, they would lack firstborns. He worked signs and wonders in you, O Egypt! against Pharaoh and against his servants. Pharaoh was the king of the Egyptians. Pay attention to the name. See how God does these things. The king is the most prominent personage of every nation. Egypt means affliction, and Pharaoh dispersion. Therefore affliction has dispersion as its king, because those who afflict the Church afflict it dispersed. What's more, to afflict her they disperse. But as the king leads and the people follow, the dispersion precedes and affliction follows. Hear, hear these names in typical and wisdom-filled significance, and you will not find even one of them that indicates any good in which God exercised his wrath. 20 [v.10-11]. He wounded many nations and killed powerful kings. Tell what nations and what kings: To Sion king of the Amorites. Hear the names, full of mysteries. He says he killed Zion. of his servants and in the temptations that his Church endures; Let not your hand cease to kill such kings and such people, for Sion means temptation of the eyes, and Amorites, provokers of anger. Is it any wonder that the provokers of wrath have such a king as their king, a mendacious king? If simulation and lies do not precede, there are no provokers of anger in the Church, since they provoke anger because they pretend. May the hand of the Lord kill this one and those; to this one so that he does not induce those to correct themselves. Indeed, each man kills this king in himself when he condemns simulation and loves the truth. The hand or power of God does not cease to do this, because as he did then in historical reality, so he does it now spiritually so that what he prophetically announced may be fulfilled. He also killed another king and his people: Og, king of Bashan. This one, how bad it was! Og means occlusion, and Basan confusion. Perverse is the king who intercepts the path to God. The devil does this; Therefore, always opposing his fictions and deceptions, opposing his idols, opposing himself, as something necessary for the possessed, for the spell-hackers, for the soothsayers, for the soothsayers, for the enchanters, for the rites of demons, he closes the way. Audite, audite nomina haec, interpretatione typica et sapientia plena: nec unum inveni sex istis nominibus, quod boni aliquid interpretetur, ubi exercuit Deus iram suam. 20 [10-11]. Percussit gentes fines, et occidit reges fortes. Dic quos reges et quas gentes? Seon regem Amorrhaeorum. Audite nomina gravida sacramentis. Seon regem, inquit, Amorrhaeorum occidit. Occidit plans; et nunc occidat a cordibus servorum suorum, et a temptationibus

Ecclesiae suae, nec cesset manus eius in occidendis talibus regibus et talibus populis: interpretatur enim Seon, Tentatio oculorum; Amorrhaei interpretantur, Amaricantes. Iam hic videte si intelligere possumus quomodo amaricantes regem habeant temptationem oculorum. Tentatio oculorum non est nisi mendacium: colorem habet, veritatem non habet. Iam quid mirum est si amaricantes talem habeant regem, mendacem regem? Nisi enim mendacium et simulatio praecedat, non sunt amaricantes in Ecclesia; inde enim amaricant, quia fingunt. Praecedit tentatio oculorum, amaricatio sequitur: et in ipso diabolo praecessit; nam tentatio oculorum est quod transfigurat se velut angelum lucís (2 Cor 9:14). Occidat manus Domini et illum et illos; illum, ne inducat; illos, ut corrigantur. Etenim in unoquoque homine occiditur ille rex, quando damnat simulationem, et diligit veritatem. Manus Dei non quiescit id agere. Nam quemadmodum egit ad litteram tune, sic agit nunc spiritualiter, ut impleat quod tune prophetice praenuntiavit. Occidit etiam alium regem et alium populum eius: Et Og regem Basan. Et hic quam malus! Og interpretatur Conclusio: Basan interpretatur, Confusio. Malus est rex ille qui intercludit viam ad Deum. Hoc enim agit diabolus; semper opponendo figmenta sua, opponendo idola sua, opponendo se necessarium per arreptitios, sorceresses, augurs, haruspices, magicians, sacra daemoniorum, concludit viam. Quomodo per Christum id agitur, ut patat via, quae fuet Inter-

Through Him a certain redeemed person says: And with my God I will cross the wall, so the devil does nothing but close the way so that people do not believe in God. If you believe in God, the way is clear, because Christ himself is the way. If you don't believe in Him, you are obstructed. If, then, it has been obstructed because it is not believed, what remains? That, when the one who was not believed comes, those who did not believe will be confused. Because? Because obstruction precedes and confusion follows. Obstruction precedes as a king, and confusion follows as a people. Those who are now prevented from believing in Christ, when Christ appears, will all be confused, and their iniquities will cause them to pass over to the opposite party. And then the wicked will say in confusion: What good did pride do to us? Deep mystery, my brothers: dispersion is the king of affliction; They are scattered to be afflicted. Profound mystery: the temptation of the eyes, that is, deception, is the king of those who provoke anger, they deceive to provoke it. Occlusion is the king of confusion: they close themselves so as not to believe, and when the One in whom we believe comes, they will be confused. And God killed all the kingdoms of Canaan. Canaan means the prepared for humility. Humility represents a good; but humility is profitable, because perverse humility is worthy of punishment. If humility were not also penal, it would not be said: He who exalts himself will be humiliated, since no mercy is given when he is punished with humiliation. Therefore Canaan now means proud. Every wicked and every unfaithful exalts his heart, because he does not want to believe in God. But this exaltation prepares the Clusa; nam per eum redemptus quidam dicit, Et in Deo meo transgrediar murum (Ps 18:30): sic diabolus nihil aliud agit, nisi ut intercludat viam, ne credatur in Deum. Si enim creditur in Deum, patet via; et ipse Christus est via (lo 14,6): si autem non creditur in Deum, interclusa est via. If autem interclusa fuerit, quia non creditur; quid restat, nisi ut cum venerit qui non credebatur, confundantur qui non crediderunt? Quare? Quia conclusio praecedit, et sequitur confusio: conclusio praecedit ut rex, sequitur confusio tanquam plebs. Quos moda condudit, ut non credant in Christum, quando apparuerit Christus, omnes confundentur, et comunicant eos ex adverso iniquitates eorum. Tune digont impii confusi: Quid nobis profuit superbia? (Wis 5:8). Magna mysteria, fratres mei. Dissipatio rex afflictionis; dissipantur ut affligantur. Magna mysteria.

Tentatio oculorum, id est fallada, rex amaricantium; fallunt enim ut amaricent. Conclusion rex confusionis; concluduntur enim ne transeant ad fidem, et cum venerit in quem credimus, confundentur. Et omnia regna Chanaan occidit Deus. Chanaan interpretatur, Paratus humilitati. Humilitas quasi bonum aliquod significat, sed si sit utilis humilitas: nam mala humiliatio poenalis est. Si enim humiliatio ad poenam non pertineret, non diceretur, Qui se exaltat humiliabitur (Luke 14,11; et 18,14): non enim beneficium illi praestatur, quando punitur ut humilietur. Chanaan ergo superbus mode est. Omnis impius, omnis infideiis exaltat cor suum; non vult credere in Deum. Sed haec exaltatio parata est humilitati

unbelievers humiliation for the day of judgment, because then he will be humiliated when he does not want to; for there are vessels of wrath that are prepared for perdition. Now become arrogant, chatter, throw yourself at the faithful, laugh at them, mock the Christians, say: "The things they say about the day of judgment are old wives' tales." This conceit of theirs prepares humiliation. When the judge who is now announced and laughed at comes, then the one who now prides himself will be humiliated, not profitably, but penally. Now he is not humiliated, but he is preparing to be humiliated; that is, he prepares for condemnation, he prepares to be a victim. 21 [v.13]. God executed all this, materially, when our fathers were taken out of the land of Egypt; spiritually, now, and furthermore his work does not cease until the end. Lest you think that, having then materially accomplished these things, the power of God ceased, he says: Lord, your name endures forever. That is, your mercy does not cease, your hand or power does not cease to do in this age these things that you then announced prefiguring, since all things happened in figure to them, but were written for our correction on whom the end of the ages has come to fall. Lord, your mercy will endure from generation to generation. The generation of this life and the generation of the next, the generation through which we become faithful and are reborn through baptism, the generation through which we will rise from the dead and live, together with the angels, eternally. Your memory, Lord, will remain on this generation and on the next, because not even now have you forgotten us in diem iudicii; tune humiliabitur, quando non vult: sunt enim vasa irae, quae perfection sunt ad perditionem (Rom 9:22). Modo extollant se, garríant, extendant se super fideles, irrideant fideles, blasphement Christianos; dicant, Anicularia sunt ista quae dicunt de die iudicii. Ista elatio eorum parata est humilitati. Quando venerit iudex, qui moda annuntiatus irridetur; tune ille qui modo superbit, non utiliter, sed poenaliter humiliabitur. Modo autem non humiliatur, sed paratur humilitati, id est, paratur damnationi, paratur victimae. 21 [v.13]. Omnia ergo ista evertit Deus; corporaliter tune, when patres nostri educti sunt de terra Aegypti; evertit spiritualiter nunc, nec cessat manus eius usque in finem. Ideo ne istas potentias Dei tune putes peractas cessasse: Domine, nomen tuunt, inquit, in saeculum.

Id est, non cessat misericordia tua, non cessat manus tua in saeculum faceré ista, quae tune praenuntiasti figurando: «Omnia enim illa in figura contingebant illis; scripta sunt autem ad correptionem nostram, in quos finis saeculorum obvenit” (1 Cor 10:11). «Domine memoriale tuum in generationem et generationem». Generatio ista et generatio altera: generatio qua fideles efficimur, et per Baptismum renascimur; generatio qua a mortuis resurgemus, et Angelis coniuncti vivemus in aeternum. Memoriale tuum, Domine, et super generationem istam, et super illam generationem: quia nec nunc nos oblitus est, ut vocaret; nec tune oblivisce-

call us nor then will he forget to crown us. Your memory, Lord, will remain from generation to generation. 22 [v.14]. The Lord judged his people. The Lord completed all those things for the Jewish people. But perhaps his works remained stagnant after he brought his people into the promised land? Without a doubt he will still judge, for the Lord judged his people and will be called by his servants. He has already judged his people. Leaving aside future judgment, the Jewish people have already been judged. What does "it is already judged" mean? That the just are already separated and the unjust have remained. If I lie, or you think I lie because I said that it is already judged, hear the Lord, who says: For judgment I came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may remain blind. The proud were blinded and the humble were enlightened. Then he judged his people. Isaiah indicated this judgment (by saying): And now you, house of Jacob, come; let us walk in the light of the Lord; this is little. What's next? Well, he abandoned his people, the house of Israel. The house of Jacob is the same as Israel, because Jacob is Israel. You know the holy Scriptures, and I think you will remember that Jacob, when he saw the angel fighting against him, received the name Israel. One man is Jacob and Israel, one person. So the house of Jacob and the house of Israel are one nation, one people; Therefore, he rejects and invites the same. Now you have killed Christ, oh house of Jacob! You already killed Christ, you already shook your head at the cross, you already mocked her pendant and said to her: If it is

the Son of God, come down from the cross. The Doctor already prayed for the frantic: Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they are doing. No doubt you have already done all these things; now believe in Him whom you killed; drink the blood you shed. Now, house of Jacob, I wish to expound with the testimony of Isaiah what the psalmist said: The Lord judged his people and by his servants he will be called. It is understood that he judged his people by separating in the same people the good from the bad, the believers from the unbelievers, the apostles from the lying Jews. Against the opponents, against the rebels, against those who unknowingly made martyrs with the slaughter of the faithful, the Lord prevailed. And how did it prevail? the word of the Lord are called gods, should angels also be called gods, since just and holy men are promised the great reward of being equal to the angels? I doubt that there is or can easily be found in Scripture any testimony that clearly calls angels gods. However, when the Lord God was told that he is terrible above all gods, then, as if declaring which gods he was referring to, he added: because the gods of the nations are demons. About these gods he said that the Lord was terrible in his saints, whom he made heavens and by whom the demons are afraid, for the psalm continues, saying: but the Lord made them heavens. Therefore they are not gods without addition, that is, in any way, but gods of the Gentiles, which are demons. Previously God said: It is terrible over all the gods, and not "over all the gods of the Gentiles", although perhaps He would have wanted this to be understood by adding the following: because the gods of the Gentiles are demons. In the Hebrew text it was not written this way, but: The gods of the Gentiles are simulacra. 4 [v.2]. I worshiped in your holy temple. What is your holy temple? The one where we will live, where we will worship. Let us run to worship. Our heart being pregnant, is ready to give birth, and looks for a place to give birth. What is the place where God should be worshiped? What world, what building, what throne between the sky and the stars? We search the holy Scriptures, and find

In the book of Proverbs the following words of Wisdom: I was with Him, I delighted every day. He declares his works to us and shows us his throne. What throne? When he established, he says, the impetuous clouds on high, when he isolated his throne above the winds. His throne is his temple. Then where will we go? Should we worship on the winds? If we worship above the winds, the birds surpass us. But if we understand souls by winds, that is to say that souls are symbolized under the name of wind, as Scripture says in a certain place: He flew on the wings of the winds; that is, about the virtues or power of souls; and hence the breath of God is called soul, as if it were wind; not because this wind or breath is understood from which we perceive the substance when it is thrown, but because under its name something invisible is indicated, which cannot be seen by the eyes, nor perceived by the ear, nor entered into the smell, nor be tasted on the palate, nor be touched by the hands; which is, without a doubt, a certain life by which we live, and which is called soul; If we understand the winds as souls, there is no reason to look for marital wings so that with the birds we can fly towards the temple of God to worship Him, but rather we will find that God is seated above us if we want to be His faithful. See if this is not what the Apostle says: The temple of God that is you is holy. However, it is true and evident that God dwells in the angels. Then when our joy coming from spiritual things, not from earthly goods, begins to sing the song to God to praise before the angels, the same congregation of angels is the temple of God and

et invenimus in verbis Sapientiae: Ego, inquit, eram cum illo; ego eram ad quam adgaudebat quotidie. Et dicit opera eius, et exponit nobis sedem ipsius. Quam? Quando validas, inquit, faciebat in supreme clouds quando sedem suam segregabat super winds (Prov 8,30.27-28). Sedes autem eius templum eius. Quo ergo ibimus? Super ventos adoraturi sumus? Si autem intelligamus ventos animas, id est, ventorum nomine significatas animas, sicut ait quodam loco Scriptura, Volavit super pennas ventorum (Ps 17:11); hoc est, super virtutes animarum: unde et flatus Dei dicitut anima (Gen 2,7), tanquam ventus, non ut iste intelligatur ventus quo corpus propellente sentimus, sed ut eius nomine significetur aliquid invisibile, quod ñeque oculis cerni potest, nec sensible auribus, nec odoratu duci, nec palato gusta, nec manu contrectari; quod est utique vita quaedam, qua vivimus, quae anima dicitur: si hos ventos intellexerimus, non est quare quaeramus pennas visibiles, ut cum avibus volemus ad adorandum ad templum Dei; sed super nos ipsos inveniemus Deum sedere, si eius fideles esse voluerimus. And before the angels I will praise you. I will not praise before men, but before angels. My psaltery is my joy; but my joy, which comes from lower things, is the joy that I manifest before men; The joy of higher things is what I demonstrate before the angels. The wicked does not know the joy of the righteous: Joy does not belong to the wicked, says the Lord. The wicked rejoices in the tavern, the martyr in prison. She was happy to be arrested, to be brought before the judge; when she was put in prison, when, tied, she was presented before the crowds, when she was lifted up on the rack, when she was judged, when she was condemned; In all circumstances she rejoiced, and the wretched considered her to be unfortunate who rejoiced before the angels.

What did it provide us if not what we eat and drink today? Therefore, having served us as the Lord of the angels, let us not be afraid of later being equal to the angels. 5. And I will praise your name for your mercy and for your truth. For these two things we will praise, for this is also read in another psalm: All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth. For these two things we will praise: for your mercy and for your truth. Through mercy you looked upon the sinner, through truth you gave him the promise. Then for your mercy and truth I will praise you. According to my strength, I return to you these things that you gave me by working mercy and truth: mercy by helping and truth by judging. Through them we are helped by God, through them we deserve God. Therefore all the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth. There are no other ways by which He comes to us, there are no other ways by which we go to Him.

6. Because you exalted your holy name above all. What congratulation is this, brothers? He magnified his holy name over Abraham, for Abraham believed God, and righteousness was imputed to him. All other nations sacrificed to idols, served demons. Isaac was born to Abraham, and God was magnified over that house; Jacob was born from him, and God, magnified, says: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob. From Jacob came twelve sons, and from them the people of Israel, delivered from Egypt, led through the Red Sea, trained in the desert and placed in the promised land having expelled its people from it. The name of the Lord was magnified over Israel. From here came the Virgin Mary, from here our Lord Jesus Christ, who died for our sins, who was resurrected for our justification, who filled the faithful with the Holy Spirit and commanded to preach among the nations: Do penance, because the kingdom of heaven is at hand. See, then, how he exalted his holy name above all. 7 [v.3]. On any day that I call upon you, immediately hear me. Why instantly? For you said: You will be found still speaking, and I will say: "Here I am." Why instantly? Because I am no longer heading for earthly happiness, since I learned the holy desire of the New Testament. I ask neither the fertility of the flesh, nor temporal health, nor the submission of enemies, nor riches, nor honors; I ask for none of this; so hear me soon. Because you taught me what to ask for, give me what I ask for. Let's say to this one: Do you ask for something similar? Let's hear; declare your

templum Dei. Ecclesia deorsum, et Ecclesia sursum: Ecclesia deorsum in omnibus fidelibus, Ecclesia sursum in omnibus Angelis. Sed descendit ad Ecclesiam deorsum Dominus Angelorum, et ei Angelí in terra ministraverunt ministrantí nobis (Mt 4,11). Non enim veni, inquit, ministrari, sed ministrare (ib. 20,28). Quid nobis ministravit, nisi quod hodieque manducamus et bibimus? Cum ergo Dominus Angelorum nobis ministravit, non desperemus non Futures aequales Angelis. Maior enim Angelis descendit ad hominem, et Creator Angelorum suscepit hominem, Dominus Angelorum mortuus est pro homine. I worship ergo ad templum sanctum tuum: intelligo templum tuum non manu factum, sed quod tu fecisti tibi. 5. Et confitebor nomini tuo, in misericordia tua et veritate tua. In duobus istis confitemur: sic enim et in alio psalmo legitur. Universae viae Domini misericordia et veritas (Ps 24:10). In duobus istis confitemur: in your mercy, et in your veritate. Misericordia peccatorem respexisti, veritate promissionem reddidisti. In tua ergo misericordia et veritate confitebor tibi. Has etiam ego pro meis viribus reddo, quas mihi donasti, faciens misericordiam et veritatem; Misericordiam in subveniendo, veritatem in judicando. His adiuvamur a Deo, his promeremur Deum. Merit ergo mercy et veritas universae viae Domini. Non sunt aliae viae, quibus ad nos vinot; non sunt aliae viae, quibus ad illum veniamus.

6. Quoniam magnificasti super omne, nomen sanctum tuum. Qualis ista gratulatio, fratres? Magnificavit nomen suum sanctum super Abraham. Credidit enim Abraham Deo, et deputatum est illi ad iustitiam (Gen 15,6; Rom 4,3). Caeterae omnes gentes idolis immolabant, daemonibus serviebant. Ñatus est ex Abraham Isaac; magnificatus est super illam domum Deus: inde Iacob; magnificatus est Deus, qui dicit, Ego sum Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus Iacob (Ex 3,6): inde duodecim filii, inde populus Israel liberatus ab Aegypto, ductus per mare Rubrum, exercitatus in eremo, eiectis Gentibus in terra promissionis collocatus est. Magnificatum est nomen Domini super Israel. Be inde et virgo Maria, inde Dominus Christus, mortuus propter peccata nostra, resurgens propter iustificationem nostram (Rom 4,25), implens fideles Spiritu sancto, mittens praedicari per gentes, Agite poenitentiam, appropinquavit enim regnum caelorum (Mt 3,2): et ecce magnificavit super omne, nomen sanctum suum. 7 [v.3]. In quacumque die invokevero te, I quote exaudí me. Quare, quote? Quia tu dixisti, Adhuc loquente te dicam, Ecce adsum (Is 58,9). Quare, quote? Quia iam non peto congratulatem terrenam, didici sanctum desiderium de novo testament. Non peto terram, non fecunditatem carnalem, non salutem temporalem, non inimicorum subiectionem, non divitias, non honores; nihil horum peto: ideo cita exaudí me. Quia docuisti quid petam, da quod peto. Dicamus huic: Tale aliquid petis?

request and see what he asks, and learn through him to ask so that we deserve to receive. You had come to church today to ask for I don't know what. What did we think you had come to ask for? You had come with your wish; I don't know with what. I wish I were innocent, even if I were carnal! But put away iniquity, put away carnality; Learn what you have to ask for, attend the party you celebrate today. You celebrate the birth of the holy and blessed woman Crispina and perhaps you wish for earthly happiness. She, out of holy desire, abandoned the happiness she had on earth; She left her children crying and complaining, as if she were a cruel mother, since the one who rushed to obtain the divine crown seemed to have lost human compassion. Was he perhaps unaware of what he longed for, what he trampled on? On the contrary, he knew how to chant before the angels of God, and to desire their company, holy and pure friendship, where from now on he would not die, where he would know the judge before whom lying can have no place. Well what? In that life, is there no good? What do I say? There are only goods there; There are no goods mixed with evils, but tranquility, in which you will enjoy as much as you want and no one will tell you: "Refrain." Here it is too annoying and dangerous to enjoy earthly goods; do not enjoy so that you run aground, and, rejoicing badly, you perish. For why does God mix tribulations with earthly joys if not so that, feeling tribulation and bitterness, we may learn to desire eternal sweetness? 8. Then let's see what he asks, what he based himself on to say: Hear me soon. What do you ask so that you can instantly be heard? I

you will multiply. Multiplication or increase can be understood in many ways. There is an earthly increase, according to the first blessing of our nature, which we heard when it was said: Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth. Did he who said: Hear me soon want to be multiplied in this way? Still, this multiplication is profitable and comes only from God's blessing. What will I say about other increases? One was increased in gold; another, in silver; the one beyond, in cattle; this one, as a family; that one, in estates, and the other, in all these things. Many are the earthly accretions; However, the best is that of children, although this increase is annoying to avaricious men, since those to whom many children are born fear being impoverished. This care forces many to impiety; so that, forgetting that they are parents, stripped of all affection of humanity, they abandon their own children to take on those of others; They throw away what they gave birth to and gather up what they did not give birth to; they despise the former and love the latter; The former is a mother in vain through the flesh, the latter is more truly a mother through love. Therefore, there being many and many kinds of increases, what increase does he intend who said: Hear me quickly? So he says: You will multiply me. We hope to hear about what things. Hey: in my soul. Not in my flesh, but in my soul: You will multiply me in my soul. Is there anything to add, lest perhaps multiplication in the soul does not always mean happiness? Indeed, men increase in the soul attentively

Audiamus nos, eructet petitionem suam, et videamus quid petat; et discamus per eum petere, ut mereamur accipere. Veneras ad Ecclesiam, nescio quid hodie petiturus. Quid putamus veneras petiturus? Veneras cum desiderio tuo, nescio quo, utinam innocenti, etsi carnali. Sed remove iniquitatem, remove carnalitatem; say quid petas, quid hodie celebres attende. Natalitium sanctae et beatae feminae celebrates, et forte congratulatem terrenam desideras. Illa propter desiderium sanctum dimisit felicitatem quam habebat in terra; dimisit filios flentes et tanquam crudelem matrem dolentes, quia velut perdiderat humanora misericordiam, quae ad divinam festinabat coronam. Nesciebat vero illa quid desideraret, quid calcaret? Imo vero noverat psallere coram Angelis Dei, eorumque desiderare consortium, amicitiam sanctam etpuram, ubi ulterius non moreretur, ubi iudicem nosset apud quem non valere posset mendacium. Quid ergo? in illa vita nulla sunt bona? Imo vero ibi sola sunt bona, non malis mixed bona; securitates in quibus gaudeas quantum vis, et nemo dicat tibi, Tempera te. Hic autem de bonis terrenis gaudere molestan est, et periculosum nimis; ne sic gaudeas ut haereas, et gaudendo male pereas. Nam unde Deus miscet tribulationes gaudiis terrenis, nisi ut tribulationem semientes et amaritudinem, discamus aeternam desiderare dulcedinem? 8. Quid ergo petit, videoamus; quo merit dixerit, Cito exaudí me. Quid enim petis, ut cita exaudiaris? Multiply me. Multis modis mul-

tiplicatio intelligi potest. Est multiplicatio terrenae generationis, secundum primam naturae nostrae benedictionem, quam audivimus: Crescite, et multiplicamini, et implete terram, et dominamini eius (Gen 1:28). Sicne ille volebat multiply, qui dicebat. I quote exaudi me? This plan is to multiply fructuosa est, and it does not come nisi de benedictione Domini. Iam quid dicam of alus multiplicationibus? Multiplicatus is ille auro, ille argento, ille pecore, ille familia, ille possessionibus, ille his Ómnibus. Multae sunt terrenae multiplicationes; felicior autem filiorum: quanquam hominibus avaris etiam ipsa fecunditas molesta est. Time enim ne pauperes relinquantur, qui multi nasci potuerunt. Quae sollicitudo plerosque ad impietatem coegit, ut obliviscerentur quod parentes essent, omnique humanitatis affectu exspoliati, exponent filios suos, ut eos facerent alienos; proiiceret quae peperit, colligeret quae non peperit; illa contemneret, illa diligeret; illa frustrates mater carne, illa verior volúntate. In the soul, where vices multiply, it is seen that this one, only miser, multiplies; that one, only superb; the one beyond, only lustful; This greed, pride and lust increased in his soul, but to his harm. This multiplication is one of poverty, not abundance. Then you who said: Hear me quickly, and who separated yourself from everything corporeal, from every earthly good, from every desire of the world, what do you desire, since you say to God: You will multiply me in my soul? Explain to us what you want. You will multiply me—he says—in my soul with strength or virtue. He has already declared the desire, he has already expressed the desire very clearly, without confusion. If I had simply said: You will multiply me, you would think of I don't know what earthly goods; to avoid this he added in the soul; And so that, furthermore, you do not think that these are vices in the soul, continue: with virtue or strength. There is nothing more excellent that you can desire from God if you want to say with a lifted and sincere head: Hear me quickly. 9 [v.4]. Praise you, Lord, all the kings of the earth. This is how it will be done and this is how it is done, and it is done every day. Therefore it is shown that it was not said in vain, since it was to happen: Let all the kings of the earth praise you, Lord. But when they praise you, when they confess you, do not desire earthly goods from you. For what should the kings of the earth desire? Don't you already have this domain? What more has man to desire on earth when his desire has reached the point of dominion? What more could you want? It needs a more excellent greatness; but perhaps, the more excellent it is, the more dangerous it is. For the vitia. lile tantummodo avarus est, ille tantummodo superbus, Ule tantummodo luxuriosus; iste et avarus, et superbus, et luxuriosus: multiplicatus est in anima sua, sed malo suo. Multiplicatio ista egestatis est, non ubertatis. Ergo quid tu qui dixisti, Cito exaudí me, et te abstulisti ab omni corpore, ab omni terrena re, ab omni desiderio saeculari, ut díceres Deo, Multiplicabis me in anima mea? Adhuc esplana quid desideres. Multiplicabis me, inquit, in anima mea, virtute. Expressum votum, expressum desiderium, ab omni confusione circumcisum. Si diceret, Multiplicabis me; terrena nescio quae cogitares: addidit, in anima mea. Rursus, ne in anima vitia cogitares, addidit, virtute. Nihil est quod amplius a Deo desideres, si vis bona et vera fronte dicere, Cito exaudí me. 9 [v.4]. Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnes reges terrae.

Ita fiet, et ita fit, et quotidie fit; et ostenditur non frustra dictum, nor did it erat futurum. Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnes reges terrae. Sed et ipsi cum tibi confitentur, cum laudant te, non terrena desiderint a te. Quid enim reges terrae desideraturi sunt? Nonne iam habent ipsum imperium? Quidquid amplius desideraverit homo in terra, usque ad imperium est desiderium eius. Quit amplius potest? Altior sublimits necessary est. Be strong as much altior, as much periculosior. Ideoque reges quanto sunt in maiore sublimitate terrena, mucho magis humiliari Deo debent. Utquid

Likewise, the greater the earthly greatness of kings, the more they must humble themselves before God. Why do they do it? Because they heard all the words of your mouth. Oh Lord! all the words of your mouth. I do not know in what other nation the law and the prophets were hidden: All the words of your mouth. Praising this nation, the Apostle says: What is the advantage of fudio or what is the usefulness of circumcision? Great beyond measure. Because first the words of God were entrusted to him. There, then, were the words of God. Present to me Gideon, that holy man who lived in the time of the judges, and see what sign he asked of the Lord: I will put, he says, a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; let the fleece be shaken, and the threshing floor be dry. And so it happened: the fleece became wet, and the threshing floor remained dry. Again he asked for another sign: Let the entire threshing floor be mowed and only the fleece remain dry. And this happened: the threshing floor became wet and the fleece remained dry. First the fleece got wet, leaving the threshing floor dry; Then the threshing floor got wet, leaving the fleece dry. What do you think, brothers, what is the era? Is it not the terrestrial orb? And what is the fleece but the Jewish nation in the middle of the world, having within itself the sacrament of grace, not in plain sight, but in the darkness of the secret, as the rain was found hidden in the fleece? The time will come when the rain will be seen on the threshing floor; then it will be manifested, it will not remain hidden. Then what was said came to pass: Confess, Lord, all the kings of the earth, for they have heard all the words of your mouth. What were you hiding, oh Israel? How long did you hide it? The fleece was squeezed, and water came out of you. Only Christ faciunt? Quoniam audierunt omnia verba oris tuil O Domine, omnia verba oris tui! Nescio in qua gente abscondita weret Lex et Prophetae, omnia verba oris tui. Sed in gente Iudaeorum sola fuent omnia verba oris tui: quam gentem laudans Apostolus ait, Quid ergo amplius est Iudaeo? aut quae utilitas circumcisionis? Multum per omnem modum. Primum quidem, quia credita sunt illis eloquia Dei (Rom 3,1 et 2). Ibi werent verba Dei. Sed da mihi illum Gedeon quemdam sanctum virum tempore Iudicum; videte quale signum petivit a Domino: Ponam, inquit, vellus inarea; compluatur vellus, sicca sit area. Et factum est: complutum est vellus solum, area sicca erat. Petiit iterum signum: Area tota compluta sit, et solum vellus siccum inveniatur. Et hoc factum est: compluta this area, sicco vellere (Iu 6,36-40).

Primo complutum vellus, sicca area; Post compluta area, sicco vellere. Quid vobis videtur area, brothers? Nonne orbis terrarum? Quid vellus? Tanquam gens Iudaea in medio orbe terrarum, habens gratiae sacramentum, non in manifestatione, thirst in cloud secreti, tanquam in velamento pluviam in vellere. Venit tempus quando revealetur pluvia inarea; manifestata est, non operta. Factum est ergo quod dictum est, Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnes reges terrae; quoniam audierunt omnia verba oris tui. Quid est, Israel, quod abscondebas? quamdiu abscondebas? Expressum est vellus, et exiit de te pluvia. Solus Christus suavitas pluviae: ipsum solum non agnoscis in Scripturis,

11 [v.6}. See how he wanted the kings to sing on the roads: humbly carrying the Lord, not being arrogant against the Lord. Because, if they become arrogant, what comes next? That the Lord is exalted and looks at humble things. Do kings want to be looked at? Be humble. But what? If they become arrogant, can they hide themselves from the eyes of God? May it not happen that perhaps because you heard: Look at humble things, you pretend to be proud and say in your soul: "God looks at the humble, he does not look at me; I will do what I want. Who sees me? Man is hidden from man; God does not want to see me because I am not humble, well

He looks at humble things; "I'll do whatever I want." Oh fool! Would you say this if you knew what you should love? Do you say that if God doesn't want to see you, you don't fear Him, because He doesn't want to see you? If you greeted a great lord of yours, and he, distracted by something else, did not look at your face, how you would feel! And if God doesn't look at you, do you think you're safe? He doesn't see you as a savior, but he sees you as a destroyer. Yet God sees you. Do not think that he does not see you, but rather pray that you deserve to be seen by him who sees you, for it was said in Psalm 33: The eyes of the Lord rest on the righteous. Since they do not sit on the unjust, they do what they want. The eyes of the Lord rest on the righteous. Continue the psalm: and your ears are attentive to your prayers. Then the wicked, who think they are safe because the eyes of the Lord do not rest on them, do not they fear because not even the ears of the Lord are attentive to their supplications? Is it not better that his eyes be upon us, and his ears attentive to our prayers? When you do the works on which you do not want the eyes of the Lord to rest, you will not deserve that his ears attend to your prayers; but, nevertheless, when you do evil, you do not take your eyes off the Lord. Well, what follows in the same psalm? The face of the Lord on those who do evil things. So that? To erase his memory from the earth. Do you see how He sees you, do you see how you can't hide from Him? Since you are seen when you work, why don't you do that by which you deserve to please God? What is said here too? I ask only this, I only say this, I only wish to ask this: Do not despise the works of your hands. Divine omniscience and omnipresence
[THE DIVINE OMNISCIENCE AND OMNIPRESENCE] SERMON TO THE PEOPLE

1. I had prepared a short psalm, which I ordered the reader to sing; but at the hour of the hour, it seems, confused, he read one by another. Therefore, I preferred to follow God's will, manifested in the reader's mistake, rather than my own, as was my intention. For the same reason, if I detain you in any way due to the abundance of material, do not impute it to me, but believe that God wanted me to work and not without fruit, since it is not in vain that we receive the penalty of eating bread with the sweat of our face for the first sin. Therefore, if it is bread that the psalm offers us, pay attention. It is bread if it is Christ, for He said: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Let us also look for the bread that the Gospel so evidently offers us in the prophets. This bread is not seen there by those who have a veil placed in their hearts, as your charity heard yesterday. However, we, like the sacrifice of the Lord's cross tore the veil, revealing the secrets of the temple, must, when Christ is preached to us, eat the bread even if it is with work and sweat. 2. Our Lord Jesus Christ speaks in the prophets sometimes in person of our Head, who is the Savior himself, who is seated at the right hand of the Father, who was born for us.

others of the Virgin, and he suffered, as you know, under the power of Pontius Pilate; and, shedding the innocent blood, which is our price, he redeemed sinners from the captivity, in which we were held by the devil, forgiving us our crimes; and furthermore, with the same price that he gave for us, his blood destroyed the document that accredited us as debtors. The Lord himself, our Head, is director, husband and redeemer of the Church. If it is a Head, it has a Body. His Body is the Church, which is also his wife; To her the Apostle says: You are the Body of Christ and members. The total Christ, Head and Body, is like a complete man; and, since woman was made from man and belongs to him, that is why it was said of the first marriage: They will be two in one flesh. Interpreting this as a great mystery, the Apostle says that it was not in vain that this was said about those two men, since Christ and the Church were already prefigured in them. This is how the Apostle explains this: They will be two in one flesh; This mystery is great, but I say in order to Christ and the Church. The Apostle also said that Adam was a figure of the one who was to come. He is—he says—a figure of the future. Therefore, if Adam was a figure of the one who was to come, as the woman was made from the side of the one who slept, so from the side of the Lord who slept, that is, of the one who died in the passion, when he was wounded with the spear while on the cross, the sacraments with which he formed the Church sprang forth. Of his future passion he says thus in another psalm: I fell asleep and took sleep; and I rose, because the Lord sustained me. Then by sleep we understand passion. Eva was formed from the side ad dexteram Patris; qui etiam propter nos natus de virgine, et sub Pontio Pilate, qualia nostis, passus est; fuso innocente sanguine, quod est pretium nostrum, redemit nocentes a captivitate, in qua detinebamur a diabolo, donans nobis delicta, et ipso pretio nostro sanguine suo delens chirographum quo debitores tenebamur (Col 2,13-14). Ipse est rector et sponsus et redemptor Ecclesiae, caput nostrum. Et utique si caput est, habet corpus. Corpus autem eius sancta Ecclesia, quae etiam coniux eius; cui dicit Apostolus, Vos autem estis corpus Christi et membra (1 Cor 12,27). Totus ¡taque Christus caput et corpus, tanquam integer vir: quia et femina de viro facta est, et ad virum pertinet; et dictum est de primo coniugio, Erunt duo in carne una (Gen 2,24).

Hoc autem ad mysterium interpretatur Apostolus non frustra esse dictum de illis duobus hominibus, nisi quia in eis iam figurabatur Christus et Ecclesia. Nam hoc sic exponit Apostolus: Erunt duo in carne, inquit, una: sacramentum hoc magnum est; authentic ego, in Christo et Ecclesia (Eph 5,31 et 32). Dicit etiam ipsum Adam formam futuri: Qui est, inquit, forma futuri (Rom 5,14). If ergo Adam forms futuri; quomodo de latere dormientis Eva facta est (Gen 2,21-22), sic ex latere Domini dormientis, id est, in passione morientis, et in intersection percusso de lancea (lo 19,34), manaverunt Sacramenta, quibus formaretur Ecclesia. Name of future eadem passione sua sic dicit in alio psalmo: Ego dormivi, et som-

of him who slept, and the Church, on the side of him who suffered. Therefore, our Lord Jesus Christ speaks sometimes in the prophets for himself, sometimes on our behalf, because he became one with us; and thus it was said: They shall be two in one flesh. Hence the Lord also said in the Gospel speaking of marriage: Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. They are one flesh because he took the flesh of our mortality; but they are not a divinity, because He is Creator, and we are creatures. Everything that the Lord speaks in person about the taken flesh, either belongs to the Head, who has already ascended to heaven, or to these members, who still suffer in this earthly pilgrimage; for which, finding himself in suffering therein when Saul pursued them, he cried out from heaven, saying, Saul, Saul, why dost thou persecute me? Then let us hear from the Lord Jesus Christ in prophecy. These psalms were sung long before the Lord of Mary was born, but not before the Lord existed, since the Creator of all things existed eternally and was born from the creature in time. Let us believe in his divinity and, as far as we can, understand his equality with the Father. For the divinity equal to the Father participated in our mortality, not according to his own, but according to ours, so that we might share in his divinity, not in ours, which we lacked, but in his. 3 [v.l]. O Lord, you examined me and knew me. Say this our Lord Jesus Christ. May He also call the Father Lord, since the Father is only Lord of Him insofar as He deigned to be nanum cepi; et exsurrexi, quoniam Dominus suscipiet me (Ps 3,6). Ergo dormitio intelligitur passio. Eva de latere dormientis, Ecclesia de latere patientis. Loquitur ergo Dominus noster lesus Christus in Prophetis aliquando ex voce sua, aliquando ex voce nostra, quia unum se facit nobiscum; sicut dictum est, Erunt duo in carne una. Unde dicit et ipse Dominus in Gospel, cum de coniugio loqueretur: Igitur iam non sunt duo, sed una caro (Mt 19,6). Una caro, quia de nostra mortalitate carnem suscepit: non autem una divinitas; Quia Ole Creator, we are creatures. Quidquid igitur Dominus loquitur ex persona susceptae carnis, et ad illud caput pertinet quod iam ascendit in caelum, et ad ista membra quae adhuc in terrena peregrinatione laborant: pro quibus laborantibus membris, cum ea Saulus insequeretur, clamavit de cáelo, Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? (Acts 9,4). Audiamus ergo loquentem Dominum Iesum Christum in prophetia.

Cantati enim sunt ipsi Psalmi longe antequam Dominus de Maria nasceretur, non antequam Dominus esset: semper enim Creator omnium; aliquando autem et natus ex creatura. Divinitatem illam credamus. et quantum possumus, intelligamus aequalem Patri. Sed illa divinitas Patri aequalis, facta est particeps nostrae mortalitatis, non de suo, sed de nostro; ut et nos efficeremur participates divinitatis eius, non de nostro, sed de ipsius. 3 [v.l]. cer according to the flesh. The Father is Father of God, and Lord of man. Do you want to know who the Father has equal? To his Son. The Apostle says of the Son: Who, having the form of God, did not consider it a shame to be equal with God. The Father is God as to this form or essence; and equal to his form he has his only begotten Son, begotten of his substance. What does the Apostle say about him trying to restore us and make us participants in his divinity once renewed in order to eternal life, since, as I said, he became a participant in our mortality? That he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, and that he was made in the likeness of men, and that he was found in habit as a man. As for the form he had as God, he was equal to the Father; but he took the form of a servant, by which he is less than the Father. Hence in the Gospel He says both things of himself: I and the Father are one; and also: The Father is greater than me. I and the Father are one he affirmed regarding the form of God. The Father is greater than me said so regarding the form of a servant. Therefore, as He is Father and Lord: Father in the form of God, and Lord in the form of a servant, let Jesus Christ also say, and let us not marvel or be scandalized, since the only begotten Son of God says it: Lord, you tested me and knew me. You examined and knew; not because he was ignorant, but because he made others known. “You examined me,” he says, “and you knew me. 4 f/v.2] You knew my sitting and my rising. What does this session and this uprising mean? He who sits

humiliates. Then the Lord sat in the passion and rose in the resurrection. You, he says, knew this; that is, you wanted it, you approved it; according to your will it was carried out. If you want to take the voice of the Head here representing the Body, let us also say: You knew my session and my rising. Man sits down when he humbles himself by repenting, but he rises, once his sins are forgiven, when he rises in hope to eternal life. That is why it is also said in another psalm: Rise after you sit down, you who eat the bread of sorrow. The penitents who sing in another psalm eat the bread of sorrow: My tears have been my bread day and night. So what does it mean: Get up after sitting down? Do not exalt yourself if you have not first humbled yourself. Many try to get up before sitting down; They want to appear righteous before having confessed sinners. Therefore if you take it as said by our Head: You knew my session and my rising, understand it as if He had said: "You knew my passion and my resurrection." If you take it as recorded on behalf of his Body, understand it as if he had said: "Before you I will confess my sins and by your grace I was justified." 5 [v.3]. You understood my thoughts from afar, you investigated my path and my destination and you foreseen all my paths. What does far away mean? While I was still on the pilgrimage, before arriving at home, you knew my thoughts. What is my path? The one I walked through. What is my term? The one where I arrived. You found out my path and my end. My distant term was not distant in your eyes. I moved away a lot, but you were there. You found out my path and my end. 6 [v.4}. And you foreseen all my paths. He didn't say "you saw", but you foresaw. Before walking them, before walking, you provided for them, and you allowed me to carry them out in tasks so that, if I did not want to suffer, I would return to your ways. Because there is no fraud in my tongue. Why did he say this? Because behold, I confess to you that I walked my path away from you; I turned away from you, with whom it was good for me, and my own good was evil to me without you. But, if I had done well without you, perhaps I would not have wanted to return to you. Behold, Lord, you knew all things last and things ancient. You knew my last things when I fed swine, you knew my old things when I received from you the part of my inheritance. The ancient is the sin that commits prehensus fugitivus, sequente se vindicta legitima Dei, vindicantis in affectiones nostras, quacumque ierimus et quocumque progressi fuerimus; tanquam ergo deprehensus fugitivus loquitur: Semitam meam, et limitem meum investigasti. 8 [v.6]. Your knowledge was exalted, claiming me; It grew stronger, and I won't be able to get close to it. This is a bit dark; but it will be understood with great pleasure; listen carefully. The holy servant of God Moses, with whom God spoke through the cloud, since, speaking temporally, he spoke with his servant using a creature, that is, not by its substance, but by using

of some corporeal creature through which he formed the voices that hurt mortal and human ears (he knew this way of speaking about God). For that is how God spoke then, not how he speaks in his substance. How does it speak in its substance? The speech of God is the Word of God, and the Word is Christ. This Word does not sound nor pass away, but immutably remains the Word, by which all things were made. To this Word, since it is the Wisdom of God, it is said: You will change all things and they will be changed, but you are always the same; and in another place, speaking the Scripture of Wisdom, it says: Remaining in itself, it renews all things. Therefore, Wisdom subsisting, if it must be said subsisting, since it is said taking into account immutability, not immobility, and always being found in the same way, without varying place or time, since nowhere is it found in one way here and in another there, in no place is it found in one way now and in another before, it is the speech of God. The nonsense that was done to Moses was done to a man through syllables, through sounds that passed. These things would not have been done if God had not used a creature, through whom he would emit speech and voices in this way. The holy Moses knew that this locution of God was made through some corporeal creatures, and that is why he desired and longed to see the face of God; And speaking to him, he said, If I have found favor with you, show me yourself.
