Moyses sanctus Dei famulus, cum quo loquebatur Deus per cloudm, quia temporaliter loquens utique per assumptam creaturam loquebatur servo suo; id est, non per substantiam

suam, sed per assumptam aliquam corporalem creaturam, per quam voices illae ieront, et humanis atque mortalibus auribus personarent (Sic enim loquebatur tune Deus, non quomodo loquitur in substantia sua). Quomodo enim loquitur in substantia sua? Locutio Dei, Verbum Dei est; Verbum Dei Christus est: Verbum illud non sonat et transit, sed semper incommutabiliter manet Verbum, per quod facta sunt omnia (lo 1,3). Cui Verbo dícitur (ipsa est enim et Sapientia Dei); Mutabis ea, et mutabuntur; tu autem idem ipse is (Ps 101,27-28): et alio loco de Sapientia cum Scriptura diceret: In seipsa manens, ait, innovat omnia (Wis 7,27). Illa ergo Sapientia stans (si dici debent vel stans: dicitur autem propter incommutabilitatem, non propter immobilitatem) et eodemmo se semper habens, nullo loco, nullo tempore variata, nusquam aliter quam hic aut ibi, nunquam aliter quam nunc aut antea, ipsa est locutio Dei. Locutio vero illa quae fiebat ad Moysen, ad hominem fiebat per syllabas, per passeúntes sonos. Non autem ieront ista, nisi Deus assumeret talem creaturam, per quam huiusmodi sermonem et voices emitteret): Moyses sanctus noverat istam locutionem Dei assumptis quibusdam corpoteis creaturis fieri; et desideravit et concupivit videre ipsam speciem Dei, et loquenti secum Deo dixit: Si inveni gratiam ante te, ostende mihi temetipsum. Cum hoc vehementer concupisceret, et hoc quadam, si dicendum est, amica familiaritate, qua ipse dignitus est, extorquere vellet Deo, ut videret eius maiestatem et faciem, quomodo dici

that he deigned to speak to him, he would like to force God, in order to see his face and majesty, if it can be said that God has a face. Then God answers him: You cannot see my face, because no one sees my face and lives afterward. But I will place you in the stone cave, and I will pass by, and I will place my hand before you, and as you pass by you will see my back. From these words another enigma originates, that is, a certain hidden symbolism of things. As you pass by, you will see my back, says God, as if I had a face on one side and a back on the other. Far be it from us to think anything similar about that majesty. For whoever thinks this about God, what does it profit him if the temples of the pagans are closed? He already creates an idol in his heart. Then great mysteries are contained in these words. The Lord spoke, as I said, through a creature, as he wanted to speak to his servant. On this occasion the person of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ himself is already perceived. Which, considering the form of God, by which he is equal to the Father, is equally invisible to human eyes as the Father. If human wisdom cannot be seen with human eyes, can the Virtue and Wisdom of God be seen with the eyes of the flesh? But since it was Lord who had to take the flesh in due time so that it would also appear, when it was necessary for it to appear, to the carnal eyes in order to heal the health of the mind internally, predicting this, he figuratively says to Moses: You cannot see my face; You will see my back, but when it passes. However, so that you may not see my face, I will put my hand in front of you. What was the passing of the potest facies Dei; ait illi: Non potes videre faciem meam: nemo enim vidit faciem meam, et vixit. Sed ponam te in spelunca petrae, et transibo, et ponam super te manum meam; cum autem transiero, posteriora mea videbis (Ex 33,9-23). Mister? What the evangelist says: The hour having come, Jesus passes from this world to the Father. This step or transit is expressed by the word Pascha. What in Hebrew is called Pascha, in Latin is called Transitus. What does it mean: You will not see my face, but you will see my back? Who was Moses personifying when he was told: You will not see my face, but: You will see my back, and this when I pass; but, that you may not see my face, shall I put my hand before you? He called his face to his principles, and in a way his back, to the transit of this world through his passion. He manifested himself to the Jews; They didn't know him. Moses personified them when he was told: You cannot see my face. Why didn't they see God presented in the flesh? Because they felt the weight of the Lord's hand on them. Isaiah said of them: (God) dulls the hearts of this people and dims their eyes. It is also their voice that is heard in another psalm: I felt the weight of your hand on me. So that they would not then know the divinity of Christ, since, if they had known it, they would never have crucified the Lord of glory, and if they had not crucified him he would not have redeemed the earthly world with his blood, what did God do? What the Apostle says: (hide) the sublimity of the riches, wisdom and science of God where he exclaims: Oh depth of the riches of the wisdom and science of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments and his ways searchable! Who knew the mind of the Lord? Or who was his advisor? Or who gave it first and will repayment be given? For from Him, and through Him, and in Him are all things; to Him the itum significat Pascha. Quod enim Hebrew verb dicitur Pascha, Latin Transitus interpretatur. Quid est, Faciem meam non videbis, sed posteriora mea videbis? Cuius personam gerebat Ule Moyses, quando ei dictum est, Faciem meam non videbis, sed posteriora mea videbis, et hoc cum transiero: xA autem non videas faciem meam, ponam super te manum meam? Faciem suam dixit, prima sua? et quodammo posteriora sua, transitum de hoc mundo passionis suae. Apparuit Iudaeís; non eum cognoverunt. Eorum personam gerebat Moyses, quando ei dicebatur, Faciem meam non potes videre. Unde autem non viderunt Deum in carne positum? Quia gravata erat super eos manus Domini. De illis enim dixerat Isaiah, Incrassa cor populi huius, et oculos eius grave (Is 4:10): et eorum vox est in alio psalmo, Quoniamgravata est super me manus tua (Ps 31:4).

Ut ergo non cognoscerent tune divinitatem Christi (yes enim cognovissent, nunquam Dominum gloriae crucifixissent [1 Cor 2:8] non crucifixo autem Domino, sanguis illius non redimeret orbem terrarum), quid egit Deus, nisi quod ait Apostolus, altitudinem divitiarum sapientiae et scientiae Dei, ubi exclamat: O altitudo divitiarum sapientiae et scientiae Dei! quam incomprehensibilia sunt iudicia eius, et investigabiles viae eius! Quis enim cognovit sensum Domini? aut quis consiliarius eius Fuit? Aut quis prior dedit illi, et retribuetur ei? Quoniam ex ipso, et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia; ipsi gloria in saecula saecularum.

glory forever and ever. The Apostle says this because he had previously said: Blindness partly came to Israel until the fullness of the nations came in, and thus all Israel was saved. After having dealt with his disciples for forty days, he ascended to heaven; And, on the fiftieth day, on the day of Pentecost, he sent his holy Spirit to them, and, filled with the Holy Spirit, those who had been born in one and had learned one began to speak the languages ​​of all nations. Faced with such a stupendous miracle, thousands of those who crucified the Lord feared and trembled. Distressed by such a great miracle, after Christ was announced to them, seeing that ignorant men spoke the languages ​​of everyone, they asked the apostles for advice on what they should do. When the apostle Saint Peter announced to them Christ, whom they despised on the cross and whom they mocked as a mortal man, whom they reviled because he did not come down from the cross, even though it was a greater wonder to rise from the tomb than to come down from the light, they said, having announced Christ: What shall we do? Those who were cruel in Christ, Apostolus hoc dicit; quia superius dixerat: Caecitas ex parte Israel jacta est, ut plenitudo Gentium intraret, et sic omnis Israel salvus ièret (Rom 11,33-36.25-26). I will not be able to approach her for myself, since, when I can, I will not be able to do so except for you. 10 [v.7]. See that you find the fugitive in the distance, who cannot be hidden from the sight of the one who ran away. And where will he go of whom the term is known? Hear what he says: Where will he go from your Spirit? The Spirit of the Lord fills the entire earth. Who can flee in the world from that Spirit with which the world is full? Where shall I go far from your Spirit and where shall I flee from your face? Find a place to flee from the wrath of God. What place should receive him who flees from God? The men who receive the fugitives ask them where they have fled from. And, when they see that he is a servant of a less powerful lord, they receive him without any fear, saying in their hearts: "This man does not have a lord who can keep track of him." However, when they hear that it belongs to a powerful lord, they either do not receive him or they receive him with great fear, and they do this because the powerful man can be deceived. But where is God not? Who can deceive you? Who don't you know? From what place does God not bring back his fugitive? Then where will this fugitive from the presence of God flee to? That's why he turns from one side to the other as if looking for a place to flee to. 11 [v.8]. “If I go up to heaven,” he says, “there you are; If I go down to hell, you are present. At last you have learned, oh perverse fugitive!, that in no way can you separate yourself from the one who interests you. Mirificata est scientia tua ex me: invaluit; non patero ad Mam: sed subaudis, ex me. Non potero ad Mam ex me. Cum ergo potero, non potero nisi ex te. 10 [v.7]. Ecce invenís in longinquo fugitivum non latere oculos eius a quo fugit. Et quo iturus est iam, cuius limes est investigatus? Videte quid dicit: Quo ibo a Spiritu tuo? Spiritus enim Domini replevit orbem terrarum (Wis 1,7): quis potest fugere in mundo ab illo Spiritu, que plenus est mundus? What was it like to Spiritu tuo? et quo a facie tua fugiam? Locum quaerit quo fugiat ab ira Dei. What is locus recepturus fugitivum Dei? Homines qui suspiciunt fugitives, quaerunt ab eis, a quo fugerint; et quem servum invenerint alicuius domini minus potentis, tanquam sine ullo timore suscipiunt, dicentes in corde suo: Non habet iste talem dominum a quo possit investigan. Cum autem audierint dominum potentem, aut non suscipiunt, aut cum magno timore suscipiunt: quia et homo potens falli potest.

Ubi non est Deus? quis fallit Deum? quem non videt Deus? a quo fugitivum suum non repetit Deus? Quo ergo ibit fugitivus iste a facie Dei? 13 [v.10]. See who leads us. The same one from whose angry face we try to flee. So what's next? If I go down to hell, you are present there. If I took my wings back to the right. If I drink again, he says; then he had lost them. If I take my wings again to the right, I will dwell at the ends of the sea, for there your hand will guide me and your right hand will support me. Let us meditate on this, dear brothers; our hope be our comfort. Let us take back, for love, the wings that we had lost through greed. Greed became a league of our wings; she deprived us of the freedom to fly, that is, of those auras of freedom of the Spirit of God. Hence, nullified, we lost our wings and in a sense fell captive into the power of the hunters. Hence He from whom we fled when caught redeemed us with His blood. He strengthens us the wings of his precepts, and thus we spread them without the league. Let us not love the sea, but let us fly to the ends of the sea. No one trembles, but no one boasts of his wings; because, even finding-

us with our wings, if He does not extend, if He does not lead, we will rush into the sea tired and fatigued for having boasted of our strength. It is necessary that we have wings; and it is also important that He leads us, since He is our helper. We have free will, but with the same free will, what can we do if the one in charge doesn't help us? For there your hand will lead me and your right hand will support me. 14 [v. l l ]. Finding myself in this life among so many scandals, among so many sins, among so many daily temptations, daily perverse suggestions, what do I do, he says? How will I reach the ends of the sea? Calling me he separated me from death, which illuminated the night for me. Well, night is the time that passes while life passes. But how did the night light up? Christ going down into the night. Christ took the flesh of this world, and thus illuminated the night for us. The woman who lost the drachma lit the lamp. The Wisdom of God had lost the drachma. What is the drachma? The coin on which the image of our Emperor is sculpted, since man was made in the image of God and perished. What did the wise woman do? He turned on the lamp. The lamp is made of clay, but it has light, with which the drachma is found. Therefore the lamp of Wisdom, the flesh of Christ, is made of clay; but, shining with his Word, he found the lost. The night (is) light in my delights. The night became delights for me. Our delights are Christ. See how we now rejoice in Him. These acclamations of yours, these joys of yours, from what do they come but from delights? And where do these delights come from if not because the night was illuminated, because Christ was preached to us? For he sought you before you sought him, and he found you so that you might find him. The night {is) light in my delights. 15 [v.12}. For the darkness will not be obscured by you. Do not darken your darkness, for God does not darken it, but rather illuminates it, because it was said to Him in another psalm: You, Lord, will illuminate my lamp; Oh my God, you will illuminate my darkness. Who darkens their darkness that God does not darken? The bad men, the perverted men

you are By sinning they become darkness, and by not confessing the sins they committed, but also defending them, they darken their darkness. Therefore if you sinned, you are darkness. By confessing your darkness, you will deserve that it be illuminated; By defending them, you will make them denser. And when will you come out of the double darkness, you who find yourself in trouble in the simple darkness? How does the Lord not darken your darkness? Because he does not allow our sins to go unpunished, because he punishes us in this misfortune and teaches us. You know, brothers, that all this misery of the human race in which the world groans is medicinal suffering, but not a criminal sentence. You see that pain, fear, destitution and suffering are everywhere. Greed grows, but in the bad. If God delivers us here from such punishments, so that our darkness may not be darkened, let us recognize that we are under the correctional penalty and let us bless God, who mixes the bitterness with the sweetness of temporal life so that we may not be blinded by the delight of the delights of the present life, and, therefore, we may not desire eternal delights nor seek to cross the entire sea and dwell in its confines. Let the waves of the sea become angry; The more they become angry, the more the dove stays in the air with its wings. Therefore God does not darken our darkness because He inflicts punishment on our sins and bitterness on our depraved sweetness. Let us not darken ourselves defending our sins, and the night (will be) light in our delights. For the darkness will not be darkened by you.

tívum, qui terga mea flagelli plague percussit, qui me vocando, ab interitu revocavit, qui fecit mihi illuminatam noctem. Nox est enim quamdiu ista vita agitur. How is this illuminated night? They deny the confession due to conceit, and then what was written is fulfilled in these dead: The confession or praise of the dead perishes as if it did not exist. And thus they will receive their cities in vain, that is, their vain peoples, who follow their vanity, since, puffed up with the name of justice, they induce the blind and the ignorant to follow them, as if they were the righteous, once the bond of unity is broken. And as many times, by censuring the wicked, with whom they pretend to have no part, they take the opportunity to separate themselves from the unity of Christ; and, furthermore, as it usually happens that they not only defame the innocent, from whom they pretend to flee as evil, but also extol true and right things about some evil people similar to themselves, among whom the wheat of Christ groans, preserving the bond of unity; That is why he interposed the following paragraph: Bloody men, depart from me, because you will say in thought: "They will receive their cities in vain", that is, they will drag their people to their own separation, corrupting them with their vanity, because you will say in thought: Bloody men, depart from me. So that, like sinners killed in the spirit, they will receive their cities, that is, their people, in vanity; that is, by separating them, transfer them to the vanity of error; and, as if offended by the mixing of the chaff, they abandon the wheat, breaking the unity; because he advises the wheat itself, that is, the faithful good, that before the fork, which is to take place in the last time, they should not openly separate themselves from the bad, so that it does not happen that they abandon the good even mixed with the bad, but rather, through good treatment and the dissimulation of life, in a certain way. tores, quia obscurati intelligentia alienantur a vita Dei (Eph 4,18) vanos, eorum vanitatem sedatives; cum inflati iustitiae nomine persuadent ut disrupto unitatis bond, eos tanquam iustiores caecí et imperití sequantur.

Does the Spirit of God speak with us? How does he offer us his delights on this night of life? What is this, I ask you, brothers? How is it that these things are so much sweeter the darker they are? God prepares us in an admirable way a medicine for his love. He magnifies his words in such a way that, when exposing things, which you already knew; As they sprang from passages that seemed obscure to you, new knowledge was generated, so to speak. Did you not already know, brothers, that in the Church of God the wicked must be tolerated and schisms must not be caused? Did you not already know that within that net that captured good and bad fish they must be dragged patiently to the beach, and the net must not break, since on the beach the good ones must be separated, thrown into the basket, and the bad ones thrown away? You already knew all these things; However, you did not understand the verses of this psalm; but what you did not understand was exposed, and so what you knew was renewed and refreshed.

Only those who do not know how to err will count on separation. And who is the one who does not know how to err? The one who does not place the bad on the right nor the good on the left. It is difficult for us to know ourselves in this life; Therefore, how much less should we utter a hasty opinion! Because, if we know the bad guy today, we don't know what he will be tomorrow, and perhaps the one we hate passionately is our brother and we don't know him. However, we surely hate the malice in the wicked and we love the creature. Let us love what God did in them and hate what man did in himself. What did man do? Thus you will put to death what man made, saving what God made. 3 [v.l]. Finally, a psalm for David. Do not set your sights on any other end than that which the Apostle presented to you, for he says: The end of the law is Christ in order to bring about justice for every believer. Then when you hear the psalm say: For the end, let hearts turn to Christ, since the title of the psalm is the proclamation of the psalm, it is like the one who announces and says: "Behold, He is coming"; For the same reason, I have to speak, I have to sing about Christ. I also understand the words for David only from Him who was made from the lineage of David according to the flesh. Because of the lineage, the name suits him. By carnal nature it comes from David, by spiritual nature it is before David; and not only before David, but before Abraham; and not only before Abraham, but before Adam; and not only before Adam, but before heaven and earth, before all the angels, before all powers and virtues, before all things visible and invisible. Because? For in order to exist these, all things were made by Him, and without Him nothing was made. Then, since he came from the lineage of David, not according to divinity, through which he was the Creator of David himself, but according to the flesh, he deigned to be called prophetically David, look at the end, because the psalm is sung for David; and he also hears the voice of his Body and remains in it. Let your voice be the voice you heard and pray and say what follows. 4 [v.2]. Deliver me, Lord, from the evil man. Not of one, but of this entire lineage; not only of his henchmen, but of his prince.

Becoming light, but not in ourselves, but in the Lord, let us pray not only to be on guard against darkness, that is, against sinners that the devil still possesses, but also against his own prince, the devil, who works in the children of unbelief. Deliver me from the unrighteous man. It is the same to deliver me from the evil man as from the unrighteous man. He was called evil because he is unjust, lest you perhaps think that some unjust person is good. For there are many unjust people who seem innocent, they do not appear cruel or harsh, they do not persecute or oppress men; but, nevertheless, they are unjust, because, on the other hand, they are lustful, drunk, given over to the pleasures of the flesh. And how is it that they do no harm to anyone, if they do not forgive themselves? He who does not harm is innocent, but he who harms himself is not. And how can it not but harm you?

fights? That things aroused in me that I had to continually fight against. From these hearts springs everything that the Christian fights against. They sharpened their tongues like snakes. If you examine the man, see the similarity. In the snake there is maximum cunning and the concealment of harm; For the same reason, it drags. He lacks feet so that, when he approaches, his steps cannot be heard. In his walk, the glide is smooth, but not straight. Therefore, they crawl and crawl to harm, inoculating the hidden poison under gentle contact. That is why he goes on to say: (They have) asp poison under their lips. He says that it is under his lips so that we realize that it is one thing to be under his lips and another on his lips. These he declares completely openly in another place where he says: Those who speak peace with their neighbors, but hide evil in their hearts. 7 [v.5]. Protect me. Lord, from the hand of the sinner, deliver me from unjust men. These are the same ones he previously talked about; They are known. Here there is no need to understand, but to act; It is necessary to pray, not ask who they are. He then tells you how you should pray against this kind of homquae pugnarem tota die mihi constituebant. Inde enim hoc nascitur de talibus cordibus, quidquid est contra quod pugnat christianus. Si seditio, si schisma, si haeresis, si contradictio turbulenta, non hoc erumpit nisi de illis cogitationibus quae tegebantur: et quando labia bona loquebantur, tota die constituebant bella. Pacata audis verba; sed belli constitutio a cordibus non discedit. Quod enim dictum est, tota die, Sine intermissione significat, id est, toto tempore. 6 [v.4]. Acuerunt linguas suas sicut serpentes. Si adhuc quaeris hominem, aspice similarityinem. In serpente maxime astutia est et dolus nocendi; propterea etiam serpit. Non enim vel pedes habet, ut eius vestigia cum venit audiantur. In eius itinere velut lenis est tractus, sed non est rectus. Ita ergo repunt et serpunt ad nocendum, habentes occultum venenum et sub leni contactu.

Et ideo sequitur: Venenum aspidum sub labiis eorum. Ecce est illud sub labiis; ut aliud sub labiis, aliud in labiis advertamus. Quos etiam aperte manifestat alio loco, ubi dicít, Qui loquuntur pacem cum cerca suo; mala autem in cordibus suis (Ps 27,3). 7 [v.5]. Preserve me, "Domine, de manu peccatoris; ab hominibus iniustis erue me. Ipsi sunt, noti sunt: non hic opus est intelligere, sed agere; orare opus est, non quaerere qui sint. Sed quomodo ores adversus huiusmodi nomines, aperit tibi in consequenti. Multi enim adversus malo imperite orant. Qui cogitaverunt, inquit, supplantare gressus meos.

brethren, for many pray foolishly against the wicked. Those who thought of tripping my feet: this can still be understood carnally. For example, a man has an enemy who engages in trade with him; In the business he plans to commit fraud, take money from him. Another has a neighboring enemy, and he plans to cause harm to his house by reducing his inheritance. Without a doubt, he thinks it maliciously, he does it fraudulently; employs, to accomplish these things, diabolical machinations; no one doubts it. However, these should not be avoided because of these actions, but rather because they insidiously drag you into doing what they do, that is, separating you from the Body of Christ and making you into their own. For just as the Head of the good is Christ, so the devil is the Head of the bad. Those who thought to trip me up. What does it mean to trip my feet? Not exactly that you lose in the business you have with him and that he deceives you in the common cause that you have pending in court with him. He will throw a trip at your feet if he hinders you in the path of God, so that the right thing you were trying to do will waver, deviate from the path, fall into it, retreat, remain static in it, or turn your back and head back to the place from which you started. Anything they do to you is deceiving you and tripping you up. Pray against such individuals so that you do not lose the heavenly patrimony, so that you do not lose Christ as co-heir, because you must live eternally with the One who made you heir. He did not make you an heir to succeed him when he died, but so that you would live eternally with Him. 8 [v.6]. The proud ones hid a trap for me. When he said the proud, he briefly explained everything that constitutes the body Adhuc potest carnalíter accipi. Habet quisque inimicum; in negotio cogita! ei fraudm faceré, et ei auferre pecuniam, qui versatur in communi negotio: habet quisque inimicum vicinum, et cogitat malum ingerere domui eius, aliquid de re ipsius minuere; et utique dolo cogitat, fraud cogitat, machinamentis diaboli haec ipsa gestit implere; nemo doubt. Sed tamen non propter ista isti cavendi sunt, sed ne insidiando tibi adducant te ad se; Id est, a corpore Christi separent te, et faciant de corpore suo. Sicut enim bonorum caput Christus est, sic illorum caput diabolus. Qui cogitaverunt, inquit, supplantare gressus meos. Quid est, supplantare gressus meos?

Non quasi ut erres in negotio quod cum illo habes, et decipiat te in causa quae tibi communis est in foro cum illo. Supplantavit gressus tuos, si te impedierit in via Dei, ut illud quod rectum intendebas, titubet, aut labatur a via, aut cadat in via, aut recedat de via, aut remaneat in via, aut retro revertatur unde venerat. Quidquid tibi tale fecerit, supplantavit te, decepit te. Contra huiusmodi insidias ora, ne perdas caeleste patrimonum, ne amittas Christum cohaeredem, quia victurus es in aeternum cum eo qui te fecit haeredem. Non enim talis te fecit haeredem, cui mortuo succedas, sed cum quo in aeternum vivas. 8 [v.6]. Absconderunt superbi muscipulam tnihi. Totum corpus diaboli explicavit breviter, cum ait, superbi. Inde est quod et iustos plerum
Prayer against cursing enemies

of the devil Hence it is that those who are wicked are often called righteous. From this it follows that nothing is as harmful to them as confessing sins. These are those who, being falsely righteous, necessarily envy the truly righteous. No one envies another in what they do not want to appear or be. Does anyone envy you because you are rich? Or he envies you because he wants to be one, or because he longs to be considered one. Does another envy you because you are illustrious and noble? or pretends to be one or wants to be considered such. The same must be said of all things that appear good in this world and are reputed to be such. What each person wants to have and what they long to excel in, they envy you, because they perceive the fame of it. These falsely righteous people want to appear to be so without being so, and it is necessary that they envy those whom they see as truly righteous and try to do with him whatever is in their power so that he loses what he acquired glory for. From here come all the insidiousness and betrayals. This was first intended by the devil, who, fallen, envied the man, who was standing. For since he lost the kingdom of heaven, he did not want man to reach it, nor does he want it, and that is why he now strives so that man does not obtain the place from which he was thrown. Therefore, since he is proud, and, therefore, envious, his whole body being arrogant, it is the body of envious people. Let us pray against him, which cannot be corrected, but in favor of those who can; so that we say to the unjust man: Why do you envy the just, O unjust man? Why do you want to be considered righteous? Do quickly what is good, and you will do it more easily and quickly than you think. Be fair; so amaque se dicunt, cum sint iniqui. Inde est quod nihil illis tam noxium est, quam confiten peccata. Ipsi sunt qui cum sint falsi iusti, necesse est ut invideant veris iustis. Nemo enim invidet alteri in eo quod non vult vel esse vel videri. Alius tibi invidet, quia dives es; aut dives vult esse ut tibi invideat, aut putari vult dives: alius tibi invidet, quia clarus es et nobilis; aut hoc esse affectat, aut hoc se putari cupit. Et sic omnia quae videntur bona in hoc saeculo et putantur; quod quisque vult habere, et in quo vult excellere, vel cuius rei famem tumbat, in eo tibi invidet. Isti autem qui falsi iusti sunt, videri volunt iusti, cum non sint; et necesse est ut quem viderint verum iustum, invideant illi, et hoc cum illo agant, quomodo amittat unde gloriatur.

Inde veniunt omnes seductiones et supplantationes. Hoc prior ipse diabolus voluit, qui cadens stanti homini invidit: et quia ipse amisit regnum caelorum, hominem illuc pervenire noluit (Gen 3), et non vult; et id agit nunc, ut homo illuc non perveniat, unde ipse deiectus est. Quia ergo superbus est ipse, et ideo invidus quia superbus, omne corpus ipsius talium corpus est. Sed nos oremus contra illum, qui corrigi non potest, et pro ipsis qui possunt, ut dicamus homini iniusto: Quare invides iusto, o homo iniuste? Quia vis videri iustus? I quote fac quod melius est, et facilius eris quod vis videri. Esto iustus: ita diliges cui invidebas; quia quod illum doles esse, eris et tu, et amabis in eo te, et ipsum in te. Etenim si invideres diviti,

You will be the one you envied, because what you grieve about being him, you will be, and you will love yourself in him and him in you. If you envy the rich, it will not be in your power to be rich; If you envy some honest and noble senator, it will not be within your reach to be noble and enlightened either; If you envy the beautiful, you will never become beautiful; If you envy the strong and robust, you will never give yourself strength; If you envy the just, it is in your desire to be so; I know that what you are grieving about is another, because you should not buy what you are not and is another; It is obtained for free, it is obtained instantly: Peace on earth to men of good will. 9. But the proud hid the trap, they tried to trip my feet. And what did they do? They stretched ropes like snares to my feet. What ropes? This word restis is known in Holy Scripture and elsewhere we find what it means. The Lord made a whip of cords, with which he drove out of the temple those who traffic in it; and he indicated to us how we should understand the word restis, since it says in another place: Each one is chained with the bonds of his sins; and more clearly Isaiah says: Woe to those who drag sins like a rope or long rope! Why do you say maroma? For every sinner who perseveres in his sins adds sins to sins; and, when he should be corrected by the confession of his sin, he doubles down by defending what he could destroy by confession; and so many times he wants to defend himself from sins committed with other sins. He committed, for example, adultery; In order not to be killed, he prepares murder; add sin to sin. If he committed murder, he who feared for one crime now fears for two; non esset in potestate tua ut dives esses; si invideres honest alicui senatori nobili, non esset in potestate tua ut nobilis tu esses et clarus; si invideres pulchro, nunquam te pulchrum faceres; si invideres forti et valido, nunquam tibi vires dares: si invides iusto, res in volúntate est; this quod doles esse alterum. Non enim empturus es quod tu non es et alius est; gratis constat, I quote constat: Pax in terra hominibus bonae voluntatis (Luke 2:14). 9. lili autem superbi absconderunt muscipulam: quaesierunt supplantare gressus meos. Et quid fecerunt? Et restes extensount pedibus muscles tneis. What remains? Notum est hoc verbum in Scripturis, et invenimus alibi quid significant restes.

Dominus flagellum de resticulis fecit, unde expulit eos de temple, qui ibi male versabantur (lo 2,15); et significavit nobis quomodo intelligamus restes: quia: Criniculis peccatorum suorum unusquisque constringitur (Prov 5,22), dicit alia Scriptura; et apart Isaiah, Vae iis qui trahunt peccata sicut restem longam! (Is 5:18). Quare autem dicitur restis? Quia omnis peccator perseverans in peccatis suis, addit peccata peccatis, et cum debenet aecusatione peccati sui corrigi, defensione duplicat quod confessione posset auferri, et plerumque alíis peccatis vult munitus esse propter illa quae commisit. Fecit adulterium, et ne occidatur, parat homicidium; addit peccato peccatum. Rursum si ei contigerit faceré homicidium, iam qui unum crime timebat

and, seeing that he now fears more than he feared before, he does not think of diminishing what he has done, but of adding what he has not yet done; maybe he tries the curse. See that it already has three. Who will think of more? Who will end the string or rope of sins? It is rightly called rope or rope, because the sin is added by twisting the rope, that is, they are not added in straight strands, but twisted. Perversity, when it gets stuck, extends itself lengthwise and does not intend to cut what it has poorly woven, but rather to add, stretch, extend lengthwise, so that at last it finds something with which it can bind its feet and hands and is thrown into the outer darkness. These sins of the wicked serve as a snare for the righteous when they incite them to commit the evils that they themselves commit. That is why he said: They laid ropes like snares at my feet, that is, with their sins they wanted to throw me to the ground. And where? Next to the road they placed the stumbling block for me. Not on the road, but along the road. Your ways are the precepts of God. The wicked put stumbling blocks by the roads; Do not stray from the path and you will not fall into traps. Do not say: "God would have forbidden them to place stumbling blocks along the way, and so they would not have placed them." Furthermore, God allowed them to put stumbling blocks along the paths so that you would not depart from them. Next to the roads they placed scandals, or tripezos, on me. 10 [v.7]. What remains? What remedy is there among so many evils in these temptations, in these dangers? I said to the Lord: "You are my God." They are men, but not mine; You are God, and also mine. I said to the Lord: "You are my God." Sublime voice of duet timet: et utique cum videat se plura timere, quam antea timebat, non cogitat minuere quod fecit, sed addere quod nondum fecit; quaerit forte et maleficium. Tria ecce habet. Inde iam quis cogitet? quis finiat restem peccatorum? Et optimale dicitur restis: ut enim torqueatur restis, additur; et non adduntur straight row, sed cake. Pravitas sibi connexa ducitur in longum, et non cogitat praecidere quod male texuit; sed addere, prodúcete, in longum protendere: ut habeat in fine unde illi ligentur manus et pedes, et proiiciatur in exterior darkness (Mt 22,13). Haec autem peccata sua tendunt iustis, quando eis suadent faceré mala quae ipsi faciunt. Ideo dixit, Restes extensount muscipulas pedibus meis; id est, de peccatis suis me deicere voluerunt. Et ubi hoc? Iuxta semitas scandalum posuerunt mibi: non in semitis, sed iuxta semitas.

Semitae tuae, ptaecepta Dei sunt. lili scandala iuxta semitas posuerunt; tu, noli recedere a semitis, et non irrues in scandala. Nec volódicas: Et prohiberet illos Deus will put mihi scandala iuxta semitas, et non ibi dondetent. Imo permisit Deus will put scandala illos iuxta semitas, et tu non recedas a semitis. Iuxta semitas scandala posuerunt mibi. 10 [v.7]. Et quid restat? quod remedium Inter tanta mala, in istis tentationibus, in istis periculis? Dixi Domino, Deus meus es tu. lili nomines sunt, et non mei; tu et Deus, et meus es. Dixi Domino, Deus meus es tu. Magna vox orationis; movet fiduciam. Numquid illorum non

prayer; she excites confidence. Isn't He their God too? Whose God is not true God? However, he is properly the God of those who enjoy Him/who serve Him, who are willingly submitted to Him; for the evil ones, although forced, are also subject to him. The first approach God, who crowns them; The latter flee, being subject to the one who condemns them. The wicked one, who does not want to have the Lord as his God, where will he flee from the God who is God of all? It is good for him to convert to the God of all and to make him his own through conversion, so that, placed among sinners, seducers, hypocrites and arrogant, he says to God, whom by his conversion he made his God: I said to the Lord: "You are my God. Perceive with your ears, Lord, the voice of my prayer." This is a simple and easy to understand sentence. But, nevertheless, it is pleasant to think why he did not say: "Perceive with your ears my prayer", but, manifesting more evidently the affection of his mind, he says: The voice of my prayer, the life of my prayer, the soul of my prayer; not what sounds in my words, but what they live by. Other soulless noises can be called sounds, but not voices. The voice is typical of animated beings, of living beings. How many pray to God who do not perceive God or think well of Him! These may have the sound of prayer, but not the voice, because there is no life there. The voice of his prayer was that of this one who lived, who knew his God and saw by whom he was delivered and from whom. 11 [v.8]. Directing to the ears of God the voice of his oraest Deus? Cuius enim non est Deus, qui est verus Deus? Sed tamen proprie eorum est, qui eo fruuntur, qui ei serviunt, qui libenter sub ipso sunt. Nam et mali quamvis inviti, sub ipso sunt. lili appellant Deum, a quo coronentur; sub illo illi fugiunt, a quo damnentur. Et iniquus qui non vult habere Dominum Deum suum, quo fugiet Deum omnium? Bonum est illi ergo ut convertatur ad Deum omnium, faciatque illum conversione suum; et positus inter such peccatores, seducers, hypocrites, superbos, dicat ad Deum, quem sui conversione sibi fecit Deum suum: Dixi Domino, Deus meus es tu. Percipe auribus, Domine, vocem deprecatiónis meae.

Simplex quidem sententia est, et facilis ad intelligendum: sed tamen delectat forte cogitare quare non dixerit, Percipe auribus deprecationem meam; sed velut evidentius exprimens affectum animi sui, ait, vocem deprecatiónis meae, vitam deprecatiónis meae, animam deprecatiónis meae, non quod sonat in verbis meis, sed unde vivunt verba mea. Caeteri enim strepitus sine anima, soni dici possunt, voices non possunt: ​​vox proprie animatorum est, vivorum est. Quam multi autem deprecantur Deum, et non sentiunt Deum, nec bene cogitant de Deo? Sonum deprecatiónis habere possunt, vocem non possunt; quia vita ibi non est. Huius qui vivebat, quia Deum suum intelligebat, et a quo liberaretur videbat, et a quibus líberaretur sentiebat, ipsa erat vox deprecatíonis eius. 11 [v.8].
Ipsam commendans auribus Dei dicat, Domine, Domine.

i tion, say: Lord, Lord. You, Lord, Lord, that is, you who are most true Lord; not like gentlemen, not like gentlemen who buy with money, but like a Lord who buys with blood. Lord, Lord, strength of my health, that is, you give strength to my health. What does strength of my health mean? Who lamented the scandals and the snares of sinners, of evil men, instruments of the devil, who barked and lurked around, among whom life must necessarily be spent while we live here on this pilgrimage. The abundance of these future scandals was predicted by the Lord when he said: Iniquity will abound, and because it will abound, the charity of many will grow cold. But then he declared the consolation: He who perseveres to the end will be saved. The psalmist considering this sentence in spirit, feared, and, troubled by the abundance of iniquity, looked to hope, for he who perseveres to the end will be saved. He gave himself into the hands of perseverance and saw a long life; And since persevering is a great and difficult thing, he prayed, to obtain the perfection of his perseverance, from the same one who commanded him to persevere. Certainly I will be saved if I persevere to the end; but perseverance, as to merit health, belongs to fortitude; but you are the strength of my health, you give me the perseverance so that I can achieve health. Lord, Lord, strength of my health. Why do I trust that you are the strength of my health? Because you made a shadow over my head on the day of fighting. See that now I fight; Tu Domine, Domine, id est, tu verissime Domine, non quales domini nomines, non quales domini qui emunt saccello; sed qualis Dominus qui emit sanguine. Domine, Domine, virtus salutis meae: id est, qui das vires saluti meae. Quid sibi vult, virtus salutis meae? Conquerebatur de scandalis et insidiis peccatorum, de circumlatrantibus et circuminsídiantibus malignís hominibus vasis diaboli, de superbis invidentibus iustis, inter quales necesse est vitam ducere, cum hic vivimus in peregrinatione nostra hac. Talia vero scandala abundantiafutura Dominus praedixit, et ait: Abundabit iniquitas, et quoniam abundabit iniquitas, refrigescet charitas multorum. Sed adiunxit statim solatium: Qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit (Mt 24,12-13). Attendit iste, et timuit; et abundantia iniquitatum turbatus respexit spem: quia qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit.

Extendit se perseverare, et vidit longam viam; et quia perseverare magnum est et difficile, ipsum oravit ad perfectionem perseverantiae suae, a quo illi iussum est ut perseveraret. Certe salvus ero, si perseveravero usque in finem; sed perseverantia ad virtutem pertinet, ut merear salutem: tu es virtus salutis meae, tu me facis perseverare, ut perveniam ad salutem. Domine, Domine, virtus salutis meae. Et unde spero quia tu es virtus salutis meae? Obumbrasti super caput meum in die belli. Ecce moda adhuc pugno: pugno foris contra fictos bondes, pugno intus contra concupiscentias meas; quoniam video aliam legem in membris meis, repugnantem legi mentís meae, et captivum me

I fight externally against the false good, and internally against my lusts, because I see a law in my members that militates against the law of my mind and holds me captive in the law of sin that is in my members. Wretched man I! Who will free me from the body of this death? The grace of God through Jesus Christ, our Lord. Then, striving in this battle, he cast a glance at the grace of God; and, as it was already beginning to burn and dry, he found the shade in which to live: You made a shade over my head on the day of combat, that is, in the heat, so that I would not get tired or dry. 12 [v.9]. Do not hand me over, Lord, to the sinner according to my desire. This is what your shadow is for me: so that I don't bear the heat on my own. But what will the sinner do to me no matter how angry he is against me? The wicked were cruel to the martyrs; They dragged them, chained them, imprisoned them, killed them with the sword, threw them to the beasts, handed them over to the fire; They did all these things with them, but the Lord did not hand them over to sinners, because he did not hand them over according to their desire. Then ask as much as you can that the Lord does not hand you over to the sinner based on your desire, because by your desire you give a place to the devil. See that the devil proposed profit to you and invites you to fraud. You can't get the profit unless you commit fraud. Profit is the bait, fraud is the snare. Look at the bait so you can also see the loop. You can't get profit if you don't commit fraud; But, if you commit fraud, you are caught. I am not saying that you were caught because you have been conducentem in lege peccati, quae est in membris meis. Miser ego homo, can you free me from corpore mortis huius? Gratia Dei, per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum (Rom 7,23-25). Igitur laborans in hoc bello, respexit ad gratiam Dei; et quia iam coeperat aestuare et arescere, tanquam umbram invenit, sub qua viveret: Obrumbrasti super caput meum in die belli; Id est, in aestu, ne fatiguerer, ne arescerem. 12 [v.9]. Ne.Iradas me, Domine, a desiderio meo peccatori. Ecce quo mihi valebit umbraculum tuum, ut aestum non patiar a meipso. Et quid mihi peccator faceret ille, quantumlibet saeviret? Saevierunt enim in martyres iniqui; traxerunt eos, catnis ligaverunt, carceribus incluserunt, gladio fetietunt, bestiis subrexerunt, ignibus consumpserunt: haec omnia fecerunt; sed non eos tradidit Deus peccatoribus, quia non sunt traditi a desiderio suo.

Illud ergo ora, quantum potes, ut a desiderio tuo non te tradat Deus peccatori. Tu enim desiderio tuo locum diabolo das. Ecce enim diabolus proposuit lucrum, et invitation ad fraudm: lucrum habere non potes, nisi fraudm feceris. Sed lucrum esca est, fraus laqueus. Sic attende escam, ut videas et laqueum: quia lucrum non potes adipisci, nisi fraudm feceris; fraudm autem si feceris, capieris. Non ideo dico, capieris, quia invenieris: aliquando enim non invenieris, sed ab hominibus; never give Deo? Capieris, et traheris, et occideris. Omnis enim qui talia facit, perimit seipsum. Ibi est ergo esca, ibi est

trado. Sometimes you are not found, but by men. And by God? By God you are found, dragged away and killed. Anyone who commits such acts kills himself. Then here's the bait, here's the snare. Restrain desire, and you will not fall into the snare; because, if the desire for the bait overcomes you, your neck will be put in the noose and the hunter of souls will catch you. Do not hand me over to the sinner because of my desire. That is why the day of the fight is shaded. Desire breeds ardor, but the shadow of the Lord tempers desire so that we can contain ourselves to where we were led; so as not to become so inflamed that we fall into the trap. They plotted against me; do not forsake me, lest they become arrogant. In another psalm you read: Those who oppress me will rejoice if I am moved. This is also how these are, because that is also how the devil is. When she seduces man, she rejoices, she triumphs over him; He becomes arrogant, because he humiliated you. Why was the man humiliated? Because he was poorly exalted. Yet he who triumphed over man will be humiliated. So it is with all those who rejoice in evil; It seems to them that they boast, they become arrogant, they temporarily raise their necks. Do not delight in his arrogance; They have the bait and the hook in their mouths; in it is that by which they delight and by which they are carried away. Do not forsake me, lest they become arrogant, that is, do not triumph over me, do not rejoice in me. 13 [v.10]. The head of his rodeo, the work of his lips, will cover them. "The shadow of your wings will cover me," he says, "you made me a shadow on the day of battle." What will cover them? The head of its detour, that is, pride. What does his et laqueus mean; frena desiderium, et non cades in laqueum: si autem vicerit te desiderium escae, mittit tibi collum in laqueum, et capiet te auceps animarum. Ne tradas me a desiderio meo peccatori. Inde inumbratur in dei belli. Desiderium enim aestus facit; umbraculum autem Domini temperat desiderium, ut possimus refrenare quo rapiebamur, ut non ita exaestuemus, ut ad laqueum perducamur. Cogitaverunt adversum me; ne derelinquas me, ne forte exaltentur. Habes alio loco: Qui me premuní exsultabunt si motus fuero (Ps 12,5). Tales sunt et isti, quia talis est et ipse diabolus. Quando seduxerit hominem, gaudet, triumphat de illo; exaltatur ipse, quia ille humiliatus est. Quare autem ille humiliatus est? Qui male exaltatus Fuit: et ille qui de illo triumphat, humiliabitur.

Such sunt enim omnes qui gaudent de malo; videntur sibi ad tempus gloriari, superbire, cervicem erigere. What is called true charity of Christians was defined by Saint Paul, and, therefore, circumscribed with its own limits, even though it is infinite by divinity; so that it is completely distinguished from the others, since it says: The end of the precept is charity. Up to this point he could say this. Because in other places, where he spoke as to experts, he said: The perfect fulfillment of the law is charity, and he did not explain what charity. You love badly and uselessly, by loving your neighbor like this, what good do you do for them? When do you love yourself badly? Therefore the charity that comes from a pure heart is that which conforms to the standard of God and springs from a good conscience and an unfeigned faith. This charity defined by the Apostle contains within itself two precepts: the love of God and that of neighbor. Look for nothing else in the Scripture; Nobody sends you anything else. In everything that is hidden in Scripture, this love is hidden, and in everything that is evident in it, this love is evident. If it were nowhere to be seen, I would not feed you; If it did not appear hidden in any of them, it would not exercise you. This charity cries out from the pure heart, from the heart of those who pray these words with which this one here now prays. I will instantly say who this is: this is Christ. 3. 10. You know, brothers, and it must not be overlooked, that in the Manichean sect those who are considered among them to be the most eminent just are called elect, as if they had the supreme degree of justice. Those who know it, remember it; Let those who do not know it hear that the elect are all the saints of God, according to the Scriptures. But the Manichaeans usurped this name for themselves and applied it familiarly; so that they are already called elect as with their own name. Who are these chosen ones? Those to whom, if you say: "You have sinned," they immediately take up the impious defense, worse and more sacrilegious than the rest, saying: "It was not I who sinned, but the race of darkness." What is this race or people of darkness? The one who is at war with God. And this is the one who sins when you sin? "She," says the Manichean, "because I am mixed with her." But God, who mixed you up, what did he fear? They say that that prosapia of darkness rebelled against God before the world was created, and that He then, to prevent His kingdoms, when the opportunity arose, from being devastated with hostile impetus, sent here His particles, His substance, what He is; if I gold, I gold; yes light, light. What He is, this He sent; and they add that he mixed with the most intimate part of the race of darkness, and of this he made the world. They also say that we, souls, are of the members of God, but that we are tormented here by the bowels of the race of darkness, and everything we call sin is committed by that race. They certainly excuse themselves from sin, but they do not excuse God from the imputation of fear, nor the very substance of God from imputing guilt. Nostis, fratres, quod non est praetermittendum, quasi iustus eminentiores in se tenentes velut primum gtadum iustitiae, Electos vocari apud Manichaeos. Qui noverunt, recognoscant; qui nesciebant, audiant Electi quidem Dei sunt omnes sancti, et habemus hoc in Scripturis (Mt 34,22.24.31): sed usurparunt sibi illud nomen, et quasi familiarius sibi applicaverunt, ut tanquam proprie iam electi appellentur. Who sunt isti electi? Quibus si dixeris, Peccasti; statim illam defensionem impiam et peiorem caeteris magisque sacrilegam proferunt: Non ego peccavi, sed gens tenebrarum. Quae est ist gens tenebrarum? Quae bellum gessit cum Deo. Et ipsa peccat, cum tu peccas? Ipsa, inquit, quia commixtus sum illi. Deus enim qui te commiscuit, quid timuit?

Non enim nec mortem solam; sed nec cruzem, qua morte nihil videbatur exsecrabilius. Ipsam Dominus suscepit, ne discipuli eius mortem quidem non timerent, sed nec genus mortis horrescerent. Ergo a non timentibus cum dicuntur haec, praevaluerunt. 21 [v.7]. Quid ergo mortes illae omnium martyrum, quid fecerunt? Audi: Sicut crassido terrae disrupta est super terram, dissipata sunt iuxta infernum ossa nostra. Iuxta infernum dissipata sunt ossa martyrum, id est corpora testium Christi. Occisi sunt enim martyres, et

quasi praevaluerunt qui occiderunt. Praevaluerunt illi persequendo, ut praevalerent verba Christi praedicando. Et quid factum est de mortibus sanctorum? Nam dictum est et in quodam psalmo iacuisse mortes sanctorum; et non Fuit qui sepeliret (Ps 78,3). Sed illae omnes mortes factae sunt crassitudo terrae. Quomodo accipit terra quamdam pinguedinem de rebus contemptibilibus et abiectis; sic ex eo quod contempsit hic mundus, accepit crassitudinem terra, ut inde seges Ecclesiae feracius pullularet. Iam nostis, fratres, quia contemptibilia terrae huius, de quibus pinguescit terra, nec appellare voló, nec dicere decet: talis est quaedam sagina terrae, et quaedam pinguedo; et contemplibile est hominibus, et quasi sordidum est, et abiicitur. Sed qui fecit hic, ut iam et ipsius verbis utar? De terra erexit inopem, et de stercore exaltavit pauperem; ut collocaret eum cum principibus, cum principibus populi sui (Ps 112,7-8). Pretiosa est in conspectu Domini mors sanctorum eius (Ps 115,15). Sicut contemptibilis is saeculo, ita pretiosa is agricolae. Novit enim ibi utilitatem et uberem suecum, et novit quid

On the one hand, those who threaten are vicious; on the other, those who consent fall. I fear that this person is not someone I fear, that this person is not someone I imitate. Sinners will fall into their net. What does it mean, brothers, sinners will fall into your net? That not all sinners will fall into its net, but only sinners who are sinners in such a way that they love this life in such a way that they put it before eternal life. But what do you say? The evidence was presented, the accusation was presented, and the person questioned, and not by some exalted power, but by the lowest slave, by a slut, by a little girl, succumbed. He denied three times. Having denied one, remembering it, he denied again; Having denied two, remembering it, he denied a third time. The Lord had predicted this, he had not commanded it, he had not forced him. If it is believed that Peter acted rightly because the Lord had predicted it, then Judas, who betrayed him, also acted rightly, because the Lord also announced it to him. Far be it from us, my brothers, to believe such a thing. This voice is that of those chosen who rather defend than confess their sins. Let us preferably attend to Peter himself; If he sinned in nothing, why did he cry? Let us not question Peter, but Peter's tears. On this matter we do not find more faithful witnesses. He wept bitterly, says the evangelist. He was not yet in a condition to suffer. You will follow me later, he was told. He who was to be confirmed with the resurrection of the Lord was still weak.

If they were certainly not killed for confessing the name of Christ, they were nevertheless killed for the truth. To such an extent no one died for this name, that is, for confessing the name of Christ before the grain fell to the ground, of which it was said: I am the only one until it passes, that not even John the Baptist himself, who was recently beheaded by the wicked king, handed over to the jumping young woman, was killed for confessing Christ. Without a doubt it could have been for this reason, and so could many others; since, if the wicked king killed him for another reason, how much more could those who killed Christ kill him for Christ! Well, John bore witness to Christ. But those who heard about Christ tried to kill Christ, not him who bore witness to Him. However, if for Christ's sake they had fallen upon John, he would not deny him, because he had great strength, and because of it he was called the friend of the bridegroom. He possessed extraordinary grace, supreme excellence: Among those born of women, no one appeared greater than Juan Bautista. Violence raged against him who did not have such strength; He was angry at Peter, not at John. However, Peter later received this strength; at first it was weak. He who had no strength was questioned for the name of Christ, and he who had strength did not suffer persecution for this name, so that he would not precede Christ by suffering for his name. [PRAYER OF THE MAN ABANDONED BY GOD] SERMON TO THE PEOPLE

1. Just as the fervor of your attendance is due to the festival of the martyrs, so is the homage of my sermon. Your charity should remember the many things we said yesterday. But not because, due to the eagerness of your heart, you attended the entire sermon tirelessly, we should forget the common weakness. First of all, it is advisable to honor the words of sublime virtue, as it was written, because the sublime words of wisdom are from the Lord; However, by me, as by an instrument, they are provided to you; and though the tray is brittle, yet the bread is heavenly. The Apostle says: We have this treasure in earthen vessels so that the surpassing power of virtue is from God. This treasure is the bread itself, since, if the treasure were not bread, it would not have been written elsewhere about the treasure: The desirable treasure is found Christo, quem occiderunt Iudaei; et occiditur ab Herode, quia dicebat ei, Non tibí licet habere uxorem fratris tui (ib. 14,3-11). deposited in the mouth of the wise man, but the foolish man swallows it. That is why we admonish your charity that you store the things that you hear in the pantry of your memory, thinking about them and reviewing them, you ruminate on them. This is, then, the desirable treasure is deposited in the mouth of the wise man, since the foolish man swallows it up. For this reason he briefly said: the wise man ruminates, the fool does not ruminate. What does this mean in Spanish and clearly? That the wise man thinks about the things he heard, and the fool, on the contrary, consigns them to oblivion. For no other reason than this, in the law those who chew the cud were called world animals, and those who do not chew the cud were called unclean, since every creature of God is worldly. For the creator God, the pig is as worldly or pure as the lamb, since he created all things exceedingly good. And the Apostle says: Every creature of God is good; and he also writes: All things are pure to the pure. Therefore, even though, as regards nature, the pig and the lamb are both pure, yet, by symbolism, the lamb signifies something pure, and the pig something impure; The lamb signifies the innocence of the wisdom of the one who chews the cud, and the pig, the filth of the folly of the one who forgets. Taking into account the festivity, a short psalm was chosen; Let us see if it can be briefly discussed. 2 [v.2]. With my voice I cried to the Lord. It would have been enough to say: With my voice I cried to the Lord; Therefore, it was not in vain that it was added with mi. Many cry out to the Lord, not with their voice, but with that of their body. Then the inner man, in which he began to dwell desiderabilis requiescit in ore sapientis; vir autem stultus glutit illum (Prov 21:20). Unde admonemus Charitatem vestram ut ea quae audiendo tanquam ventre memoriae conditis, rursus revolvendo et cogitando quodammodo ruminetis. Hoc est enim, Thesaurus desiderabilis requiescit in ore sapientis; vir autem stultus glutit illum: breviter dixit, Sapiens ruminat, stultus non ruminat. Hoc autem aperte et latine quid est? Sapiens cogitat ea quae auditerit; stultus autem audita oblivioni tradit. Ñeque enim propter aliud in Lege, munda ea dicta sunt animalia quae ruminant, immunda quae non ruminant (Lev 12:2-8): nam creatura Dei omnis munda est. Artifici Deo tam mundus est porcus quam agnus. Creavit enim omnia bona valde (Gen 1,31): et, Omnis creatura Dei bona est, dicit Apostolus (1 Tim 4,4); et, Omnia munda mundis (Tit 1:15).

Cum ergo in natura utrumque sit mundum; significatione tamen agnus significat aliquid mundum, porcus significat aliquid immundum: agnus significat innocentiam sapientiae ruminantis; porcus significat immunditiam stultitiae obliviscentis. Christ by faith, cry out to the Lord with the voice of the affection of your heart, not with the noise of your lips. Man does not hear where God hears; If you do not cry with the voice produced by the lungs, the mouth and the tongue, man will not hear you; However, your thought is a cry to the Lord. I cried out to the Lord with my voice; With my voice I prayed to the Lord. By saying I prayed he manifested what he cried out for, since those who blaspheme also cry out to God. In the first verse he recorded the cry, in the second he declared this cry. As if asked: "What did you cry to the Lord?", he says: I prayed to the Lord. My cry is my prayer, not an insult, a murmuring, a blasphemy.

3 [v.3]. I will pray before Him. What does it mean before Him? In his presence. What does "in his presence" mean? Where you see. But where can't you see? We say where you see as if there were somewhere where you don't see. In this set of corporeal things, men and animals also see; but He also sees where man does not see. No man sees your thought, God does. Pour out your prayer where only He who rewards sees. Our Lord Jesus Christ commanded you to pray in secret. If you know your room and purify it, there you pray to God. When you pray, says the Lord, do not be like the hypocrites, who stand to pray in the squares and at the crossroads so that men can see them. You, on the other hand, when you pray, go into your room and close the door, and pray to your God in secret; and He, who sees in secret, will repay you. If men are to repay you, pray before men; but, if it is God who has

To give back, pour out your prayer before Him and close the door so that the tempter does not enter. The tempter keeps knocking to enter; but if he sees that it is closed, he passes by. Therefore, the Apostle, knowing that it is in our power to close the door, the door of the heart, not the door of the wall, since that is where the chamber is located, says, knowing, I repeat, that it is in our power to close this door: Do not give room to the devil. Therefore, if he entered and stayed, he sees that you closed the door negligently or that you were careless in closing. 4. What does "close the door" mean? This door has like two leaves: of greed and of fear. Either you desire something earthly, and it enters this way, or you fear something worldly, and it enters it this way. Then close the door of fear and greed against the devil and open it to Christ. How are you to open these two leaves to Christ? Desiring the kingdom of heaven and fearing the fire of hell. The devil enters through worldly greed, Christ through the desire for eternal life; The devil enters through fear of temporal punishments, Christ through fear of eternal fire. See how the martyrs closed the door to the devil and opened it to Christ. The world promised them many things, they despised them: they closed the leaf of greed to the devil. The world threatened them with beasts, fire, the cross; They did not fear: they closed the leaf of fear of the devil. Let's see if they opened the doors to Christ: Whoever confesses me or bears witness about me, says Jesus, before men, him I will confess before my Father who is in heaven. So they loved the kingdom of heaven, where Christ will confess to them.

strepitu labiorum, sed in affectu cordis clamet ad Dominum. Non ubi homo audit, ibi Deus audit: nisi voce pulmonum et laterum et linguae clames, homo te non audit; cogitatio tua clamor est ad Dominum. Voce mea ad Dominum clamavi; voce mea ai Dominum deprecatus sum. Quod dixit, clamavi; exposuit, cum dixit, deprecatus sum. Clamant enim ad Dominum et qui blasphemant. In superiori versu clamorem posuit, in sequenti clamorem exposuit. Quasi demandingetur, Quo clamore clamasti ad Dominum? Ad Dominum, inquit, deprecatus sum: clamor meus, deprecated mea; non convicium, non murmur, non blasphemia. 3 [v.3]. Efffundam ante eum precem meam. Quid est, ante eum? In conspectu eius. Quid est, in conspectu eius? Ubi videt, Ubi autem non videt? Ita enim dicimus, Ubi videt, quasi alicubi non videat. Sed in isto coetu rerum corporalium vident et homines, vident et animalia: ille autem videt et ubi homo non videt. Nam cogitationem tuam nullus hominum videt, Deus autem videt. Ibi ergo effunde precem tuam, ubi solus ille videt qui remunerat. Nam in abscondito te Dominus Iesus Christus iussit orare: sed si agnoscas cubiculum tuum, et mundes, ibi rogas Deum. Cum autem oratis, inquit, nolite esse sicut hypocritae, qui stant in plateis et vicis orantes, ut videantur ab hominibus. Tu autem cum oras, intra in cubiculum tuum, et claude ostium, et deprecare Deum tuum in occulto; et qui videt in occulto, reddet tibi (Mt 6,5 et 6).

Si homines reddituri sunt, effunde ante homines precem tuam: si Deus redditurus est, effunde ante eum precem tuam, et claude ostium, ne tentator ingrediatur. Tentator non cessat pulsare, ut irrumpat: si clausum invenerit, transit. Ideo Apostolus, quia in our potestate is ostium claudere: ostium cordis, non parietum; ibi enim et cubiculum: quia ergo in potestate nostra est hoc ostium claudere, Ñeque detis, inquit, locum diabolo (Eph 4,27). Etenim si intravit et possedit, attende quia tu negligenter clausisti aut claudere neglexisti. 4. Quid est autem claudere ostium? Hoc ostium tanquam duas habet valves; cupiditatis, et timoris. Aut cupis aliquid terrenum, et hac intrat; aut times aliquid terrenum, et hac intrat. Timoris ergo et cupiditatis ianuam claude contra diabolum, aperi ad Christum. Quomodo ipsas valves aperis ad Christum? Cupiendo regnum caelorum, timendo ignem gehennarum. Per cupiditatem saeculi diabolus intrat, per desiderium vitae aeternae Christus intrat: per timorem poenarum temporalium diabolus intrat, per timorem ignis aeterni Christus intrat. Ecce martyres clausérunt ianuam contra diabolum, Christo aperuerunt. Promisit eis fines mundus iste: riserunt, clausérunt valvam cupiditatis adversus diabolum. Minatus est mundus iste beasts, ignes, crosses: non timuerunt, clausérunt timoris valvam contra diabolum. How are you to confess them or bear witness to them? Saying to them: Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom that was prepared for you from the beginning of the world. He must bear witness to those placed on his right. Let's see if they opened to Christ the leaf of fear that they closed to the devil. In one and the same place the Lord admonishes to close oneself to the devil and open oneself to Him: Do not fear, He says, those who kill the body and cannot kill the soul. For this reason he commands that the sheet of fear before the devil be annulled. So then there is nothing to fear? Should not the entrance of fear, which is closed to the devil, be opened to Christ? Then, as if saying: "You closed the devil; open me," he adds: But fear him who has the power to kill and throw soul and body into the fires of hell. Then, if you believed and opened to Christ, close the door to the devil. Christ is within; there he dwells; pray before Him; Don't try to make him hear you from afar. For the Wisdom of God is not far away, which extends from one border to the other with strength and orders all things with gentleness. Then within, in you and before Him, pour out your prayer; there are your ears. For neither to the east, nor to the west, nor to the desert mountains (you will flee to hide), since God is the judge. If he is a judge, see the cause that you carry in your heart. 5 [v.4]. I will pour out my prayer before Him; I will manifest my tribulation in his presence. This is a repeat. In the two previous verses and in these next two there are two maxims, but both are repeated. One is: I cried out to the Lord with my voice; with me

voice I prayed to the Lord. The other: I will pour out my prayer before Him; I will manifest my tribulation in his presence. It is the same before Him that in His presence, as it is the same I will pour out my prayer as I will manifest my tribulation. When do you do this? When, placed in persecution, you say: My spirit has failed. Why did your spirit fail, O martyr! placed in tribulation? So that he does not attribute my strength to me; so that I may know that another is the one who works the power in me. When they hand you over to the judges - this is how the Lord admonishes those whom he wanted to be his martyrs - do not think about what you have to say, for it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks for you. Then let your spirit fail and the Spirit of God speak. No wonder he wanted to make them poor in spirit: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Therefore the poor who are blessed in their spirit are rich through the Spirit of God, for every man who pursues his spirit is proud. Submit your spirit so that you may obtain the spirit of God. He was heading to the top; stay in the valley. If He heads to the top, the water moves away from Him, running downwards. If it remains in the valley, it will be filled with it and will become a womb, of which it was said: Rivers of living water will flow from its womb. Then, as my spirit fainted, I manifested my tribulation in your presence; That is, by confessing to you that my spirit was failing, even though I am full of your Spirit, I humbled myself. 6. Perhaps the men heard that my spirit had failed within me, and they distrusted me and said, "We have caught him, we have caught him."

Si ierit in culmen, denatat ab illo aqua: si in valle resederit, implebitur ea, et fit ule venter de quo dictum est. Flumina aquae vivae fluent de ventre eius (lo 7.38). science; And if I had perfect faith, so that I could move mountains, yet if I lack charity, I am nothing; And if I distribute all my property to the poor and give my body to the flames, but have no charity, it is of no use to me. Then he called charity the most excellent way. This excellent path, brothers, is wonderful. This path, because it is most exalted, is also most excellent, since what is excellent stands out. There is nothing more excellent than the path of charity, and only the humble walk along it. He called these paths precepts of charity. You, he says, knew my paths; You knew that what I suffer for you I suffer for love; You knew that the charity that is in me tolerates all things, you knew that, if I give my body to the flames, it is because I have that flame without which it is of no use to man. 8. But who, my brothers, knows these ways of man except Him to whom it was said: Thou hast known my paths? We do not know with what intention all the human acts that are carried out before the eyes of men are done. How many impious people, measuring us by themselves, say of us that in the Church we seek honors, praise, temporal usefulness! How many say that I speak to you so that you will acclaim and praise me and that this is the goal I propose and the intention I have in speaking to you! But since I cannot prove to you that I do not speak with this intention, it only remains for me to say: You knew my paths. How do they know what you don't know? How do they know what I hardly know? But I do not judge myself, what judges me is et omnem scientiam; et si habuero omnem fidem, ita ut montes transferam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil sum: et si distribuero omnia mea pauperibus, et si tradidero corpus meum ut ardeam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil mihi prodest (ib. 13,1-3). Ergo charitatem dixit supereminentíorem viam. Magna ista via, fratres, magnum miraculum habet. Haec via certe, quia supereminentior est, et excellentior est; hoc enim supereminet, quod excelsum est. Nihil excelsius via charitatis, et non in illa ambulant nisi humiles. Has ergo semitas, dicit praecepta charitatis. Tu, inquit, cognovisti semitas meas: tu nosti quia quod pro te patior, amore patior; tu nosti quia charitas in me omnia tolerat; tu nosti quia et si trado corpus meum ut ardeam, habeo illam, sine qua illud non prodest homini. 8.

Meditating on all the works of God, the psalmist hints at grace, remembers grace, glories in having found grace; the grace by which we are saved freely, since we are saved freely. Why do you boast of your justice? Why do you conceit yourself, not knowing the justice of God? Did you perhaps give something so that you would be saved? What did you give to be a man? Then look at the Creator of your life, the author of your nature, your justice and your salvation. Meditate on the works of his hands, for you will also find that the righteousness that is in you belongs to his hand (his work).
