1 [v.l]. The title of this psalm is brief in words, but important for the depth of the mysteries. For David; against Goliath. Your charity will remember with me, paying attention to the Holy Scripture, this struggle that took place in the time of our ancestors. On one occasion, while foreigners were fighting against God's people, one provoked another: Goliath provoked David. In this contest the will of God was to be manifested with the victory of one of the parties. But why do we worry about victory when we see the one who provokes and the provoked? He provoked impiety to piety, he provoked pride to humility; In short, the devil provoked Christ. Why do you wonder that the devil was defeated? Goliath was great in corporeal stature; David, on the other hand, was small in body, but great in faith. Saint David put on war weapons to go out to meet Goliath; but, due, as we said, to his young age and his small body stature, he could not bear them. Then, putting aside what hindered him, not the nomen tuum, Domine, vivificabis me: in tua iustitia educes de tribulatione animam meam; et in your mercy ad interitum you deduce meos mimics. Et perdes omnes tribulantes animam meam; quoniam servus tuus sum ego.

1 [v.l]. Psalmi huius titulus brevis est numero verborum, sed gravis pondere mysteriorum: Ipsi David ad Goliam. Praelium hoc factum tempore patrum nostrorum, de Scripturis sanctis recolit mecum Charitas vestra. Cum enim adversus populum Dei alienigenae dimicarent, provocavit unus unum, Golias David: in quo certamine voluntas Dei pro cuiusque partís victoria proveetur. Sed crux of victory satagimus, quando provocantem provocatumque cernamus? Provocavit impietas pietatem, provocavit superbia humilitatem, postremo provocavit diabolus Christum. Quid miramini diabolum victum? Ule erat grandis statura corporis; iste autem statura parvus, fide magnus. Accepit arma bellica sanctus David, ut adversus Goliam proceedet. Haec arma per aetatem, et parvam, ut diximus, staturam corporis, portare non valuit. Abiecit onerantia, non adiuvantia: accepit quinqué lapides de illumine, et posuit in vase pastorali. His armatus corporaliter, nomine autem Dei spiritua-
Thanksgiving for victory

who was helping him, took five stones from the river and put them in his shepherd's bag. Armed, physically with them, and spiritually with the name of God, he went out to meet him and defeated him. This is what David did; but let us investigate the mysteries. We said that the title of the psalm was brief in words, but important for the depth of the mysteries. Let us remember the apostolic sentence: All these things happened figuratively to them, so that it does not appear that we petulantly investigate something hidden where everything narrated could be exposed simply without an abyss of mystery. Then we have the authority that excites our attention to search, awakens us to investigate, gives us the devotion to hear, gives us the faith to believe, and removes laziness from us to act. Christ is personified in David, but as those indoctrinated in his school tend to understand him: Christ Head and Body. Therefore do not hear anything that is said in the person of Christ as if it did not belong to you, who are members of Christ. With this established as a basis, see what follows. 2. You know that the first people of God were overloaded with an infinite number of corporal and visible sacraments: with circumcision, the laborious priesthood, the temple full of symbols, the multitude of kinds of sacrifices and burnt offerings. Our David laid down all these things as weapons that overwhelmed and did not help. For if the law had been given in such a way that it could truly give life, justice would proceed from the law. But then, what was the law given for? The Apostle himself explains it, saying: Scripture encloses everything under sin a fin liter, processit, et vicit (1 Reg 17). Hoc quidem ille David: sed mysteria perscrutemur. Proposueramus enim titulum istum brevem numero verborum, sed gravem pondere mysteriorum. Veniat in mentem apostolica illa sententia, Omnia haec in figura contingebant in Mis (1 Cor 10:11); ne impudenter videoamur quaerere aliquid absconditum, ubi possit dici totum sine mysterii profundidate simpliciter dictum. Habemus ergo auctoritatem facientem nos attempts ad quaerendum, vigiles ad investigandum, devotees ad audiendum, fideles ad credendum, impigros ad faciendum. In David Christus: sed sicut soletis intelligere eruditi in schola eius, Christus caput et corpus. Non ergo sic auditatis aliquid ex persona Christi, quasi ad vos non pertineat, qui estis membra Christi. Hoc tanquam fundament pósito, videte quae sequantur. 2.

Nostis multis sacramentis visibilibus et corporalibus oneratum esse populum primum; circumcisione, negotioso illo quodam sacerdotio, et temple figuris plena, multiplicibus holocaustorum sacrificerumque generibus. Haec David noster tanquam arma prementia, non adiuvantia, posit. Si enim data esset lex quae posset vivificare, I will see ex Lege esset iustitia. Utquid ergo Lex? Sequitur: Sed conclusit Scriptura omnia sub peccato, ut promissio ex fide Iesu Christi daretur credentibus (Gal 3, 21-22). Denique iste David, scilicet Christus caput et corpus, tempore
Ennarrations on the Psalms

that the promise was given to believers by virtue of the faith in Jesus Christ. In short, this David, that is, Christ Head and Body, what did he do at the time of the manifestation of the New Testament, at the time of the insinuation and recommendation of God's grace? He laid down his weapons and took five stones; He laid down, as we said, his oppressive weapons. Then he laid down the sacraments of the law, the sacraments of that law which we do not observe and which were not imposed on the Gentiles. For you remember how many things are read in the Old Law that we do not observe, and that, however, we know were proposed and established with some significance; not to despise the law of God, but so that, as promissory sacraments, once the promise was fulfilled, we would not celebrate them. So what they promised arrived. The grace of the New Testament was veiled in the law; in the Gospel it is revealed. We lifted the veil and learned what it was hiding; we knew by the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Head and Savior, who was crucified for us; that, upon being crucified, the veil of the temple was torn. In short, He laid down his arms as a burden for the sacraments of the Old Law. However, He took the law, because the five stones symbolized the five books of Moses. So he took five stones from the river. You know what the river means: the world. Well then: the mortal world slips away, and everything in the world runs along. In the river, as in that first town, the stones were found; There they were useless, they were idle, they were of no use, they passed by staying on the river. What did David do to make the law useful? Took the revelationis Novi Testamenti, tempore insirmandae et commendandae gratiae Dei, quid fecit? Arma posit, quinqué lapides tulit: arma, ut diximus, onetantia posit; ergo sacramenta Legis, sacramenta illa Legis, quae non sunt imposita Gentibus, posit, quae non observamus. Meministis enim quanta in Veteri Lege legamus, et non observamus; sed tamen ad aliquam significationem praemissa et proposita intelligamus: non ut abiiciamus Legem Dei, sed ut sacramenta promittentia, impleta promissione non celebremus. Quod enim promittebant, come. Gratia enim Novi Testamenti in Lege velabatur; in Gospel revelationtur. Velum removimus, quod velabatur agnovimus: agnovimus autem in gratia Domini nostti Iesu Christi, capitis et Salvatoris nostri, qui pro nobis crucifixus est; quo crucifixo etiam velum templi conscissum est (Mt 27:51).

Denique arma ille posuit, tanquam onera sacramentorum Veteris Legis; et ipsam Legem accepit. Quinqué enim lapides quinqué books Moysi significant. Tulit ergo illos quinqué lapides de flumine._ Nostis quid sit fluvius. Labitur enim mortale saeculum, et praeterfluit quidquid venit in mundum. Erant ergo in illumine, tanquam in populo illo primo, lapides; illic werent useless, vacabant, nihil proderant, transibant super fluvios. Quid fecit David, ut Lex ipsa utilis esset? Accept gratiam. Lex enim sine gratia impleri non potest: Plenitudo enim Legis chantas (Rom 13:10). Et where is this chantas? See si non ex gratia.

funny. For the law without grace cannot be fulfilled. The perfection or fulfillment of the law is charity. And where does charity come from? See if it does not come from grace. The charity of God—says the Apostle—was spread in our hearts by the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. As grace provides the fulfillment of the law, grace is symbolized in milk, since it is free in the flesh, since the mother does not demand a reward for it, but is concerned about giving it. The mother gives it freely, and is sad if there is no one to receive it. Then how did David demonstrate that the law cannot be fulfilled without grace? Wanting to unite with grace those five stones, with which the law, contained in the five books, was symbolized, he placed them in the bag in which he used to carry the milk. Thus armed, certainly armed with grace, and, therefore, not boasting of himself, but of his Lord, he went out to meet the proud Goliath, who boasted and boasted of himself. He takes a stone, throws it, and hits the enemy in the forehead, who falls face down, hitting the ground with his forehead, on which he did not have the sign of Christ. You should also note that he put five stones in the bag and only threw one. Five books were chosen, but unity prevailed, since the fulfillment or perfection of the law, as I recalled shortly before, is charity; and the same Apostle says: Let us suffer one another with charity, seeking to preserve the unity of spirit in the bond of peace. Then, wounded and thrown to the ground, he took his sword and with it cut off his head. Our David did the same when he cast out the devil from his people; for, when his primates believe, Chantas, inquit, Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis (ib. 5,5). Quia ergo gratia fecit imperi Legem, significatur autem gratia lacte; hoc enim est in carne gratuitum, ubi mater non quaerit accipere, sed satagit daré; hoc mater gratis dat, et contristatur si desit qui accipiat: quomodo ergo ostendit David Legem_ sine gratia operani non posse, nisi cum illos lapides quinqué, quibus significatur Lex in libris quinqué, coniungere volens gratiae, posit in vase pastorali, quo lac mulgere consueverat? His armatus, gratia utique armatus, et ideo praesumens non de se, sed de Domino suo, processit adversus Goliam superbum, se iactantem, de se praesumentem.

Tulit unum lapidem, iecit, inimicum in fronte percussit; cecidit ex eo loco corporis, ubi signum Christi non habuit. Hoc quoque licet atiendas: quinqué lapides posuit, unum misit. Libri quinqué lecti sunt, sed unitas vicit. Plenitudo enim Legis, ut paulo ante commemoravimus, chantas: et Apostolus ait, Sufferentes invicem in dilectione, studentes servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis (Eph 4,2-3). Deinde illo percusso atque deiecto, gladium eius abstulit, et inde caput illi abscidit. Et hoc fecit noster David, deiecit diabolum de suis: quando autem credunt magni eius, quos ille in manu habebat, et de quibus caeteras animas

those whom he had in his hand, and with whom he killed other souls, then they turn their tongues against the devil, and thus he cuts off Goliath's head with his sword. I explained the mystery of the title according to the brevity of time. Let's see what the same psalm contains. 3. Blessed be the Lord, my God, who trains my hands for fighting, and my fingers for war. It is our voice if we belong to the Body of Christ. Let us bless the Lord, our God, who trains our hands for combat, and our fingers for war. It seems like a repetition, since our hands are the same for combat as our fingers are for war. Or is there a difference between hands and fingers? With the fingers, without a doubt, the hands work; Therefore we do not absurdly understand that the fingers are held by the hands. However, in the fingers we observe the division of the work, and we also notice the foundation or root of the unity. Consider, then, the grace, of which the Apostle says: To some it is given by the Spirit speaks of wisdom; to others, the word of knowledge according to the same Spirit; to others, faith in the same Spirit; to others, the gift of healing in a single Spirit; to others, lineage of languages; to others, prophecy; to others, discernment of spirits; But all these things are worked by one and the same Spirit, who distributes his own gifts to each one as he wishes. To some this, to others that. These are the divisions of the work. All these things are accomplished by one and the same Spirit, which is the foundation or root of unity. Then, armed with these fingers, the Body of Christ fights, going to war, going out to combat.

4. Perhaps it is lengthy to enumerate the kinds of struggles and combats; However, they are easier to endure than to explain. We endure a particular combat that the Apostle commemorates: This fight of ours—he says—is not against flesh and blood, that is, against men from whom you endure discomfort. You do not fight against these, but against the princes and powers and against the rulers of the world. And so that you would not understand by rulers of the world the rulers of heaven and earth, he stated to whom he was referring, adding: of this darkness. Namely, the rulers not of that world that was made by Him, because the world was made by God, but of the world that did not know Him, since the world did not know Him. These darknesses are not darkness by nature, but by will. The soul does not shine by itself, since with all truth and humility it sings: You will illuminate my lamp, Lord; Oh my God, illuminate my darkness; and also says: In you is the source of life; with your light we will see the light; not with our light, but with your light. Our eyes are called luminaries, and yet if external light is lacking, even when they are healthy and open, they remain in darkness. Then we war against the rulers of this darkness, against the rulers of the non-believers, against the devil and his angels, against the wielders of his sword with which the devil fights against the faithful. But as, when Goliath was knocked down, he took the sword from Goliath to cut off his head with it, so, when the unbelievers believe, they are told: Once you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. You fought with

trucidabat, convertunt linguas suas contra diabolum; et sic Goliae de gladio suo caput inciditur. Mysterium tituli pro temporis brevitate tractavimus; videamus quid habeat ipse Psalmus. 3. Benedictas Dominus Deus meus, qui docet manus meas in praelium, digits meos ad bellum. Vox nostra est, si Corpus Christi sumus us. Benedicamus Dominum Deum nostrum qui docet manus nostras in praelium, digits nostros ad bellum. Repetitio sententiae videtur: quod est, manus nostras in praelium; hoc est; digits nostros ad bellum. An aliquid interest Inter manus et digits? Digitis utique operantur et manus: non itaque absurde accipimus digitos pro manibus pósitos. Verumtamen in digitis agnoscimus divisionem operationis, et tamen radicem unitatis. Vide illam gratiam: dicit Apostolus, «Alii quidem per Spiritum datur sermo sapientiae, alii sermo scientiae secundum eumdem Spiritum, alii fides in eodem Spiritu, alii donationes curationum in uno Spiritu, alii genera linguarum, alii prophetia, alii diiudicatio spirituum. Omnia autem haec operatur unus atque idem Spiritus, dividends propria unicuique prout vult” (1 Cor 12:8). Alii illud, alii hoc; divisions sunt operationis: Omnia haec operatur unus atque idem Spiritus; radix est unitatis. His ergo digitis pugnat corpus Christi, proceedens in bellum, proceedens in praelium.

4. Iam praeliorum et bellorum genera commemorare fortasse longum est, et gerere facilius quam explicare. Habemus unum bellum quod commemorat Apostolus: Non est vobis colluctatio adversus carnem et sanguinem, id est, adversus nomines a quibus videmini pati inconveniences; non adversus ipsos pugnatis: sed adversus princes et potestates et rectores mundi. Et ne intelligeres mundi, caeli et terrae, ostendit quid diceret: Tenebrarum, inquit, harum (Eph 6,12). Mundi scilicet, non qui per ipsum factus est; quia, Et mundus per eum factus est: sed mundi qui eum non cognovit; quia, Et mundus eum non cognovit (lo 1,10). Hae tenebrae non sunt natura, sed volúntate. Anima enim per semetipsam non luzet: quia humiliter et veraciter cantat, Tu illuminabis luzernam meam, Domine; Deus meus, illumina tenebras meas (Ps 17,29): et, Apud te, inquit, fons vitae; in lumine tuo videbimus lumen (Ps 35,10); non in lumine nostro, sed in lumine tuo. Nam et oculi nostri lumina vocantur; et tamen lux extrinsecus si desit, etiam sani et patents, in tenebris remanebunt. Ergo bellum gerimus adversus rectores tenebrarum harum, rectores scilicet infidelium, diabolum et angelos eius, rectores gladii eius de quo pugnat diabolus adversus fideles. Sed quomodo Goliae prostrato toUitur gladius, ut ipsi Goliae caput de gladio suo amputetur; ita eum credunt ipsi infideles, dicitur eis: Fuistis ali-

hand or the power of Goliath, cut off Goliath's head now with the power or the hand of Christ. 5. This is a certain combat; but there is another that each one bears in himself. Now we read this type of struggle in the epistle to the Galatians: The flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh, so that you do not do what you want. This is a violent fight, and, because it is internal, more annoying. If anyone wins in this combat, he immediately defeats the enemies he does not see. The devil and his angels only tempt the carnal that dominates you. Because how do we defeat the enemies we do not see if it is not because we perceive our internal carnal movements? Against these we fight and these we wound. In the love of wealth, greed dominates. As greed dominates you, the devil externally proposes profit through fraud. Many times you don't make a profit if you don't commit fraud. Then he externally proposes to your greed, which you did not win, which you did not dominate, which you did not internally submit, like a bad competition president to his athlete, the fraud and the profit: the work and the prize. Work and take (that's what it tells you). But, if you trample on greed, if it does not dominate you internally, you will defeat what you feel, because you do not perceive the seductive devil. Then, if you mastered greed, you attended to the one who proposed another work and another prize. What did he propose to you? Fraud and profit. What did this one propose to you? Probity and the crown. Work and take, both tell you. You, inner combatant, if greed did not defeat you, but you defeated it, you attended to this one, you defeated that one. Distinc-

You look at both and say: "Here I see the work and the prize; there, the bait and the snare." And you notice nothing in yourself that does not belong to you. Indeed, because of sin you were divided against yourself. You drag the spread of concupiscence and the graft of death; You have something that you have to fight against in yourself, something that you have to discover in yourself. But you have someone to invoke so that, as a combatant, he will help you, and as a victor, he will crown you, who created you when you did not exist. 6. "How am I to win?" you say. He sees that the Apostle himself proposes a very difficult combat, and declares how difficult it is, or perhaps insurmountable, if I don't understand. The flesh, he says, covets against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh, so that you do not do what you want. "How can you command me to conquer, since He says: so that you do not do what you want?" Questions: "How?" Pay attention to the grace of the pastoral bag, put the river stone in the milk container. See that I also tell you; What's more, the Truth itself tells you so. Indeed, you do not do what you want when the flesh fights against the spirit. If in the face of this struggle you boast of yourself, you must be admonished, lest you hear in vain: Rejoice in God, our helper. Well, if you accomplished everything by yourself, you wouldn't need a helper. On the other hand, if you did not do anything that came from your will, you would not be called a helper, since the helper helps the one who does something. Finally, after having said: The flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh, so that you do not do what you want; and also, after having placed you before you as if fainting

when tenebrae; nunc autem lux in Domino (Eph 5,8). Pugnastis de manu Goliae, iam in manu Christi tollite caput Goliae. 5. Hoc unum praelium: alterum autem unicuique in seipso. Mode genus hoc belli ex apostolic Epistle legebatur: Caro concupiscit adversus spiritum, et spiritus adversus carnem; ut non ea quae vultis, faciatis. Et hoc grave bellurn, et quod est molestius, internum. In quo bello si sit quisque victor, illos quos non videt inimicos, continuous superabit. Non enim tentat diabolus vel angelí eius, nisi quod in te carnal dominátur. Nam quomodo vincimus illos hostes quos non videmus, nisi quia carnal interiors motus nostros sentimus? Cum his confligimus, et illos percutimus. In amore pecuniae dominátur avaritia: dominanti tibi avaritiae diabolus forinsecus lucrum cum fraud proponit. Plerumque enim ad lucrum non pervenis, nisi fraudm feceris. Proponit ergo ille forinsecus avaritiae tuae quam íntus non vicisti, quam non domuisti, quam non tibi subiecisti; proponit tanquam, athletae suo malus agonotheta fraudm et lucrum, opus et praemium: Fac, et tolle. Tu autem si calcas avaritíam, si tibi interius non dominátur, quam sentiens vincis; nam diabolum insidiantem nonísimos: si ergo edomuisti avatítiam, attendis alterum proponentem opus et praemium. What is the proposal? Fraudem et lucrum. What did you propose? Innocentiam et coronam. Fac et tolle, et ille dicit, et iste. Iam your inner praelatior, if it is not victus avaritia,

sed victor avaritiae; illum attendis, hunc vincis. Discernís enim utrumque, et dicis: Hic video opus et praemium, illic autem escam et Iaqueum. Ñeque enim aliquid dicis in te, quod non pertineat ad te. Etením ex peccato divisus is adversum te. Trahis concupiscentiae propaginem et translatem mortis: habes contra quod pugnes in te, habes quod expugnes in te. Sed habes quem invoces, ut pugnantem adiuvet te, et vincentem coronet te, qui nonexistentm fecit te. 6. Quomodo, inquis, vincam? Ecce ipse Apostolus difficillimum praelium proponit, et quam laboriosum sit aut forte insuperabile, si non intelligo, ipse ostendit. Caro, inquit, concupiscit adversus spiritum, et spiritus adversus carnem; ut non ea quae vultis, faciatis. Quomodo me iubes vincere, cum ille dicat, Ut non ea quae vultis, faciatis? Quaeris quomodo? attende ad gratiam vasis pastoralis, lapidem de illumine inexceptio lactis pone. Ecce et ego tibí dico, imo tibi ipsa veritas dicit. Prorsus non facis quod vis, pugnante carne adversus spiritum tuum. Si ad istam pugnam de te praesumis, admonendus es, ne frustra audieris, Exsultate Deo adiutori nostro (Ps 80,2). Si enim per te impleres totum, non esset necessarius adiutor. Rursus, si tu ipse tua volúntate nihil ageres, non vocaretur adiutor: adiutor enim aliquid agentem adiuvat. in yourself, immediately sent the helper, saying: If you are led by the spirit, you are not yet under the law. He who is under the law does not fulfill the law, but is oppressed by it, as David himself was by weapons. Then, if you are guided by the spirit, see who will help you achieve what you want. (Who?) Your helper, your protector, your hope, who trains your hand for fighting, and your fingers for war. Manifest are—says the Apostle—the works of the flesh; They are: fornications, impurities, idolatries, lusts, sorceries, grudges, dissensions, drunkenness, gluttonies and similar things; I tell you about them, as I already told you, that those who do them will not possess the kingdom of heaven. Therefore (they are under the law) not those who fight against them, but those who execute them. Well, when you fight, it is a work; and, when you defeat them, another; and, when you have peace and rest, a different one. Pay attention as I demonstrate these things with a few examples. Some gain arises, it pleases you; She contains a great fraud within herself, you like her, but you do not consent. See the struggle before you; it is still persuaded, it is still incited, it is still deliberated; Therefore he who fights is in danger. Let's see the fight, let's see what still remains. You disregarded justice by committing fraud: you were defeated. You despised the gain by submitting to justice: you won. There are three things in this: I grieve for the defeated, I fear for the one who fights, I rejoice with the victor. But did he who wins, by chance, act in himself in such a way that money did not tempt him in any way, or did it not incite in him any movement of pleasure, although conquerable, although of little?

importance, although not only does he not consent to it, but he does not even deign to fight with it? There is always some loving movement. This flattery and that enemy no longer fight nor prevail; However, they are present and dwell in mortal flesh as if they no longer lived, those who will not exist. Later everything will be transformed into victory; However, now the body is certainly dead through sin, and therefore sin is in the body even though sin does not reign. However, the spirit has life through justice. And if he who raised Christ from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies by his Spirit who dwells in you. There will be no one to fight or flatter; everything will yield to peace. For one nature does not fight against another contrary nature, but rather like husband and wife in the house. If they disagree among themselves, it is a dangerous and annoying suffering; If the woman wins and the husband is defeated, there will be a disordered peace; On the contrary, if the woman submits to the husband who rules, peace will be just; However, it is not one of one nature and another of another, because woman was made from man. It is your flesh, it is your wife, it is your companion; call it what you want; It is necessary that you subdue it, and, if you fight, fight so that it takes advantage. It is appropriate that the inferior submit to the superior, so that he who wants the inferior to be subjected to him also submits to the superior. Recognize order, seek peace. You to God, the flesh to you. What is fairer, what is more beautiful? You to the Eldest, to you the youngest. Manifesta enim sunt, inquit, opera carnis, quae sunt fornicationes, immunditiae, indolorum servitus, luxuria, veneficia, contenciones, inimicitiae, ebrietates, comessationes, et his similia; quae praedico vobis, sicut praedixi, quoniam qui talia agunt, regnum Dei non possidebunt (Gal 5:17-21). Non qui adversus talia confligunt, sed qui talia agunt. Cum enim confligis, aliud est opus; cum vincis, aliud opus est; cum pacem et requiem habes, aliud opus est. Corusca coruscationem, et disperges eos; Emitte sagittas tuas, et conturbabis eos. Emitte manum tuam ex alto; et exempt me, et erue me from here multis. His sound was heard throughout the earth, and his words were heard in the ends of the earth. Then, when these heavens issued their voices throughout the earth and worked miracles, the Lord flashing and thundering from them with miracles and commandments, it was thought that gods came down from heaven to mortals, because some of the Gentiles, believing this, wanted to offer sacrifices to them. But when they saw that undue honor was being paid to them, terrified and detesting and correcting those who erred in this way, to show them the disturbance of their spirit they tore their clothes and said: Why do you do this? We are also passive men like you. And they began, supported by these words, to commend the excellence of our Lord Jesus Christ; They humbled themselves to magnify God, because they were heavens inclined so that God could descend. Then bow your heavens and come down. This is how it happened. Touch the mountains, and they will smoke, that is, the proud mountains, the earthly excellencies, the swollen dignities. Touch, he says, touch these mountains, give these mountains some of your grace, and they will smoke, because they will confess their sins. The smoke of confessed sins will also bring forth the tears of the humbled proud. Touch the mountains, and they will smoke. As long as they are not touched, they think they are great. But they must say: "You are the great, O Lord!" The mountains must also say: You alone are Most High over all the earth. 13 (v.6}. But there are some conspirators together against the Lord and against his Christ. They have joined together, they have conspired. Make the lightning shine, and you will dispel them. Increase your miracles,

and their conspiracy will disappear. Shine the lightning, and you will dispel them. Terrified by miracles, they will not dare to act against you, since, overwhelmed by the miracles themselves, they will hesitate. Who is this so powerful? Who is this who is thus exalted and whose name has so much influence? When they say: "Who is this," it is because they must believe, since you made miracles shine and dispersed their perverse community. Send your arrows, and you will trouble them. Sharp arrows of powerful; That is, your precepts, your sayings, will hurt his heart. Send your arrows, and you will trouble them. Let those who are poorly healthy be wounded so that those who are well wounded may heal and be established in the Church, in the Body of Christ; Say with the Church: I am wounded by charity. Send your arrows, and you will trouble them. 14 [v.7]. Send your hand (your power) from above. Then what? Finally, what? How does the Body of Christ overcome? With celestial help. For the Lord himself will come with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God he will come down from heaven: the same Savior of the Body, the hand of God. Send your hand from above and bring me out and deliver me from many waters. What does out of many waters mean? From among the numerous towns. From what towns? Of the strangers, of the infidels: both those who fight outside and those who insinuate within. Take me out of the many waters in which you exercised me, in which you made me roll to rid myself of the filth. This is that water of contradiction of which the book of Numbers speaks: Bring me out and deliver me from many waters.

Nam quidam ex Gentibus hoc putantes, eis etiam sacrificere voluerunt. Tune illi videntes sibi deferri indebitum honorem, et expavescentes, et detestantes, et eos qui sic errabant correctientes, ut ostenderent eis motum animi sui, consciderunt ropa sua, et dixerunt, Quid hoc jachis? Homines et nos sumus passibiles, sicut et vos. Incline ergo lower your hands, and descend. Factum est. Tange montes, et fumigahunt: montes superbos, elationes terrenas, túmidas granditates: tange, inquit, tange istos montes; de gratia tua da istis montibus: et fumigahunt; quia fatebuntur peccata sua. Fumus confitentium peccatorum extorquebit et lacrymas humiliatorum superborum. Tange montes, et fumigahunt. Quamdiu non tacti, magni sibi videntur. Dicturi sunt, Tu magnus, Domine (Ps 47,2); dicturi sunt et montes, Tu solus altissimus super omnem terram (Ps 82,19). 13 [v.6]. Emitte sagittas tuas, et conturbabis eos. 14 [v.7]. Emitte manum tuam ex alto. Who is posting? quid in fine? Quomodo vincit corpus Christi? Caelesti adiutorio. Veniet enini ipse Dominus in voce archangeli, et in tuba Dei descendet de cáelo (1 Thess 4,15); ipse Salvator corporis, manus Dei. Emitte manum tuam ex alto; et exempt me, et erue me from here multis. What is it, multis from here? Of populis multis. Quibus populis? Alienigenis, infidelibus, sive foris oppugnantibus, sive intus insidiantibus. Exempt me from here multis, in quibus me exercebas, in quibus me ad exuendum a sordibus you returned. Haec est illa aqua contradictionis (Num 20:13). Exempt me, et erue me from here multis.

15 [v. 8]. Let us now hear something said about these mighty waters from which God delivers the Body of his Christ, from which God delivers the weakness of David. What does many waters mean? What did you say, lest I understand something else by these waters? What did you call "many waters"? Listen to what I said below: From the hand (of power) of strange children. Listen, brothers, among whom we are, among whom we live and from among whom we wish to be taken out. Their mouths spoke vanity. Even today, all of you, if you had not gathered to hear the word of God and were currently mixed with them, how many vanities you would not hear! His mouth spoke vanity. In short, when, when they speak vanity, will they hear you speak truth? His mouth speaks vanity, and his right hand is the right hand of iniquity. 16 [v. 9]. What (should you say) you being among them with the bag containing the five stones? The same law that you symbolized in the five stones also means something else. Oh God, I will sing you a new song. The new song is the song of grace; the new song is the song of the new man; The new song is the song of the New Testament. I will sing to you - he says - a new song. But lest you think that grace departs from the law, whereas the law is rather fulfilled by grace, he says: With ten-stringed psaltery I will praise you. With ten-stringed psaltery: with the law of the ten commandments; with it I will praise you, with it I will make you happy, with it I will sing to you the new song, because the full perfection of the law is charity. For the rest, those who do not have charity can carry 15 [v.8]. Audiamus iam de istis aquis multis, a quibus eruet Deus corpus Christi sui, a quibus eruet Deus humilitatem David. What is it, multis from here? Quid dixisti, ne aquae aliter intelligantur? Why did you give these fines? Quid dixi, audi. De manu filiorum alienorum. Audite, fratres, inter quos simus, Inter quos vivamus, a quibus erui desideremus. Quorum os locutum est vanitatem. Hodie vos omnes, si non ad haec divina spectacula verbi Dei congregati essetis, et eis hac hora permixti viveretis, quantas vanitates audiretis! Quorum os locutum est vanitatem. Quando denique loquentes illi vanitatem, audirent vos loquentes veritatem?

Quorum os locutum est vanitatem, et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis. 16 [v.9]. Quid tu inter eos cum vase pastorali, habente quinqué lapides? Dec mihi aliter: eamdem Legem quam significasti quinqué lapidibus, significa et aliter. Deus, canticum novum cantabo tibi. Canticum novum, gratiae est; canticum novum, hominis novi est; canticum novum, Testamenti Novi est. Cantabo tibi, inquit, canticum novum. Sed ne putes gratiam a Lege discedere, cum magis per gratiam Lex impleatur: In psalterio decem chordarum psallam tibi. In psalterio decem chordarum, in Lege decem praeceptorum: ibi tibi psallam, ibi tibi gaudeam, ibi tibi cantem canticum novum; quia plenitudo Legis charitas est (Rom 13:10). Caeterum qui non habent charitatem, portare psalterium possunt, canta-

the psaltery, but they can't sing. "I, then," he says, "among the waters of contradiction I will sing to you a new song and the waters of contradiction will never stop my psaltery from being heard with their noise." With the ten-stringed psaltery I will praise you. 11 [v. 10-11]. That gives health to kings. To the smoking mountains. Who redeems his servant David. You know David; be you David. Will his servant David redeem me? What redeems Christ from? What redeems the Body of Christ from? Deliver me from the evil sword. It was not enough to say of the sword; that's why he added evil. There is certainly a benign sword. What is benign Spain? That of which the Lord says: I did not come to bring peace to the earth, but a sword, for it will separate the faithful from the unbelievers, the children from the parents, and divide the other kinships, cutting away the rot with the sword and healing the members of Christ. There is, then, a benign double-edged sword: that of the New and Old Testament, very powerful in both cuts due to the narration of past events and the promise of future ones. This sword is benign, since through it God speaks the truth. The other is evil, since through it they speak vanity. Then deliver me from the evil sword. The teeth of the sons of men are weapons and arrows; and his tongue, a sharp sword. Deliver me from this evil sword. What he now called a sword, he formerly called many waters. Deliver me from many waters. Therefore, what I called "many waters", the same thing I now call "sword." Finally, after having spoken of the many waters, continuing, he says: From the hand (of power) re non possunt. Ego itaque, inquit, inter aquas contradictionis cantabo tibi canticum novum; et nunquam strepitu suo facient aquae contradictionis, ut obtumescat psalterium meum: In psalterio decem chordarum psallam tibi. 17 [v.10,11]. Qui dat salutem regibus: iam fumarantibus montibus. Qui redeemed David servum suum. Agnoscitis David, estote David. Unde redeemed David servum suum? Where did Christum redeem? Where did I redeem Corpus Christi? Of evil gladio erue me. Of gladio, non sufficit; addit, evil. Procul dubio est gladius benignus. Quis est gladius benignus?

De quo Dominus dicit: Non veni pacem mittere in terram, sed gladium (Mt 10,34). Separaturus enim erat fideles ab infidelibus, filios a parentibus, et caeteras necessitudines dirempturus, gladio putredinem abscindente, membra autem Christi sanante. Est ergo benignus gladius bis acutus, utroque acumine praepotens, Veteris et Novi Testamenti, narratione praeteritorum et promissione Futurum. Est ergo iste gladius benignus: ille autem malignus est quo illi loquuntur vanitatem; quia benignus est, quo Deus loquitur veritatem. Ergo, A malignant gladio erue me. Filii quippe hominum dentes eorum arma et sagittae, et lingua eorum gladius acutus (Ps 56,5): ab hoc gladio maligna erue me. Quem díxit moda gladium, ipsas superius díxit aquas fines: Erue me de aquis multis. Quas dixi aquas fines, ipsum dico gladium malignum. Denique de aquis multis

of strange children, whose mouth speaks vanity. Well then: that you may know that he refers to these, also, after having said: Deliver me from the evil sword, he continued: and bring me out of the hand of the children of strangers, whose mouth spoke vanity, just as in the previous verses. Likewise what follows: Their right hand is the right hand of iniquity, he stated above when he called them "many waters." Finally, so that you would not think that the many waters were good, he made them known in the evil sword. Then now he declares what he recorded: His mouth speaks vanity, and his right hand is the right hand of iniquity. What vanity spoke his mouth? How is his right hand the right hand of iniquity? 18 [v.12]. Your children are like new plants rooted in their youth. He intends to expose his prosperity. Listen, children of light, children of peace; Pay attention, children of the Church, members of Christ; Pay attention to those whom he calls foreigners, to whom he calls strange children, to whom he calls waters of contradiction. Pay attention, I beg you, because among these you are in danger, among their tongues you fight against the desires of your flesh, among their tongues, placed at the disposal of the devil, with which he fights, you maintain the fight: Not against flesh and blood, but against the princes and powers, and against the rulers of the world of this darkness, that is, of the wicked. Pay attention so that you may discern well; Pay attention, lest it happen that you consider true happiness what weak or evil men desire for themselves. See, brothers, he called you strange sons, many waters and an evil sword. See the vanity they speak, and beware of speaking such

thing and beware of imitating them by speaking such words. His mouth speaks vanity, and his right hand is the right hand of iniquity. What iniquity did his mouth speak? And what right of theirs is the right of iniquity? Hear: Your children are like new plants rooted in their youth; their daughters, groomed and adorned, are like simulacrums of a temple; Their pantries are full and overflow from one to another; His sheep are so fertile that they multiply in their outings; his oxen are fattened; and there is no breach or exit in the fence, nor shouting in its streets. Isn't this happiness? I ask the children of the kingdom of heaven, I question the lineage of the eternal resurrection, I question the Body of Christ, the members of Christ, the temple of God: Does happiness consist in having healthy sons, adorned daughters, stocked pantries, abundant livestock, in not suffering any destruction, I'm not saying in a wall, but not even in a fence; in not having tumult and shouting in the squares, but peace, abundant provisions in the houses and in the cities? Isn't this happiness? Should the righteous flee from it? Do you not also find the house of the righteous abounding in all these things and full of this happiness? Did not Abraham's house abound in gold, silver, children, servants, and animals? Did not the holy patriarch Jacob, fleeing from the presence of Esau, his brother, to Mesopotamia, become rich in service, and give thanks to the Lord his God, because he first crossed the Jordan carrying a staff with all his possessions, and now returns with great abundance of livestock and children? What will we say? Isn't this happiness? Let's grant that yes, but despicable.

cum dixisset; secutus est, De manu filiorutn alienorum, quorum os locutum est vanitatem. Et ut noveris ipsos dici; cum et hic dixisset. Of evil gladio erue me, secutus est, Et exempt me de manu filiorum alienorum, quorum os locutum est vanitatem: similiter sicut ibi. Et quod sequitur, Dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis; hoc et supra posuerat, quando eos dixerat aquas fines. Tu enim ne aquas fines bonas putares, exposuit eas in gladio maligna. Nunc ergo exponat quod dixit, Quorum os locutum est vanitatem, et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis. Quam vanitatem locutum est os eorum? et quomodo dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis? 18 [v.12-14]. Quorum filii ipsorum velut novellae constabilitae in iuventute sua. Felicitatem ipsorum vult enumerare. Attendite, filii lucis, filii pacis; attendite, filii Ecclesiae, membra Christi; attendite quos dicat aliens, quos dicat filios alíenos, quos dicat aquas contradictíonís, quos dicat gladium malignum. Attendite, obsecro; quia inter istos periclitamini, inter horum linguas adversus carnis vestrae desideria dimicatis: inter horum linguas positas in manu diaboli, de quibus pugnat, colluctationem habetis, non adversus carnem et sanguinem, sed adversus principes et potestates, et rectores mundi tenebrarum harum (Eph 6,12), hoc est, iniquorum. Attendite, ut discernatis vos; attendite, ne putetis veram felicitatem esse, quam sibi optant nomines aut infirmi aut maligni. Ecce,

fratres, certe filios alíenos dixit, certe aquas fines, certe gladium malignum. Vídete vanitatem quam loquuntur, et cávete ne taha loquamini, cávete ne talia loquentes imitemini. Quorum os locutum est vanitatem, et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis. Quam vanitatem locutum est os eorum, et quae dextera eorum iniquitatis est dextera? Audi: Quorum filii ipsorum velut novellae constabilitae a iuventute sua; filiae eorum compositae, et omatae sicut similarity templi: cellaria eorum plena, eructantia ex hoc in hoc: oves eorum jecundae, multiplicantes in egressibus suis; boves eorum crasst: non est ruina sepis, nec exitus; ñeque clamor in plateis eorum. Ergo, isn't there, congratulations? Interrogo filios regni caelorum, interrogo progeniem resurrectionis in aeternum, interrogo Corpus Christi, membra Christi, templum Dei: Ergo non est ista felicitas, habere filios incólumes, filias ornatas, plena cellaria, abundantia pécora, nullam ruinam, non dico parietis, sed nec sepis; nullum tumultum et clamorem in plateis, sed quietem, pacem, abundantiam,copiam rerum in domibus, in civitatíbus? Ergo, isn't there, congratulations? a u t debent eam iusti defugere? aut non invenis et domum iusti abundantm rebus his omnibus, plenam ista congratulate yourself? Non erat domus Abrahae abundans auro, argento, filiis, familia, pecoribus? (Gen 12:5; et 12:2-6). Níonne Iacob sanctus patriarcha fugiens a facie Esau fratris sui in Mesopotamiam, serviens ditatus, regressus est, et egit gratias Domino Deo su o, quia in virga sua transitiit S.Ag. 22

What does "despicable" mean? Fleeting, temporary, mortal, earthly. I don't want you to take refuge in it, but I even less want you to judge it as true. These are not evil and vain because they have these things in abundance, but because what should have been considered on the left, they considered on the right. Therefore his right is right, of iniquity; That is why their tongue spoke vanity, since they placed on the right what they should have placed on the left. What should they have placed on the right? To God, eternity, the endless years of God, of which it is said: And your years will have no jin: here is the right, here our desire must rest. Let us temporarily use the left and eternally desire the right. If riches flow, do not set your heart on them. If you put your heart in the riches that pass, you have as right what is left. Correct you, recognize the wisdom that embraces you, to which it was said: He placed his left under my head and with his right embraced me. Consider the holy love songs, consider the Song of Songs of the heavenly wedding of Christ and the Church. What does the wife say about the husband? He placed his left under my head and hugged me with his right. He placed the left one under his head, and the right one on top of it. The arm of the hugger is placed above, above the head, and the left arm is placed below the head. His left—he says—under my head. He will not abandon me in temporal needs; However, he will place the left one under the head; He will not place it above the head, but under the head, so that its right hand embraces me, promising me eternal life. So, fluvium, et regressus est cura tanta abundantia pecorum atque filiorum? (ib. 31,18; et 32,7-10). Quid dicimus? Isn't this there, congratulations? Sit licet, sed sinistra. Quid est, left. Temporalis, mortalis, corporalis. Nolo illam iam diffugias, sed ñeque dexteram putes. Non enim isti ideo maligni, ideo vani, quia his abundabant; sed quia id quod sinistrum esse debuit, in dextera dondebant. Ideo et dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis; ideo os eorum locutum est vanitatem: quia hoc in dextera posuerunt, quod in sinistra habere debuerunt. Quid enim in dextera will I put debuerunt? Deum, aeternitatem, annos Dei non deficient, de quibus dicitur, Et anni tui non deficient (Ps 101,28): ibi dextera, ibi esse debent desiderium nostrum. Sinistra utamur ad tempus, dexteram desideremus in aeternum. Divitiae si fluant, ne apponatis cor (Ps 61,11).

Si enim divitiis fluentibus cor apposueritis, quod sinistrum est, dextrum facietis. Correct yourself, agnoscite sapientiam amplectentem vos; cui dictum est, Sinistra eius sub capite meo, et dextera eius complectetur me (Song 2:6). Videte amatoria sancta cantica; videte Cantica canticorum, nuptiarum caelestium Christi et Ecclesiae. Quid dicit sponsa de sponso? Sinistra eius sub capite meo, et dextera eius complectetur me. Sinistra sub capite, dextera super caput. Amplectentis enim desuper brachium super caput, sinistra autem subter caput. Sinistra, inquit, eius sub capite meo. Non enim me deseret in temporalibus necessariis: sed tamen ipsa sinistra sub capite erit; non capiti

the left will be under the head if the right is above the head. In this way what was written to Timothy is fulfilled: Having promise—he says—of the present life and the future. What promise do we have in this present life? The left one under the head. What in the future life? His right that embraces me. Do you look for the necessary things in time? Seek first the kingdom of heaven, that is, the right hand, and all other things will be given to you in addition. "You will have here," he says, "glory and riches, and in the future age eternal life. With the left hand I will support your weakness and with the right hand I will crown your perfection." Perhaps the apostles, who abandoned all their possessions or who distributed everything they had among the poor, were in this world without wealth? So how is that promise of the left fulfilled: You will receive seven times more in this world? He promised multiplication. And truly, what does the man of God lack? The infidel has one or a few houses; However, all the riches in the world belong to the faithful man. See, therefore, his left hand full under his head: He will receive in this world seven times more. He sees his right hand embracing him: And in the future century, eternal life. It is rightly said in another place about the same wisdom: On its right are the years of life, and on its left are honor and riches. 19 [v.15}. Then why are these boastful? Why did his mouth speak vanity? For his right hand is the right hand of iniquity. I do not blame them because their children are like new plants praeponetur, sed erit sub capite; ut dextera eius complectatur me, pollicens vitam aeternam. Ita enim sinistra sub capite, si dextera super caput; impleturque quod ad Timotheum scriptum est: Promissionem habens vitae praesentis etfuturee (1 Tim 4,8). Promissionem, inquit, habens vitae praesentis etfuturae. Quid in praesenti? Sinistra sub capite. What in the future? Dextera eius complectetur me. Tempori necessaria quaeritis? Quaerite primum regnum Dei, id est, dexteram; et haec omnia apponentur vobis (Mt 6:33). Habebitis hic, inquit, et divitias et gloriam, et in future saeculo vitam aeternam: et sinistra continebo iniirmitatem vestram, et dextera coronabo perfectionem vestram. An forte Apostoli relinquentes omnia sua, aut pauperibus quod habebant distribuentes, sine divitiis in hoc saeculo remanserunt? Et ubi est illa promissio sinistrae: Accipiet in hoc saeculo septies tantum? Multiplicationem promisit. Et revera, quid desit homini Dei?

Si quis forte infidelis est, unam domum aut paucas habet: Fidelis hominis totus mundus divitiarum est (Prov 17,6, apud LXX). Vide sinistram eius plenam sub capite: Accipiet in hoc saeculo septies tantum. Vide dexteram complectentem: Et in future saeculo vitam aeternam (Mt 19,29). Merito et alio loco de ipsa Sapientia dicitur: In dextera eius anni vitae, et in sinistra eius divitiae et honor (Prov 3,16). 19 [v.15]. Unde ergo isti vaniloqui? quare vanitatem locutum est os eorum? Quia dextera eorum dextera iniquitatis. Non ergo eos arguo,

rooted in youth, nor because their daughters are adorned like simulacrums of a temple, nor because the abundance of other expired goods and earthly fatherhood entered through the doors of their house. Why do I blame them? For they said: Blessed is the people that possesses these things. Oh men who speak vanity! They called the people who possess these things blessed. They lost the true right by being evil and perverse; They provided themselves, inverting the terms, with the benefits of God. Oh evil ones, oh boastful ones, oh strange children! They called the people who possess these goods blessed. They placed on the right what was on the left: They called the people who possess these things blessed. What do you say, David? What do you say, Body of Christ? What do you say, members of Cris. to? What do you say, not strange children, but of God? Since the boastful and strange children said that the people who possess these goods are blessed, what do you say? Blessed are the people who have the Lord as their God. Have left, but on the left; desire the right, but place it on the right. On the left were those who, when they were hungry, gave him food; When he was thirsty, they gave him something to drink; When he was a guest, they welcomed him into their house, and, being naked, they dressed him. They took all this from the left and turned it into works of the right to place it on the right. The boastful and strange sons said that the people who possess these things were blessed. You say with me: Blessed are the people who have the Lord as their God. quia filii eorum velut novellae constabilitae a iuventute sua, nec quia filiae eorum ornatae sicut similarityo templi, nec quia caetera abundantia et pax terrena aderat eis: sed quare arguo? Beatum dixerunt populum cui haec sunt. O loquentes homines vanitatem! Beatum dixerunt populum cui haec sunt. Perdiderunt veram dexteram; maligni, perversi, benefit Dei inverse vestierunt. Majesty and goodness- of God S ALMO
[MAJESTY AND GOODNESS OF GOD] SERMON

1. I desired to praise the Lord with you; and as He has deigned to grant it to me, so that the praise we give Him preserves its condition, lest by any imperfection it offends the one who praises, let us investigate the surest path of praise in the divine Scripture, and thus, by not deviating from this path, we will not incline either to the right or to the left. I hear your charity say: "So that God may be perfectly praised by man, God praised himself; and because he deigned to praise himself, for the same reason, man found a way to praise him, since it cannot be said to God what was said to man: Let not your mouth praise you, since praising man is arrogance, and praising God is mercy." Take advantage of loving whom we praise, since, by loving the good, we become better. Therefore, since he knows that it is profitable for us to love him, he praised himself and became kind; and in this he looked for our good, since he became kind. Then our hearts are exhorted to praise Him, for He filled His servants with His Spirit to praise Him; And since his Spirit praises Him in his servants, what else does he do if not praise himself? This psalm begins like this: 2 [v.l].
I will exalt you, my God, my king, and I will bless PSALMUS

1. Laudare vobiscum Dominum desideravimus: et quoniam hoc will concede dignitus est; ut laus quam illi dicimus habeat ordinem suum, ne forte aliquo excessu quem laudat offendat, melius iter laudis in Scriptura Dei quaerimus, ne ab ipsa via, nec in dexteram nec in sinistram digrediamur. Audeo enim dicere Charitati vestrae; ut bene ab homine laudetur Deus, laudavit se ipse Deus; et quia dignitatus est laudare se, ideo invenit homo quemadmodum laudet eum. The title of the psalm is as follows: Praise for David, But since David was called the one who came to us from the lineage of David, and He is our King, who governs us and brings us into his kingdom, by saying: Praise for David, it is understood praise for Christ himself. For Christ, according to the flesh, comes from David, and therefore is the son of David; but, according to divinity, he is the Creator and Lord of David. Finally, also the Apostle, honoring the first people of God, from where came the same apostles who believed and the many churches that executed in many thousands of men what a rich man now heard in the gospel, and turned away saddened, that is, that they sold everything they had and distributed it to the poor and sought the perfection of the Lord; Praising, I repeat, this first people, he says thus: Whose fathers, from whom descends Christ according to the flesh, who is God above all things worthy to be blessed forever. Therefore as Christ proceeds from them in regard to the flesh, therefore he is David; and since He is God above all things, worthy to be blessed forever, therefore I will exalt you, my God and my king, and I will bless—he says—your name in the world and in the world of the world. In the century it is the same as "here"; and forever and ever, forever. Then begin to praise now if you are to praise forever. He who does not want to praise in the journey of this sigium will be silent when the world of the century arrives. Hence in the following verses he said, more or less, this.

3 [v.2}. Every day—he says—I will bless you. Not a day will pass without blessing you. No wonder you bless your God on the joyful day. But what will happen if he encounters some sad day, as human things are, as the multitude of scandals and the multitude of temptations arise? What will happen if something unfortunate is offered to man? Will you stop praising God? Will you stop blessing your Creator? If you cease, you lied when you said: Every day I will bless you, Lord. If you continue to praise, even if it seems to you that things are going badly for you on the unfortunate day, it will go well with your God. While you may rejoice, it is undoubtedly transitory; But if you rejoice in the Lord, your God, you will hear the Scripture, which says: Rejoice in the Lord. You will rejoice all the more firmly, the more firmly is what you are to rejoice in. If you rejoice in money, you fear the thief; But if you rejoice in God, what do you fear? May someone take God away from you? No one will take God away from you if you don't let him. God is not like this light that shines in the sky. We do not approach this material light when we want, since it does not shine everywhere. Because of our weakness, it happens that during the winter we like to enjoy it; but now, during the summer, you see that we rather look for the place where this light does not penetrate; However, when you are in your God and delight in the light of his truth, you do not seek the place by which you approach Him, but you draw near and separate by conscience. What was said: Draw near to Him, and you will be enlightened, it was said to the spirit, not to the vehicle; It was said to the affection, not to the feet. Furthermore, abiding in Him, you will not endure the heat, for the Spirit will encourage you and under His wings you will wait. 4. the children! What was reserved for them perished and those for whom it was reserved perished; However, the one who gave him those and these did not perish. The children perished in the present century to be recognized and received in the future. However, that holy man, possessing something else in which he rejoiced and in whom the reality that we have now commemorated was fulfilled: Every day I will bless you, by chance, because that day in which he lost everything shone unhappily, that is why the internal light in his heart went out? He remained in that light and said: The Lord gave it to me, the Lord took it from me; As it pleased Him, so it was done; blessed be the name of the Lord. Then he praised every day who also praised on such a sad day. A brief teaching is that you always praise God and with a right and not a false heart (say): I will bless God at all times; His praise will always be in my mouth. This is a brief teaching, that you know that he gives mercifully when he gives and that he takes away mercifully when he takes away, and do not think that he who gives caresses you so that you do not faint that he separates you from his mercy; or the one who corrects you, being arrogant, so that you do not perish. Then you praise him both in his gifts and in his punishments. The praise of the punisher is medicine for the wound. Every day—he says—I will bless you. Bless, brothers, without exception every day; In everything that happens to you, bless God. He ensures that nothing happens to you that you cannot bear. For the same reason, you should fear when things go well for you, because you should not believe that you will never be tempted. If you were never tempted, you would never be tested. Is it not better to be tempted and tested than to be tempted? nec tamen periit qui et illud et illos dedit. Et ípsi filii praesenti saeculo perierunt, agnoscendi et recipiendi in the future. Ule tamen vir habens aliud unde gauderet, in quo verum erat quod moda commemoravimus, Ver singulos dies benedicam te; numquid quia ille dies quo totum perierat, tristis illuxit, ideo lux interior in corde defecit? Stetit quippe in illa luz, et ait: Dominus dedit, Dominus abstulit; sicut Domino placuit, ita factum est: sit nomen Domini benedictum (Iob 1). Let us see, then, the things he did in this world: those that are known to us, those that are evident to us, since his immense goodness and endless greatness, how many others he did that we do not know! Let us turn our gaze to the sky, and from the sun, the moon and the stars we direct it back to the earth. This is the space through which our gaze passes. For who directs the gaze not only of the flesh, but of the mind, beyond the heavens? Let us therefore praise God for the works known to us fueris, non ipsius sis? Audi Apostolum promittentem tibi securitatem: Sive vivimus, Domino vivimus; sive morimur, Domino morimur: sive ergo vivimus, sive morimur, Domini sumus. Et unde factum est ut eius sis et mortuus? here, since His invisible ones are visible from the foundation of the world by which they have been made. Generation and generation will praise your works. Every generation will praise your works. Perhaps it was said generation and generation for every generation, since generation and generation was not only meant to indicate the time in which the number of all (human) generations elapses, but rather the repetition of the speaker leaves the mind free to think about infinity. For you see that this generation that now lives in the flesh, and that is to pass away as it came, praises the works of God; and whoever makes way for what follows him also praises the works of God; and after her will come another, and until the end of the world, how many generations there are! Well, indicating this (the total generation), he says: The generation and the generation will praise your works. Or did he intend to insinuate through this repetition two different generations, since in the present generation we are children of God, and in the future we will be children of the resurrection? Scripture called us "sons of the resurrection," and called the resurrection itself "regeneration"; In Saint Matthew it says this: In regeneration, when the Son of man sits on the throne of his glory, neither men nor women will marry, being already children of the resurrection. Then generation and generation will praise your works. Now, when we live in this mortality, we praise the works of God; and, if we praise being in the bonds of the flesh, how we will praise Him crowned! Therefore now, in the present generation, let us attend to these works of the Lord, in whose praise it is said: The generation and the

generation will praise your works, since your greatness has no limit. It is good to contemplate your works so that you who do such things may be praised. 7. And they will publish your power. They will praise your works in order to manifest your power. At school, praise is offered to children; the things that should be praised, and that God made, are proposed; praise of the sun, the sky, and the earth is proposed to man; and, to refer to the smallest things, the praise of the rose, of the laurel, is proposed. All these things are works of God. They are proposed, accepted, praised; The works are published and no mention of the Creator is made. I want the Creator to be praised in the works, because I do not consider the panegyrist ungrateful. Do you praise what he did and do not mention the one who did it? Don't you understand that if it weren't so immense, you wouldn't have anything to praise? What is praised in what you see? The beauty, the usefulness, some virtue, some power of these things. If you delight in beauty, what is more beautiful than the Maker? If usefulness, what is more useful than Him who made all things? If power is praised, what is more powerful than Him by whom all things were made, and by whom, when made, they are not abandoned, but ruled and governed? Therefore generation after generation does not praise you in your servants when they praise your works, like silent chattering hills, who praise the creature and forget the Creator. How does he praise you? And they will publish your power. In the praises of your works they will publish your power. These holy and good faithful panegyrists, true preachers, recognized by grace, when they praise the works of God,

opera eius, laudemus eum per opera eius. Invisibilia enim eius, a constitutione mundi, per ea quae facta sunt intellecta conspiciuntur (ib. 1,20). Generatio et generatio laudabit opera tua. You have to emigrate from here, since, daily waiting for your departure, you will convert in some time. In this he manifested his great mercy. If he had appointed the day to everyone, he would multiply the sins due to security. Then he gave you hope of forgiveness so that you would no longer sin in despair. Both hope and despair are to be feared in sins. Hear the voice of the desperate, increasing sins; and listen also to the voice of the confident, increasing them; and, likewise, how the providence and mercy of God helps every voice. Hear the desperate man: "I must already be condemned," he says, "why don't I do everything I want?" Hears the same confident: "God's mercy is great; when I convert, he will forgive me all my sins. Why don't I do whatever I want?" One despairs and the other waits to sin. Both things are to be feared, both are very dangerous. Woe to despair! Woe to perverse confidence! How does God's mercy meet both dangers, both evils? What do you say, that, in desperation, you wanted to sin? "I must already be condemned. Why don't I do what I want?" Hear the Scripture: I do not want the death of the wicked, but that he convert and live. This voice of God leads to hope. But another scheme must be feared, lest, because of hope, he should sin more. What were you saying, that, by trusting, you sin more? "When I am converted, God will forgive me for all my crimes; therefore, I will do whatever I please." Hear also the Scripture: Do not delay in converting to God; Do not defer it from day to day, for suddenly his wrath will come and in the time of vengeance he will lose you. Don't say:

I see that in the angels they confess their works to Him, since the angels are His works. Men are also his works, and when men confess to him, they confess their works to him. But do trees and stones have the voice of confession? Without a doubt they confess all their works. What are you saying? Also the land and the trees? All his works. If they all praise him, why shouldn't they all confess him? Confession is not only about sins, but also about praise. I say this so that, when you hear the word concession anywhere, you do not think that it is only about sins. This is believed to such an extent that, when one hears this word in divine discourses, one immediately becomes accustomed to hurting one's breasts. He sees that confession is also one of praise. Did our Lord Jesus Christ have sins? And yet he says: "Confíteor tibí": I confess to you, O Father! Lord of heaven and earth. This confession is one of praise. Therefore, how is confiteantur tibi Domine omnia opera tua to be understood? They praise you, Lord, all your works. The difficulty that was presented in the word confession now falls on praise, since, if the trees, the earth and any insensitive being cannot confess, because they lack the voice, they will not praise either, because they lack the voice to praise. But the three young men who walked among the harmless flames and who had time, not only to be burned, but also to praise God, did they not enumerate all the beings of creation, and they all said, starting from the

lests even to the terrestrials: Bless and sing hymns and praise him forever? See how they sing hymns of praise. However, let no one think that the insensitive rock or the animal world has a rational mind to know God. Those who believed this departed immensely from the truth. God created and ordered all things; To some he gave meaning, understanding and immortality, like the angels; to others, meaning, understanding and mortality, as to men; to others he gave bodily sense, but not understanding or immortality, like the beasts; To others he did not give meaning, understanding, or immortality, such as to herbs, trees, and stones; However, they themselves in their kind cannot falter, since he ordered the creature in certain degrees, from heaven to earth, from visible things to invisible things, from mortal things to immortal things. This concatenation of the creature, this most ordered beauty, rising from the lowest to the highest and descending from the highest to the lowest, never interrupted, but accommodated to disparate beings, all of it praises God. Why does she all praise God? Because, when you contemplate it and see it beautiful, you praise your God for it. The dumb earth has a voice, it has a face. You attend and see its face, its surface; you see its fertility, you see its vigor, you see how the seed germinates in it; how it often makes what was not sown in it sprout. You see this, and with your reflection you question it, since this inquisition is an interrogation. Well then; when, admired, you have investigated and scrutinized, and you have found the immense vigor, the great beauty, the sublime power,

Video quidem in Angelis confiten illi opera eius; etenim opera eius sunt Angeli: et homines opera eius sunt; et cum confiten tur illi homines, opera eius illi confitentur: numquid ligna et lapides vocem habent confessionis? Prorsus confiteantur ei omnia opera eius. What do you say? Et terra et ligna? Omnia opera eius. Si omnia laudant, cur non omnia confitentur? Confessio enim non peccatorum tantum dicitur, sed et laudis: ne forte ubicumque auditis confessionem, putetis iam non esse nisi peccati. Usque adeo enim hoc putatur, ut quando sonuerit de divinis eloquiis, continuo sit consuetudo pectora tundere. Audi quia est et laudis confessio. Numquid Dominus Iesus Christus habebat peccatum? Et tamen ait: Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine caeli et terrae (Mt 11,25). Confessio est ergo in laude. Proinde quid accipiendum, Confiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua? Laudent te omnia opera tua. Sed talis quaestio redit ad laudem, qualis erat in confessione. Si enim propterea confiten non poterunt terra, ligna et quaeque insensata, quia vocem non habent confitendi; ideo nec laudabunt, quia vocem non habent praedicandi. Nonne tamen omnia tres illi pueri enumerant, wandering inter flammas innoxias; quibus spatium erat, non solum non ardendi, sed etiam laudandi Deum? Omnibus dicunt a caelestibus usque ad terrena: Benedicite, bymnum dicite, et superexaltate eum in saecula

(Dan 3,20.90). Ecce quomodo dicunt hymnum. Nemo hoc sentiat, quod mutus lapis aut mutum animal habeat rationem intelligendi Deus: hoc qui putaverunt, multum a veritate aberraverunt. Deus ordinavit omnia, et fecit omnia: quibusdam dedit sensum, et intellectum, et immortalitatem, sicut Angelis; quibusdam dedit sensum et intellectum cum mortalitate, sicut hominibus; quibusdam dedit sensum corporis, nec intellectum, nec immortalitatem dedit, sicut pecoribus; quibusdam vero nec sensum, nec intellectum, nec immortalitatem, sicut herbis, lignis, lapidibus: tamen et ipsa in genere suo deesse non possunt, et gradibus quibusdam ordinavit creaturam, a terra usque ad caelum, a visibilibus ad invisibilia, a mortalibus ad immortalia. Ista contextio creaturae, ista ordinatissima pulchritudo, ab imis ad summa conscendens, a summis ad ima descendens, nusquam interrupta, sed dissimilibus temperata, tota laudat Deum. Quare ergo tota laudat Deum? Quia cum eamconsideras et pulchram vides, tu in illa laudas Deum. Vox quaedam est mutae terrae, species terrae. Attendis et vides eius speciem, vides eius fecunditatem, vides eius vires, quomodo concipiat semen, quomodo plerumque afferat quod non est seminatum: vides, et consideratione tua tanquam interrogas eam; et ipsa inquisitio interrogatio est. That they may make known to the children of men your power and the glory of the immense beauty of your kingdom, Your saints remember the glory of the immense beauty of your kingdom and the glory of the immense beauty. Beauty is that in which the saints rejoice, to whom it will be said: Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom? Where will they go from? Where will they go? See, brothers; If you can, think as much as you can about the beauty of that kingdom that is to come. Hence it is said in our prayer: Your kingdom come. We wish this kingdom to come; The saints preach that it is to come. Behold this world; It has beauty. How beautiful the earth, the sea, the air, the sky and the stars are! Don't all these things terrify everyone who considers them? Does this beauty not shine so brightly that it seems that no more beauty can be found? And yet, in this beautiful sura, in this almost ineffable beauty, live, live here with you the worms, the mice and all the animals that crawl; these live with you in this beauty. What is the beauty of the kingdom in which only the angels live with you? Therefore, it would have been too little to say the glory of beauty. For it could be said "the glory of the beauty of any species established in this world", whether on this verdant earth or now in the splendid sky; But through the words the glory of the "immense" beauty of your kingdom is recommended something that we do not yet see, that we believe not seen, that we believe we desire, for whose desire we endure all the inconveniences. Then there is an immense beauty of something; It loves me before seeing it so that, when it is seen, it possesses itself. 16 [v. 13]. Your kingdom. What do I call your kingdom? To the kingdom of habet decorem, et magnum decorem. Quandoquidem quidquid habet decorem, a te habet decorem; ipsum regnum tuum qualem decorem habet! What ibunt? Videte, brothers; et si potestis, quantum potestis, cogitate decorem regni illius quod venturum est; unde est in oratione nostra, Adveniat regnum tuum (ib. 6,10). Ipsum enim regnum optmus ut veniat; hoc regnum venturum sancti praedicant. Mundum istum attendite; decorem habet. Quem decorem habet terra, mare, aer, caelum, sidera! The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works. The Lord is faithful in all his words. What did he promise and not give? The Lord is faithful in all his words. Certainly he promised some things that he has not yet given; but he is believed for the things he gave, because the Lord is faithful in his word. We could believe him just by saying it, but he did not want to be believed through speech, but rather preferred to record it in writing. This is as if you were to say to someone to whom you promise something: "You don't believe me; I put it in writing." As one generation passes and another comes, and thus these centuries pass, mortals giving way to those who succeed them, for the same reason, the Scripture of God and a certain manuscript of his must have remained so that all who passed by could read it and retain the safe conduct of its promise. Men hesitate to believe him about the resurrection of the dead and the future century, which only remains to be fulfilled. to the one who fell. It already raised him to such a height that in his very serious wound, with which his entire body had been battered, he responded to the tempting wife, who the devil reserved to help him: You spoke like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the hands of the Lord, should we not endure evil? How he exalted him who had fallen! The Lord lifts up all those who fall. When the righteous fall, they will not be troubled, because the Lord holds their hand. And he raises up all the downcast: all those who belong to him, for God is opposed to the proud. 19 [v.15]. The eyes of all wait on you, and you give them food in due time. As if restoring the sick person in a timely manner, you give him when he should and what he should receive. So, sometimes you want to receive from Him, and He doesn't give. He who restores knows the time to give. Why do I say these things, brothers? So that, when perhaps someone, asking for something just or good from God, is not heard, since, if he asks for something unjust or bad, for his punishment he is heard, he should not be daunted, not faint when asking for something just and not being heard; Let your eyes wait for the food that He gives in opportune time, since, when He does not give, He does not give so that what He gives does not harm. Without a doubt, the Apostle was asking for nothing unjust when he prayed that the thorn of the flesh, the angel of Satan that slapped him, would be removed. He begged and did not receive, because he was still in the time to exercise his weakness, but not to receive food. My grace is sufficient for you, says the Lord, because strength is made perfect in weakness. The devil asked to tempt you, quam solam sibi diabolus reliquerat adiutricem: Locuta et tanquam una ex insipientibus mulieribus: si bona percepimus de manu Domini, mala non sustinebimus? (Iob 2,7-10). Quomodo confirmaverat decidentem! Confirmat Dominus omnes deciding. Cum deciderit, inquit, iustus non conturbabitur, quoniam Dominus confirmat manum eius (Ps 36,24). Et erigit omnes elisos: omnes ad se pertinent. Nam Deus superbis resistit (lac 4,6). 19 [v.15]. Oculi omnium in te sperant, et tu das escam illis in opportunitate. Prorsus tanquam reficiens aegrotum in opportunitate, quando debent accipere, tune das; et quod deben, hoc das. Itaque aliquando desideratur ab illo, et non dat: novit horam dandi, qui curat. Quare is dico, fratres?

He is just when he punishes and when he heals, since in Him there is no iniquity. Finally, all the saints who found themselves in the midst of tribulations first exalted the justice of God and then asked for his gifts. First they said, "That's just what you do." Quis est ergo qui dicit, Lauda, ​​anima mea, Dominum? Nihil invcnimus amplius in homine, quam carnem et animam: totus homo hoc est, spiritus et caro. An forte ipsa anima sibi dicit, et sibi quodammo imperat, et se exhortatur atque excitat? Quibusdam enim perturbationibus ex quadam sui parte fluitabat; ex quadam vero parte, quam vocant mentem rationalem, illam qua cogitat sapientiam, inhaerens Domino iam et sighs in illum, animadvertit quasdam suas inferior parts perturbari notibus saecularibus, et cupiditate quadam tierrarum desideriorum Iré in exteriora, relinquere interiorem Deum: revocat se ab exterioribus ad interiora, ab inferioribus ad superior, et dicit, Lauda, anima mea, Dominum. Quid tibi placet in saeculo?

Quid est quod vis laudare? quid est quod vis amare? Quacumque corporeis sensibus you become, occurrit tibi caelum, occurrit tibi terra: quod amas in terra, terrenum est; quidquid amas et in cáelo, corporeum est. Locate amas, et ubique laudas: quomodo laudandus est ille qui fecit ista quae laudas? Iam ergo diu occupata vixisti, et desideriorum diversitate verberata, pest carriers, saucia, insignia per amores multos, ubique inquieta, nusquam secura; colligere ad te ipsam: quidquid tibi foris placebat, quaere quem habeat auctorem, Nihil melius in terra, verbi gratia, quam hoc et
