liked outside. There is nothing better on earth than this and that, namely, gold, silver, animals, trees, foliage; think of all the earth. What is better in the sky than the sun, the moon and the stars? Think of all the sky. All these things together are exceedingly good, because God made all things exceedingly good. Everywhere (appears) the beauty of the work that reminds you of the Artificer. You marvel at the factory, you love the architect. Do not surrender to that which was made and turn away from Him who made it. For these things that took hold of you were made by Him inferior to you, and He made you inferior to Himself. If you cling to the higher, you will trample on the lower; On the contrary, if you separate yourself from your superior, these things will become a torment for you. Well, this is how it happened, my brothers. Man received a body for bondage, having God as Lord, and the body as his servant; Above him he has the Creator; below, that which was created inferior to it; But, the rational soul placed in an intermediate place, it received the order or law to unite with the superior and to rule or govern the inferior; but she cannot govern the inferior if she is not governed by the superior. Therefore, being carried away by the inferior, she abandoned the better. In this way she cannot govern what she governed, because she did not want to be governed by who she was. Then stand back now and praise. The soul, through the rational mind, gives itself advice from the divine light, by which it conceived the eternally stable ruling of its Creator. There he reads something worthy of being feared, praised, loved, desired and desired; It does not yet possess it, it has not yet achieved it, since, dazzled by a certain lightning, it is not so vigorous that illud remains: aurum, argentum, animalía, arbores, amoenitates, totam terram cogita. Quid melius in cáelo solé, luna, sideribus? Totum caelum cogita. Omnia is simul bona valde, quia fecit Deus omnia bona valde. Undique pulchritudo operis, quae tibi commendat artificem. Miraris fabrícam, ama fabricatorem. Non occuperis in eo quod factum est, et recedas ab illo qui fecit. Haec enim quibus occuparis, sub te fecit, quia sub seipso te fecit. If haerebis superiori, calcabis inferiora; si autem recedes a superiori, ista tibi in supplicium convertentur.

Sic enim factum est, fratres mei: accepit homo corpus tanquam in famulatum, Deum autem Dominum habens, servum corpus, habens supra se Conditorem, infra se quod sub illo conditum est; in medio quodam loco rationalis anima constituta, legem accepit, haerere superiori, regere inferiorem. Regere non potest inferiorem, nisi regatur a meliore. Trahitur ab inferiore, deseruit ergo meliorem. Non potest regere quod regebat, quia regi noluit a quo regebatur. Ergo mode redeat, laudet. Consilium sibi ex luz Dei dat ipsa anima per rationalem mentem, unde concipit consilium fixum in aeternitate auctoris sui. Legit ibi quiddam tremendum, laudandum, amandum, desiderandum et appetendum: nondum tenet, nondum capit; coruscation

over there. Therefore, he concentrates on himself, paying attention to his health and says: Praise the Lord, my soul. 6. What's up, brothers? Do we not praise the Lord? Don't we continually sing a hymn? Do not our mouths sing daily, according to our ability, and our hearts burst out in praise of God? And what do we praise? Great is what we praise, but what we praise is still weak. When does the praiser fully praise the excellence of the Praised One? See a man; sometimes he sings to God profusely; Their lips frequently move while singing; However, his thoughts wander about I don't know what desires. Our mind, in a certain way, remained attentive praising God, but our soul wandered here and there, busy with different hobbies or worldly business concerns. Therefore, as if watching out our mind for the fluctuation from one side to the other, turning as it were to the restlessness of its annoyances, it says: Praise, my soul, the Lord. Why do you worry about other things? Why do you entertain the care of earthly and mortal things? Stay here with me, praise the Lord. But the soul, as if overloaded and without the strength to remain as it should, responds to the mind: I will praise God in my life. What does it mean in my life? that now I find myself in my death. Then first admonish yourself and say: Praise the Lord, my soul. But your soul answers you: "I praise as much as I can: dimly, weakly, badly." Because? Because, while we are in the body, we make a pilgrimage towards God. By quadam perstringitur, it is not also valid ut maneat ibi. Itaque colligit se ad sanitatem quamdam, et dicit, Lauda, ​​anima mea, Dominum. 6. Et quid est, fratres? Nonne laudamus Dominum? nonne quotidie hymnum nos cantamus? nonne quotidie pro modulo nostro sonat os nostrum, parturit cor nostrum laudes Dei? Et quid est quod laudamus? Magnum est quod laudamus; sed quod laudamus adhuc infirmum est. When implet laudator excellentiam laudati? Ecce homo stat, cantat Deo aliquanto prolixius, et saepe labia moventur ad cantum, cogitatio autem per nescio quae desideria volat. Stabat ergo mens nostra quodam moda ad landem Dei, et anima nostra per diverse cupíditates vel curas negotiorum hac atque illac fluitabat. Quasi desuper attendit ipsa mens ad fluitantem hac atque illac, et eius disturbinginem annoyingum quasi conversa alloquitur: Lauda, ​​anima mea, Dominum. Quid est quod de alus rebus satagis? quid est quod te occupat cura rerum terrenarum atque mortalium?

Sta mecum, lauda Dominum. Et quasi ipsa anima praegravata, et non valens ita consístere ut dignum est, respondert mentí: Laudabo Dominum in vita mea. Quid est, in vita mea? Quia modo in morte mea sum. Ergo prius exhortare te, et dic, Lauda, ​​anima mea, Dominum. Respondet tibi anima tua: Laudo quantum possum, tenuiter, exiliter, ínfirmiter. Quare? Quia quamdiu sumus in corpore, pilgrimage to Domino (2 Cor 5,6). Quare sic laudas Dominum, non perfecte, non stabiliter? Interroga Scripturam: Quia Corpus quod corrumpitur,

that you praise the Lord imperfectly and unstablely? Question to the Scripture: The corruptible body overburdens the soul, and the earthly habitation depresses the mind that thinks many things. "Remove me of the body, which burdens the soul, and I will praise the Lord. As long as I remain in this way, I cannot, I find myself overloaded." So what? Will you be silent and not praise the Lord perfectly? I will praise the Lord in my life. 7. What does it mean in my life? You are my hope here. You, we say, are my hope in this world; but you are not my portion here, but in the land of the living. This land here belongs to the dead; from here we will pass; but it is interesting to know where. Because the bad man and the good man make a pilgrimage here, and the good man does not pass here and the bad man stays, nor does the bad man pass here and the good man stay; They both pass, but not to the same place. There were two men: one poor and ulcerous who lay at the door of a rich man; another rich man who was dressed in purple and linen and who ate sumptuously every day. Both were in the world; Both passed, but not to the same place, since they received different places by lot, because they carried different merits. The poor went to Abraham's bosom, and the rich to the torments of hell. On earth they were physically close: the rich man, in the palace; the poor man, before the door; Only after death were they separated, and in such a way that Abraham says: Between us and you there is a great abyss. Then, brothers, as hope sustains us here and our life is not perfect, but the promised one, for here we groan, here aggravat animam, et deprimit terrena inhabitatio sensum plana cogitantem (Wis 9:15). Tolle mihi corpus quod aggravat animam, et laudo Dominum; toíle mihi terrenam habitationem deprimentem sensum fines cogitantem, ut a multis in unum confluam, et laudo Dominum: quamdiu autem ita sum, non possum, praegravor. Quid ergo? silebis, et non laudabis perfecte Dominum? Laudabo Dominum in vita mea. 7. Quid est, in vita mea? Spes mea you are hic. Spes mea es tu hic, dicimus: portio autem mea non hic, sed in terra vivostium (Ps 141,6). Nam ista terra morientium est: hinc transimus: sed interest quo. Quoniam et malus homo peregrinatur hic, et bonus homo peregrinatur hic. Non enim bonus transit, et malus hic permanet; aut malus transit, et bonus hic permanet: ambo transeunt, sed non ambo ad unum.

Erant duo; pauper ulcerosus ad ianuam iacens divitis, et dives indutus purpura et bysso, in epulis quotitidie splendidis: ambo hic erant, ambo hinc transierunt, sed non ad unum locum; diverse loca suscipiunt, quia diverse merita perducunt. Transit pauper in sinum Abrahae, et transit dives in storm inferorum. Vicini corpore in terra; ílle in domo, ille ante ianuam: post mortem tantum separati, ut dicat Abraham, inter nos et vos chaos magnum jirmatum est (Luke 16,19-26). Ergo, fratres, quoniam spes hic pascít, vita autem nostra perfection non est, nisi illa quae promittitur; hic gemitus, hic temptationes, hic anguishe, hic moerores, hic pericula: laudabit anima nostra Dominum quomodo laudandus est, secundum quod

Temptations, anguish, sadness and dangers surround us, for the same reason, our soul, when all our occupation is praise, will praise the Lord as he should be praised, as it is said in another psalm: Blessed are those who dwell in your house; forever and ever they will praise you. But when will this take place? In my life. So now, what is it? I could tell you: my death. What is my death like? Because I am a pilgrim towards God; If being united with Him is life, being apart from Him is death. But what consoles you? The hope. You already live on hope; praise, sing in hope. Where death is, do not sing; Sing where you live. Your death is in the affliction of this world, and you live in the hope of the future age. I will praise, he says, the Lord in my life. 8. How will you praise your Lord? I will salt my God while I exist. What praise is this: I will praise my God while I exist? See, my brothers, what that being or existence will be. Where praise must be eternal, existence will be eternal. Now you exist. Will you praise your God while you exist? See that you salmeted, but you gave yourself over to another occupation; You no longer salme, and yet you exist; see that you exist and do not salmear. Perhaps also, carried away by the greed of some business, not only do you not salmete, but you offend their ears, and yet you exist. What praise will be that for which while you exist you praise? Why do you say while I exist? By chance you must not exist at some time? What do I say? Eternal will be that while, and therefore it will be true while. Because everything that has an end in time, no matter how long it lasts, is not while. I will salt God while I exist. dicitur in alio psalmo, Beati qui habitant in domo tua, in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5); quando totum negotium nostrum ipsa laus erit. Sed when hoc? In vita mea. Enim mode what is it? Posset tibi dicere, Mors mea. Unde mors tua? Quia pilgrim to Domino. Si enim haerere illi, vita est; I will retreat ab illo, mors est. Sed quid console you? Spes. Iam vivis in spe; of spe lauda, ​​of spe sings. Unde mors tua est non cantes; Once you live, sing. Mors tua est de moerore huius saeculi, vivis in spe saeculi futuri. Laudabo, inquit, Dominum in vita mea. 8. Et quomodo laudabis Dominum tuum? Psallam Deo meo quamdíu sum. Qualis illa laudatio, Psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum? Videte, fratres mei, quale erit illud esse. Ubi sempiterna laudatio erit, sempiternum esse erit. This mode is; numquid psallis Deo tuo quamdiu is?

Ecce psallebas; avertisti te ad aliquod negotium, iam non psallis, et es: ecce es, et non psallis. Fortassis etiam cupiditate ínclinatus ad aliquid, non solum non psallis, sed et offendis auditum eius; et es tamen. Quae erit illa laudatio, ubi quamdiu is laudes? Sed quid ait, quamdiu sum? Aliquando forte non erit? Imo aeternum erit ipsum diu, et ideo veré diu erit. Nam quidquid finem habet in tempore, quamlibet longum sit, diu non est. Psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum.
Only trust should be placed in God

9. As long as you praise your God well in the future while you exist, you will praise the Lord in your life. Very good, but '; Expect from God everything that has to be undertaken in this world. We are surrounded on all sides by work and anguish; hope does not abandon us in this pilgrimage and temptation, in these audacity and snares of the enemy. What will we do? Listen to what follows: Do not trust princes. Brothers, here we have received a great occupation; It is a divine voice that makes itself heard for us from above. Now, I do not know by what weakness, the human soul, being troubled, despairs of the Lord in this world and tries to trust in man. Say to a man who is in trouble: "There is a powerful man who can deliver you." Hearing this, the breath returns to the body, it rejoices and lifts the spirit. But if you say to him: "God delivers you," as if in despair, he freezes. A mortal promises you help, and you rejoice; The Immortal promises it to you, and you become sad! He who is to be delivered with you promises to deliver you, and you rejoice as if at some great help; The Liberator promises it to you, who does not need a liberator, and you consider it a fable. Woe to such thoughts! They wander very far, in them is the true and unfortunate death. Draw near, begin to desire, begin to seek and know the One by whom you were made. He will not abandon his work if his work does not abandon him. Turn to Him to whom you say: I will praise the Lord in my life and praise my God while I exist. Filled with a great spirit, the psalmist warns us and says how those who are far away and pilgrims are distant9. Interim bene, laudabis Dominum in vita tua, psallis of the future Deo tuo quamdiu es. Bene: quidquid hic praesumendum est, de illo spera. Non nos deserat spes in this peregrinatione et temptatione, in istis improbitatibus et insidiis inimici, circumstrepentibus undique tentationibus saeculi, undique in laboribus et angoribus constitutos. Quid ergo faciemus? Audi quid sequatur: Nolile confidere in principes. Fratres, magnum negotium hic accipimus; divina vox est, et desuper sonat nobis. Modo enim nescio qua infírmitate anima humano, quando fuerit tríbulata, hic desperat de Domino, et vult praesumere de homine. Dicatur homini in afflictione aliqua constituto, Est quídam homo magnus, per quem possis liberai: arridet, gaudet, erigitur. Quod si dicatur illi, Liberat te Deus: quasi desperatione frigescit.

Promittitur auxilium mortalis, et gaudes: promittitur immortalis, et tristis es! Promittitur tibi quod liberet te tecum líberandus, et tanquam aliquo magno auxilio exsultas: promittitur ille liberator qui liberatore non indiget, et quasi ad fabellam desperas. Vae talibus cogitationibus; longe peregrinantur: veré misera et magna mors in eis. Appropinqua, incipe desiderare, incipe quaerere et agnoscere eum a quo factus es. Non enim deseret opus suum, si ab opere suo non deseratur. Converte ergo te ad illum cui dicis, Laudabo Dominum in vita mea, psallam Deo meo quamdiu sum. Monet enim nos iam impletus both spiritu iste, et dicit quasi longe remotis, et longe peregrinantibus, et non solum Deum non volentibus laudare, sed nondum vel de Deo speranti-
Unanations on the Psalms

ized, and who not only do not want to praise God, but do not even trust in God. Do not trust in princes or in the sons of men, in whom there is no health. There is only health in one son of man; and in him not because he is the son of man, but because he is the Son of God; not for what he received from you, but for what he reserved in himself. Therefore health does not exist in any man; because in Him who exists, exists because He is also God. God above all things, worthy to be blessed forever. Of Christ it was said: From whom Christ proceeds according to the flesh. Who does it come from? Of the Jews, of the patriarchs according to the flesh; but is Christ everything as far as the flesh is concerned? No. Because as far as the flesh is concerned, it is not God over all things, worthy to be blessed forever. Therefore in Him is health, because health is from the Lord. Another psalm says: Health belongs to the Lord and you bless your people. Without reason, then, men arrogate to themselves the power to give health. Give it to yourselves. Answer the proud man: "Do you boast of giving me health? Give it to yourself. See if you have it. If you consider your weakness well, you will see that you do not have it yet. Therefore do not advise me to expect it from you; expect it with me." Do not trust in princes, nor in the sons of men, in whom there is no health. You see that certain princes who I don't know where they come from come up to us and tell us: "I baptize; what I give is holy; and if you receive it from another, you have received nothing; if from me, you received something." Oh man, oh prince! Do you want to count yourself among the sons of men, among the princes in whom there is no health? I possess health because you seek me: Nolite confidere in principes, et in filios hominum, quibus non est salus. In one filio hominis salus; et in ipso non quia fiíius hominis, sed quia Filius Dei; non propter id quod susceptit ex te, sed propter id quod servavit in se. Ergo in nullo homine salus: quia et in illo ideo salus, quia Deus, qui est super omnia Deus benedictus in saecula. De Christo dictum est: Ex quibus Christus secundum carnem (Rom 9,5). Ex quibus? Ex Iudaeis, ex patribus Christus secundum carnem: sed numquid hoc totum Christus, quod secundum carnem? Non: ñeque enim secundum carnem id est, super omnia Deus benedictus in saecula. Ideo in illo salus, quia Domini est salus. Dicít enim alius psalmus: Domini est salus, et super populum tuum benedictio tua (Ps 3,9). Et sine causa sibi arrogant homines quia dant salutem. Sibi dent.

Reply superbo homini: Gloriaris, quia dicis I will give you mihi salutem; lukewarm da. See if you have eam. Considers bene fragilitatem tuam, vides quia nondum habes. Ergo noli monere ut exspectem a te, sed exspecta mecum. Nolite confidere in principes, et in filios hominum, quibus non est salus. Ecce nescio qui principes procedunt, nescio unde, et dicunt: Ego baptizo, et ego quod dedero, hoc est sanctum: et si ab alio acceperis, nihil accepistí; If you accept me, I accept you. O homo, o princeps, Inter filios hominum vis esse, et Inter principes quibus non est salus? Ideo ergo habeo salutem, quia tu mihi das? Tuum est enim quod das? Aut vero etiaro tu das? vel hoc digandum est, quia tu

do you give it? Is what you give yours? Do you certainly give? Or should it be said that you give? Let the pipe also say that it gives water, let the canal also say that it is the one that flows, let the crier say that it is the one that delivers. I, in the water, attend to the fountain; In the crier's voice I see the judge. You are certainly not the author of my health, but He of whom I am sure; I trust nothing of you. If you are not arrogant, not only will I not trust you, but you will not trust yourself either. My health comes from Him who is above all things, for health is from the Lord. You are among the sons of men, among the princes; but I hear the voice of the psalm, saying: Put not your trust in princes nor in the sons of men, in whom there is no salvation. 10 [v.4]. Considering the multitude of men, what are these sons of men? Do you want to know what they are? His spirit will come out, and (the flesh) will return to its land. See what he speaks, not knowing how long he spoke; threatens, not knowing how long he has to live. Suddenly his spirit will come out, and (the flesh) will return to its land. Will his spirit come out whenever he wants? He will go out, but when he doesn't want to go out, and when he ignores it, he will return to his land. When his spirit goes out, the flesh will return to the earth. But since it was the flesh that spoke thus, then only those of whom it was said: They are flesh would say: "Trust in me, I give it to you"; For the same reason, the spirit will go out, and (the flesh) will return to its land; and on that day all his thoughts will perish. Where is the swelling? Where is the pride? Where is the boasting? But perhaps he will pass to the good place, to the righteous, if he passes; because who do you give? Dicat et fistula quia et ipsa dat aquam; dicat et canalis quia ipse manat; dicat et praeco quia et ipse liberat. Ego in aqua attendo fontem, in voce praeconis agnosco iudicem. Non eris tu plañe auctor salutis meae; ille erit de quo securus sum; de te incertus sum, sed et tu de te. Ab illo ergo mihi salus, qui est super omnia; quia Domini est salus. Your inter filios hominum, your Inter principes: sed audio vocem Psalmi, Nolite confidere in principes, et in filios hominum, a quibus non est salus. 10 [v.4]. Secundum turbam hominum, quid sunt isti filíi hominum? Quid sunt vis scire? Exiet spiritus eius, et revertetur in terram suam. Ecce totum quod loquitur, nesciens quamdíu loquatur; minatur, nesciens quamdiu vivat. Sudden exiet spiritus eius, et revertetur in terram suam. Numquid quando vult, exiet spiritus eius?

Exiet, et quando non vult exiet, et quando nescit revertetur in terram suam. Exeunte spiritu, expensive revertetur in terram. Sed quia caro erat quae sic loquebatur (De me enim praesume, et ego tibi do, non dicerent nisi lili de quibus dictum est, Quia caro sunt [Gen 6,3]), Exiet spiritus eius, et revertetur in terram suam: in illa die peribunt omnes cogitationes tus. Ubi is typhus? Is ubi superbia? ubi est iactantia? Sed forte ad locum bonum transierit, ad iustos: si tamen transitiit. Nam qui sic loquebatur, nescio quo transierit. Loquebatur enim superbia; et nescio quo transeant such nomines, nisi quia inspicio alterum psalmum, et video malum eorum esse transitum.

He speaks like this, I don't know where he will go. So pride spoke; and I would not know where such men are to pass if it were not for the fact that I consult another psalm and see that their passage is evil: I saw the proud one who exalted himself above the cedars of Lebanon, and who passed away and was no more; I looked for him, and I didn't find his place. The righteous man who passed by and did not find the wicked, came to where the wicked is not. Then, brothers, let us all listen; beloved of God, let us all listen. In any tribulation, in any desire for divine goods! Let us not trust in princes or in the sons of men, in whom there is no health. All this is mortal, transitory and expired. His spirit will come out, and the (flesh) will return to its land; On that day all his thoughts will perish. 11 [v.5]. What shall we do if the sons of men and princes are not to be trusted? What will we do? Blessed is he who has the God of Jacob as his helper. Not this or that angel, but blessed is everyone who has the God of Jacob as his helper; for he helped Jacob in such a way that he made him Israel from Jacob. Immense help, because Israel is the one who sees God. Then, placed on this pilgrimage, still not seeing God, if you receive the helper God of Jacob, you will be Israel, and you will see God; and all work and all groaning will disappear, bitter toils will pass and happy praises will take place. Blessed is he who has the God of Jacob, of this Jacob, as his helper. How is he blessed when he still groans in this life? Their hope lies in the Lord, their God; Therefore he is blessed, because his hope is in the Lord,

his God; and he who is your hope will be your reality. Brothers, was I wrong because I said that God must be our reality? What would happen if I said it was to be our inheritance? You are my hope and my portion in the land of the living. You will be my portion. You will be a possession and you will possess: you will be God's possession, and God will be your possession; You will be a possession to be cared for by Him, and He will be your possession to be cared for, because you cultivate God, and God cultivates you. It is rightly said "cultivation of God"; but how are you cultivated by God? For we see that the Apostle says: You are God's agriculture and God's edification; and the Lord also says: I am the vine, you are the branches, and my Father is the farmer. God cultivates you to bear fruit, and you cultivate God to bear fruit. It is good for you that God cultivates you and that you cultivate God. If the farmer God departs from man, man becomes a desert; If the man farmer turns away from God, he is also converted into a wasteland. God does not increase by getting closer to you nor decrease by moving away from you. Then He will be our possession to feed us, and we will be His possession to govern us.

Vidi impium exaltari super cedars Libani, et transivi, et ecce non erat; et quaesivi eum, et non est inventus locus eius (Ps 36,35-36). Iste pius qui transit et non invenit impium, illuc pervenit ubi non est impius. Which one and in what does it hold truth? Doing justice to those who suffer injury. Come, my brothers, to those who suffer injury, give them justice. To whom? To those who endure injury, punishing all the unjust. If you must help those who endure injury and punish those who revile, see now who you wish to count yourself among. Go, listen, if you want to be among those who endure injury or among those who commit it. Instantly the apostolic voice meets you and tells you: It is absolutely a crime for you to have disputes among yourselves. Why do you not tolerate insults? Correct men who cannot tolerate insults. It does not exhort you to suffer inconveniences, but to endure insults, since not all annoyance is an injury. Everything you endure in justice is not an insult. So that you do not say: "I also count myself among those who suffer injuries, because I suffered that in that place, that for that reason." See if you suffered injury. Thieves suffer many evils, but not injuries. It is one thing to suffer injury, and another to endure tribulation, or punishment, or annoyance, or torture. Consider where you are; See what you did, why you suffered, and therefore you will realize what you suffered. Justice and injustice or injury are opposite things. Justice is what is fair, and not everything that is said to be fair is fair. For what would we say if someone established an iniquitous right? It could not be called a right, because it is unjust. Therefore true justice or true right is what is at the same time just. Examine then what you do, not what you suffer. If you have done justice, you will endure insults; If you committed injuries, you will endure justice. Facientem iudicium iniuriam accipientibus. very difficult for man, it is very easy for God. Then He to whom all things are very easy makes hay grow on the mountains. There is nothing more sterile than the harsh mountains. But it rains who makes hay grow on the mountains, and grass for the service of man. For whose service? Pay attention to Saint Paul himself: We—he says—are your servants through Jesus Christ. He who said: If we sow spiritual goods for you, will it be a big deal if we reap your carnal goods?, was called a servant. We serve you, brothers. We will be greater if we are more humble. The apostle Saint Paul, living by his own work, did not want to receive this hay from the mountains; he wanted to feel the need; but, nevertheless, the mountains offered hay. Perhaps because He did not want to receive it, should the mountains not provide hay, remaining barren? Cover the sky with clouds and prepare rain for the earth; He makes hay grow on the mountains, and grass for man's service. 18 [v.9]. And give the beasts their food. These animals are God's flock. God does not stop giving his flock its own food through men, for whose service he makes grass sprout. Hence the Apostle says: Who feeds the flock and does not drink its milk? And He gives food to the beasts, and to the chicks of the ravens that cry out to Him. Do we perhaps think that the ravens call upon God to give them food? Do not think that the irrational soul invokes God; Only the rational soul knows how to invoke God. Understand that this was said figuratively, and do not believe, as some impious people say, that human souls are reincarnated in beasts, in dogs, in pigs, in crows. Remove such a thing from your thoughts and your faith. The human soul was made in the image of God, (and God) will not give his image to the dog or the pig. Then what does the chickens of the crows that invoke him mean? Who are the crows' chickens? The Israelites said that only they were righteous, because they had received the law, and that all the remaining men of all the other nations were sinners. Certainly all nations were involved in sin, in idolatry, in the worship of stones and trees. But did they remain like this? If the same ravens, our fathers, did not call upon God, yet we,

19 [v.10]. He will not take pleasure in the strength of the horse. The strength of the horse is pride. The horse seems arranged to be the man's box, so that he walks taller. And, in truth, he has a neck, which symbolizes pride. Men are not conceited by their dignities, nor are they considered exalted by honors; Be careful not to be rushed by the untamed horse. See what is said in another psalm: The potentates, some trust in chariots, others in horses; but we will exalt ourselves in the name of the Lord our God. That is, they will exalt themselves with temporal honors, we will exalt ourselves in the name of the Lord, our God. For the same reason, what happens to them? See what follows: Their feet were tied, and they fell; we rise and we are standing. He will not take pleasure in the strength of the horse nor will he take pleasure in tabernacles.

Ne hoc cogitetis, irrationalem animara invokere Deum; non novit anima invokere Deum, nisi sola rationalis. In figura accipite dictum, ne putetis, sicut ímpii quídam dicunt, I stirred up human souls ad pécora, ad canes, ad porcos, ad corvos. Hoc a cordibus vestris exckidite, et a fide vestra. Israelitae se solos iustos esse dicebant, quia Legem acceperant; caeteros omnes omnium gentium homines peccatores dicebant. And I will see omnes gentes in sin, in idololatria, in adoratione lapidum atque lígnorum erant; sed numquíd sic remanserunt? Etsi non ipsi corvi patres nostri, tamen pulli corvorum nos ipsi evocamus Deum. Dat pecoribus escam ipsorum,

et pullis corvorum qui invokent eum. Ipsi sunt pulli corvorum, quibus dicit Petrus: Quia non corruptibili argento vel auro redempti estis de supervacua vestra consuetudine a parentibus vestris tradita (1 Petr 1,18). Proficientes enim pulli corvorum qui simulacra colere videbantur parentum suorum, conversi sunt ad Deum. Et audis moda pullum corvi invokentem unum Deum. Quid ergo? dimisisti patrem tuum, dicit pullo corvi? Dimisi plane: ille enim corvus non invokens Deum, ego pullus corvi invoco Deum. Et pullis corvorum qui invoking eum. 19 [v.10]. Non in potentatu equi voluntatem habebit. Potentatus equi is superbia. Videtur enim equus veluti ad suggestum hominis accommodatus, ut altior incedat. Et revera est in eo cervix, indicas quamdam superbiam. Non se extollant homines in suis dignitatibus, non se sublimes putent honoribus; caveant ne equo untamed praecipitentur. Vide enim quid dictum est in alio psalmo: Hi in curribus, et hi in equis; nos autem in nomine Domini Dei nostri magnificabimur. Hoc est, illi in honoribus temporalibus, nos in nomine Domini Dei nostri magnificabimur. Propterea illis quid accidit? Videte quid sequitur: lilis obligati sunt pedes, et ceciderunt; nos vero surreximus, et erecti sumus (Ps 19,8-9). Non in potentatu equi voluntatem habebit; nec in tahernaculis viri bene sentiet. In tahernaculis, inquit, viri. Est enim tabernaculum Domini, ipsa sancta Ecclesia toto orbe diffusa. Haeretici dividentes ab Ecclesiae

Raven chicks, we call upon him. He gives his food to the beasts, and to the chicks of the crows that call upon him. 20 [v. l l ]. What else do you add? The Lord will be pleased with those who fear him and those who trust in his mercy. The Lord will be pleased with those who fear him; But do we fear God like a thief? It is true that the thief, the beast, is feared; the unjust and powerful man is greatly feared. Well, if we love Christ, we must also desire his coming. It is perverse, and, for the same reason, I do not know or I do not believe that it has any place to fear the coming of Him whom you love; May you ask for your kingdom to come, and fear being heard. But where does fear come from? What should the judge come from? Is he perhaps unjust, malevolent, envious? Or, in short, do you hope that your cause will be known to another, so that it does not happen that the one to whom you presented it, either deceives you by prevarication or that, because he lacks science and oratory faculty, cannot prove your innocence with words? None of this will happen. Who is to come? Why aren't you happy? Who will come to judge you but the one who came to be judged for your benefit? Do not fear the accuser, of whom He Himself said: The prince of this world was thrown out into the open. Do not fear that he will be a bad lawyer, because the one who is your lawyer now must then be your judge. There he will be, you and your cause; The manifestation of your cause is the testimony of your conscience. Whoever you are who fears the future judge, correct your present conscience now. Does it seem too bad to you that I don't investigate the past? Then he will judge in an instant, but now, with how much time he does not warn! Then not anymore

there will be room for correction; Now who stops it? Remembering this on Sunday with great insistence, since, in fact, almost only this must be said, I spent not a little time, and I was forced to defer until today this psalm that I proposed to treat. Well, what patient will dare to give advice to the doctor? 2. When (the psalm) was read, I think that all, or many of you, noticed that it has some verses that to make them clear should be called; mainly those who say that it gives snow like wool and spreads fog like ashes, sends hail like pieces of bread; Faced with its cold, who will resist? Hearing these things, everyone who takes them literally thinks of divine works. Well, who gives the snow but God? Who spreads the fog and who hardens the hail outside of Him? Still, these three things have their appropriate and opposite similarities, for wool is not unlike snow, nor ash to fog, nor the piece of white bread to the splendor and innocence of ice or hail. Hail or glacial is a certain kind of glass, but white. This way of being is reported by those who knew him, and we should not doubt it, since the most faithful Scripture attests to it. It is said that the glacier, since the snow does not liquefy, hardening for many years, freezes to such an extent that it is difficult to liquefy. it was resurrected in its entirety; see that he showed himself in the eyes of his disciples; see that he offers himself to be touched with the hands; See that they touched the scars, which, once hope was lost, became wounds of love. He presented himself to their eyes so that they could see him, and to their hands so that they could touch him; Yet they think it is spirit; They therefore doubted his health. He exhorts them, confirms them in the faith, telling them: Feel and see, that the spirit has no flesh or bones, just as you see me who have them. They touch, they rejoice, they are amazed, and they even doubted their joy, because this is how it is written. Things that cause too much delight, even if they are true, are hardly believed. The doubt of a reluctant believer engenders the desire to possess. Man must be extremely happy when what he distrusted appears. To engender and increase this joy he did not want to be recognized instantly. He veiled the eyes of two of his disciples, whom he found on the road conversing with each other distrustfully and saying: We hoped that He would be the redeemer of Israel. They had believed this, but they no longer believed it. They had already lost hope, and yet Christ was with them; but the one who joined them gave them hope again. Later, after having met him at the breaking of bread and having appeared to other of his disciples, he said when they believed he was a spirit: Feel and see, because the spirit has neither flesh nor bones, as you see me who have them. And as they still doubted because of their joy, he said to them: Do you have anything to eat here? He took it, blessed it, ate it and gave it to them. The reality of his body has been made clear and all suspicion of falsehood has been destroyed. What does he say next? Ignotíbus manibus, ecce tetigerunt scars, quae desperatae sunt vulnera. Exhibit se oculis eorum videndum, manibus contrectandum: putant spiritum esse; desperverunt enim de salute sua. Praise the Lord from the heavens. He already listed the celestial beings. Hear now the terrestrials: (Praise) dragons and all the abysses. The abysses are the depths of water. All the seas and this gloomy air belong to the abyss. He called the whole place where the clouds, the winds, the storms, the rain, the lightning, the thunder, the hail, the snow and everything that God wants to be done on the earth of this dark humid air, with the name of earth, because it is too changeable and perishable, unless you believe that it rains above, in the stars. All these things happen here, next to the earth. Well, sometimes, while men are on the tops of the mountains, they see that, with the clouds under their feet, it is raining. These phenomena,

caused by the disturbance of the air, are declared to those who attend well to take place here in this lower part of the world. That is why the devil, who fell with his angels from the order of the heavenly beings, was condemned to this caliginous place, that is, to this air, as if to prison, since the apostle Saint Paul says this about him: According to the prince of the power of the air, who now works in the children of unbelief. And Saint Peter also writes: God did not forgive the angels who sinned, but confined them in the caliginous prisons of hell and handed them over to be kept to punish them in judgment. He called hell the lower part of the world. Do not consider what the devil received, but what he lost. You see that all these things are changeable, confusing, terrible, corruptible; However, they occupy a place, they have their order, they all come together, according to their condition, to complete the beauty of the universe, and, for this reason, they praise God. Then, turning to them, as if exhorting them, or rather, exhorting us so that by considering them we praise the Lord, for in this way they praise God, engendering praise to God by considering them, the psalmist begins to say: Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all the deeps. The dragons are by the water; They come from the caves and go to the air and through them the air is excited. Dragons are certain large animals; the greatest on earth. Dracones et omnes abyssi. Abyssi, profunditates aquarum sunt: ​​maria omnia, nubilosus iste aer ad abyssum pertinet. Ubi clouds, ubi venti, ubi teropestates, ubi pluviae, coruscationes, tonitrua, grandines, nix, et quidquid vult Deus fieri super terras de isto humido et caliginoso aere, totum hoc terrae nomine appellavit, quia nimis mutabile est atque mortale: nisi forte putatis quia sursum pluit stellis. Omnia ergo ista videtis qualia sunt, mutabilia, turbata, terribilia, corruptibilia: tamen habent locum suum, habent ordinem suum, implent et ipsa universi pulchritudinem pro moda suo, et ideo laudant Dominum. Conversus ergo ad illa, tanquam exhortans et ipsa; imo exhortans nos, ut eorum consideratione laudemus Dominum (sic enim laudant Deum, cum considerata pariunt laudem Dei), coepit dicere, Laúdate Dominum de terra, dracones et omnes abyssi. But why do lightning sometimes strike the mountains and not kill the thieves? All that I can say, explaining why God strikes the mountains and does not kill the thief, according to the capacity of my mind and to the extent that God grants me, and those of greater capacity will know more sublime things and will understand more widely, and I hope that God will grant you to perceive more than what I say, but with temperance and without pride, I can say, according to my capacity, that it happens because perhaps the conversion of the sinner is still waiting. And, therefore, strike the mountain that does not fear so that the man who fears may change, for you too sometimes, when you punish, strike the earth so that the child may be afraid. Other times she hurts the man she loves. But he tells me: "See that he hurts the innocent and sets the wicked free." Don't be surprised; Death, from whatever quarter it comes, is good for the pious. How do you know the penalty that is reserved for that criminal in the secret of God if he does not want to change his life? Wouldn't those who will finally be told: Go to the eternal game, would not have preferred to be burned by lightning? The interesting thing is to be innocent. Well what? Is it bad to die in a shipwreck, and good to die from fever? Whether he dies from this or the other cause, investigate who it was who died stultis, et quasi casibus agitari, addidit, Quae faciunt verbum eius. Non tibi ergo videantur casibus moveri, quae verbo Dei in omni motu suo deserviunt. Quo vult Deus, illuc ignis, illuc fertur clouds, sive pluviam, sive level, sive grandinem portet. Et quare aliquando percutiunt montem fulmina, et non pecutiunt latronem? Quodcumque possum dicere pro captu mentís meae, quantum Deus donare digntur: maiores maiora noverint, et amplius intelligant; et det vobis Deus plus sapere quam dico, tamen cum tempetantia, sine superbia: possum ergo pro module meo dicere quare percutiant montem, et non percutiant latronem: quia forte adhuc latronis, conversionem quaerit; et ideo percutítur mons qui non timet, ut mutetur homo qui timet. Aliquando et tu, cum das disciplinam, terram feris, ut infans expavescat. Et aliquando ferit et quem vult hominem.

Sed dicis mihi: Ecce ferit innocentiorem, et dimittit sceleratiorem. Noli mirari: undecumque mors pio bona est. Unde autem six illi sceleratiori, si se mutare noluerit, quid poenarum in oceulto servetur? Nonne mallent fulmine íncendí, quibus in fine dicetur: I te in ignem aeternum? (Mt 25,41). Opus est innocens sis. Quid enim? malum est mori shipwreck, et bonum est mori febre? Sive inde, sive inde moritur, quaere qualis sit qui moritur; quo post mortem iturus est, non unde de vita exíturus. Quacumque occasione, hinc exituri sumus, Quibus exitibus martyres exire meruerunt? numquid febribus, quomodo multi optant ut

and where he must go after death, not for what cause he died. Whatever the reason, we must die. What kind of death did the martyrs deserve to die with? Perhaps with death due to fever, as many wish to die? Some died by sword blows, others by fire, others by beasts. The beasts devoured the bodies of the martyrs; They were not afraid that their bodies would perish. God, for whom our hairs are numbered, will bring the bodies of his saints back to life from anywhere. When he wanted, he freed the three young people from the fire. But did he abandon the Maccabees in the fire? He delivered the first clearly, the second he crowned secretly. God knows what he's doing. You fear and be good. Wherever He wants to take you out of the world, He finds you ready. You are a tenant, not the owner of the house. The house was rented to you. This house was rented to you, not donated to you. Even if you don't want to, you will get out of it, since you did not rent it on such a condition that you would set the time. What did your Lord say? When He wants to say: "Immigrate, be prepared. I throw you out of the inn, but I give you the house; on earth you are a tenant, in heaven an owner." 12. Therefore everything that happens here against our will, you must know that it happens by the will of God, by his providence, by his disposition, by his will, by his order; and, if we do not understand why he does this or that, let us attribute it to his providence, which does nothing without a cause, and let us not blaspheme. Well, when we begin to discuss the works of God and say: "Why does he do this or that? He should not have acted like that; he did this wrong," where is the praise of febre solvantur? There is one ictu gladií, there is ignibus, there is bestiis. Et devoraverunt bestiae corpora martyrum, et non timuerunt ne perirent corpora ipsorum. Undique enim Deus reducet corpora sanctorum suorum, cui capilli nostri numerati sunt (ib. 10,30). Et quando voluit, tres pueros ab igne liberabit (Dan 3,24.93): numquid ideo Machabaeos in igne deseruit? (2 Mach 7). Illos aperte liberavit, istos occulte coronavit. Novit igitur Deus quid agat. Your time, et bonus this. Undecumque voluerít ut exeas hinc, paratum te inveniat. Inquilinus enim es (Ps 118,19), non possessor domus. Locata est enim tibi domus; domus ista tibitoucha est, non donata; etsi nolis, migrabis: et non eam talí conditione, accepisti, ut quasi tempora certa tibi sint. Quid dixit Dominus tuus? Quando voluero, cum dixero, Mígra; stop this.

Expello te de hospitio, sed dabo domum: inquilinus es in terra, erís possessor in cáelo. 12. Quidquid ergo hic accidit contra voluntatem nostram, noveritis non accidere, nisi de volúntate Dei, de providentia ípsius, de ordine ipsius, de nutu ipsius, de legibus ípsius: et si nos non intelligimus quid quare fiat, demus hoc providentiae ipsius, quia non fit sine causa, et non blasphemabimus. Cum enim coeperimus disputare de operíbus Dei, Quare hoc, quare illud; et, Non debuit sic faceré, male fecit hoc: ubi est laus Dei? Perdidisti Alleluia. Omnia sicconsidera, quomodo placeas Deo, et
Glory to God in heaven and on earth

God? The hallelujah disappeared. Consider in all things how you please God and praise the Creator. If you happen to enter a forge, perhaps you will not dare to reproach the bellows, the anvils, the hammers. However, present to me an ignorant man who does not know at all what that is for, and he reviles everything. But, if he lacks the skill of a blacksmith, but has at least the prudence of a man, what is said? "The bellows are not placed in this place without reason; the craftsman knows it, although I do not know it." He does not dare to censure the blacksmith in the forge, and would he dare to revile God in the world? Therefore, just as fire, hail, snow, frost, and tempest execute their word, so all things that appear to be vain to be done inconsiderately in the nature of things, execute only the word of God, because they only act by his command. 13 [v.9-12]. Then he says that the mountains and all the hills, the fruit trees and all the cedars, the beasts and all the animals of the field, the creeping things and the winged birds, praise the Lord. Then he addresses the men and adds: (They praise him) the kings of the earth and all the peoples, the nobles and all the judges of the world, the young men and the virgins, the elderly along with the children praise the name of the Lord. The praise of heaven and earth has already been expounded and explained. 14 [v.13]. Because only his name is excellent. Let no man try to exalt his own name. Do you want to be exalted? Submit to Him who cannot be humiliated. Only his name is excellent. laudes artificem. Quia si intrares forte in officinam fabri ferrarii, non auderes reprehenderé folies, incudes, malleos. Et da imperitum hominem nescientem quid quare sit, et omnia reprehendit. Sed si non habeat peritiam artificis, et habeat saltera considerationem hominis, quid sibi dicit? Non sine causa hoc loco folies positi sunt; artifex movit quare, etsi ergo non novi. In officina non audet vituperare fabrum; et audet reprehenderé in hoc mundo Deum! Ergo, quemadmodum ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus tempestatis, quae faciunt verbum eius; sic omnia quae vanis videntur in rerum natura I will fear fieri, non faciunt nisi verbum eius, quia non fiunt nisi iussu eius. 13 [v.9-12]. Deinde dicít, ut Dominum laudent: Montes et omnes colles, ligua fructifera et omnes cedri; bestiae et omnia pécora, reptilia et volatilia pennata.

Deinde ad homines: Reges terrae et omnes populi, principes et omnes Indices terrae; iuvenes et virgines, seniores cum iunioribus laudent nomen Vomini. Explain this laus de cáelo, explicata this laus de terra. 14 [v.13]. Quia exaltatum est nomen eius solius. Nemo hominum quaerat exaltare nomen suum. Did you see exaltari? lili te subde, qui non potest humiliari: Exaltatum est nomen eius solius.

Glory to God in the heavens and on earth

15 [v.14]. His confession (takes place) in heaven and on earth. What does his confession take place in heaven and on earth? The one for which He confesses? No, but that by which all things confess and cry out. The beauty of all beings who confess God is, in a certain way, their voice. Heaven says to God: "You made me, not I." The earth says: "You created me, not me." How do these beings cry out? When they consider themselves and this beauty is perceived in them, they cry out for your consideration, and they cry out for your voice. His confession (takes place) in heaven and on earth. Pay attention to the sky, it is beautiful; Take care of the earth, it is beautiful; Both together are extremely beautiful. He made, He directs, He governs at his own will, He orders the times and He by Himself distributes the movement. Therefore all things praise Him, now in rest, now in movement; now down, on the earth; already up, in the sky; now in old age, now in renewal. When you contemplate these things, and rejoice, and rise to the Artificer, and perceive the invisible things through the visible, his confession takes place in heaven and on earth, that is, you confess to him for terrestrial and celestial things. But since He made all things, and there is nothing better than Him, everything He made is beneath Him and everything that pleases you in these things is inferior to Him. Therefore, do not be so pleased with what He did that you separate yourself from the one who did it. If you love what he did, love who did it much more. If the things He created are beautiful, how much more beautiful is the Creator! His confession (takes place) in heaven and on earth.

16. And he will exalt the power of his people. See what Haggai and Zechariah prophesied. Now the power of his people is broken by afflictions, tribulations, temptations, beatings of the chest. When will he extol his power? When the Lord himself comes and our Sun appears; not this one that our carnal eyes see and goes forth for good and evil, but He of whom it is said: For you who fear God the sun of righteousness will rise, and health under its wings, and of whom the proud and wicked will say: The light of righteousness did not shine for us, and the sun did not rise for us. This will be our summer. Now, during the winter, the fruit that is on the root does not appear; You look at the trees, and you see them during the winter as dry. He who does not know how to see thinks that the vine is dry; and perhaps next to her there is another that truly is, because during the winter they appear alike: one is alive, another dead, but the life of one and the death of another are hidden; Summer appears, and the life of one and the death of another are manifested; The ornamentation of the leaves and the fertility of the fruit spring forth; The vine dresses externally with what it has at the root. Therefore, brothers, now we are equal to other men. As they are born, eat, drink, dress, spend this life, so do the saints. Sometimes events deceive men, and they say: "Why did he begin to be a Christian? Did he not become upset? Does he have something more because he is a Christian than I do?" Oh dry vine! Next to you you see the vine naked in the winter, but it is not dry. Summer will come, the Lord, our sister, will appear.

15 [v.14]. I confess eius in tena et cáelo. Quid est, Confessio eius in terra et cáelo? qua ipse confitetur? Non; sed qua illum omnia confitentur, omnia clamant: omnium pulchritudo quodam moda vox eorum est, confitentium Deum. Clamat caelum Deo: You fecisti me, non ego. Clamat terra: Tu me condidisti, non ego. Whomodo clamant ist? When they consider tur, et hoc invenitur; ex tua consideratione clamant, ex voce tua clamant. Confessio eius in terra et cáelo. Attende caelum, pluchrum est; attende terram, pulchra est: utrumque simul valde pulchrum est. Ipse fecit, ipse regit, ipsius nutu gubernantur, ipse traiicit tempora, momenta ipse instaurat, per seipsum instaurat. Qmnia ergo ista laudant illum, sive in statu, sive in motu, sive de terra deorsum, sive de cáelo sursum, sive in vetustate, sive in renovatione. Cum vides haec et gaudes, et attoíleris in artificem, et invisibilia eius, per ea quae facta sunt, intellecta contueris (Rom 1,20), Confessio eius in terra et cáelo; id est, confiteris ei de rebus terrenis, confiteris ei de rebus caelestibus. Et quia ipse fecit omnia, et melius illo non est aliquid, quidquid fecit, intra illum est; et quidquid in his tibi placet, minus est quam ipse. Non ergo ita tibi placeat quod fecit, ut recedas ab eo qui fecit; Be if you love quod fecit, multo magis eum qui fecit. Si pulchra sunt quae fecit, quanto pulchrior est qui fecit? Confessio eius in terra et cáelo.

16. Et exaltabit cornu populi sui. Ecce quod prophetabant Aggaeus et Zacharias. Modo cornu populi ipsius humile est in trituris, in tribulationibus, in tentationibus, in tunsione pectorum: when exaltabit cornu populi sui? Quando venerit ipse Dominus, et ortus fuerit sol noster: non iste qui oculis videtur, et oritur super bonds et malo (Mt 5,45); thirst for quo dicitur, Vobis qui timetis Deum, orietur sol iustitiae, et sanitas in pennis eius (Mal 4,2); et de quo dicturi sunt superbi et impii, Iustitiae lumen non luxit nobis, et sol non est ortus nobis (Wis 5,6). Ipsa erit aestas nostra. Modo fructus per hibernum in radice non apparent; You attend almost arid trees per hiemen. Qui non novit videre, aridam putat vitem: et forte iuxta est quae veré aruit; similes sunt ambae per hiemem; illa vivit, illa mortua est; sed illius vita et illius mors in abscondito est: aestas procedit, vita illius clarificatur, mors illius manifestatur; proceedit honor foliorum, fecunditas fructuum; vestitur vitis in facie, ex eo quod habet in radice. Ergo moda, fratres, such sumus, quales sunt alii homines: quomodo nascuntur, manducant, bibunt, vestiuntur, transigunt vitam istam; sic et sancti. Aliquando ipsa res decipit homines, et dicunt: Ecce quia coepit esse christianus, numquid non ei dolet caput? aut quia christianus est, quid habet plus a me? O vitis arida, attendis iuxta te vitem nudam in hiberno, sed non aridam. Aestas veniet, veniet Dominus, honor noster, qui latebat in radice; et tune

17. Let all your saints sing a hymn. Do you know what a hymn is? A song that praises God. If you praise God and do not sing, you do not utter a hymn; If you sing and do not praise God, you do not utter a hymn either. If you praise something that does not belong to the praise of God, even if you sing praises, you do not utter a hymn. Then the hymn carries with it these three things: song, praise, and this from God. Therefore the praise of God in the song is called a hymn. Therefore, what does it mean, let all the saints sing a hymn? Sing your holy hymn, sing your holy hymn, because this is what you will finally sing, an eternal hymn. Therefore the psalmist says in another place: The sacrifice of praise will glorify me and

Here is the path in which I will show you my health; and also: Blessed are those who dwell in your house; forever and ever they will praise you. This is precisely the hymn that is sung for its saints. Who are your saints? The children of Israel, the people close to Him. Let no one say: "I am not a son of Israel." Well, do not think that the Jews are children of Israel and we are not; I dare to tell you, my brothers, that they are not and we are. Hear why: because he who is born according to the spirit is greater than he who is born according to the flesh. Who does Israel come from? Of Abraham. Israel was born from Isaac, and Isaac from Abraham. And how did Abraham please God? Abraham believed God, and righteousness was imputed to him. Therefore he who imitates Abraham is Abraham's son; He who degenerates from the faith of Abraham loses the lineage of Abraham. The Jews degenerated, they lost their lineage. We imitate Abraham, we have found his lineage. Hear how they lost it. What did the Lord answer when they said to him: We are children of Abraham? If you were Abraham's children, you would do the works of Abraham. Then, if the Jews lost the lineage of Abraham, we get it. We find by believing what they lost by not believing; for Abraham believed God, and righteousness was imputed to him. Furthermore, Christ is the offspring of Abraham, and we are in Christ, since Mary comes from the people of Israel, from whom Christ was born, and we are in Christ; Therefore we are children of Israel. Even more: to point us out the psalmist added: Let it be sung for the children of Israel, "for the people close to Him." Pay attention to the Jews; if they come close,

exaltabit cornu populi sui, post capitivitatem in qua mortaliter vivimus. Unde dictit Apostolus: Nolite ante tempus quidquam indicare, doñee veniat Dominus, et illuminabit abscondita tenebrarum; et tune laus erit unicuique a Deo (1 Cor 4,5). You say mihi: Ubi est radix mea? Ubi est fructus meus? If you believe, nosti ubi est radix tua. Ibi est enim, ubi est fides tua, ubi spes est et chantas tua. Audi Apostolum: Mortui enim estis. Quasi per hiemem mortui apparebant; audi quia vivunt: Et vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo. Ecce ubi habes radicem. When ergo honore ornaberis? When will you fertilize fruit? Audi illum sequentem: Cum Christus apparuerit, vita vestra, tune et vos apparebitis cum ipso in gloria (Col 3,3-4). Et exaltabit cornu populi sui. 17. Hymnus omnibus sanctis eius. Hymnus scitis quid est? Cantus est cum laude Dei. Si laudas Deum, et non cantas, non dicis hymnum: si cantas, et non laudas Deum, non dicis hymnum: si laudas aliud quod non pertinet ad laudem Dei, etsi canto laudes, non dicis hymnum. Hymnus ergo tria ista habet, et cantum, et laudem, et Dei. Laus ergo Dei in canticle, hymnus dicitur. Quid est ergo, Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius? Accipiant sancti eius hymnum, dicant sancti eius hymnum; quia hoc est quod accepturi sunt in fine, hymnum sempiternum. Ideo alio loco dicit psalmus, Sacrificium laudis glorificabit me; et ibi est via qua ostendam Mi salutare meum (Ps 49,23): et, Beati qui habitant in domo

tua; in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). Hoc est, Hymnus omnibus sanctis eius. Who sunt sancti eius? Filiis Israel, populo appropinquanti sibi. Nemo dicat: Non sum filius Israel. Ne putetis ludaeos filios Israel esse, et nos non esse filios Israel: audeo vobis dicere, fratres mei; illi non sunt, et nos sumus. Audite quare: quia maior est natus secundum spiritum, quam natus secundum carnem. From Israel? Former Abraham; quia Isaac ex Abraham, Israel ex Isaac. Quomodo placuit Deo Abraham? Credidit autem Abraham Deo, et deputatum est illi ad iustitiam (Rom 4:3). Quisquís imitatus fuerit Abraham, filius est Abrahae: quisquís degeneraverit a fide Abraham, perdidit progeniem Abrahae. Iudaei degeneraverunt; perdiderunt: imitati sumus nos; invenimus. Audi quia illi perdiderunt: quid lilis dicit Dominus dicetibus, Filii sumus Abrahae? Ausi sunt ostentare se, et erigere cervicem de nobilitate generis iusti; et quid illis Dominus? Si filii Abrahae essetis, facta Abrahae fecissetis (lo 8,33.39). Si ergo perdiderunt ipsi quod filii sunt Abrahae, invenimus nos ut filii simus Abrahae. Credendo quippe invenimus quod illi non credendo amiserunt: quia credidit Abraham Deo, et deputatum est illi ad iustitiam. Et semen Abrahae Christus (Gal 3,16), et in Christo nos sumus; et ex Israel populus, de quo populo Maria, de qua Maria Christus, in quo Christo nos: ergo filii Israel nos. Et quomodo addidit, ut discerneret nos? Filiiis Israel, populo appropinquanti sibi. Attendite ludaeos: si propinquant, ipsi sunt. Et forte propinquant, dicit mihi

mosura, which was at the root, and then he will exalt the power of his people, after the captivity, in which we mortally lived. Hence the Apostle says: Do not judge anything before its time until the Lord comes, who will illuminate the hidden things of darkness; and then praise will be given to each one by God. But you say to me: "Where is my root, where is my fruit?" If you believe, you will know where your root is. It is where your faith, your hope and your charity are found. Hear the Apostle: (Now) you are dead. They appeared dead during the winter; but hear that they live: And your life is hidden with Christ in God. See where you have the root. Then when will you be beautified with adornment? When will you be fertile with the fruit? Hear the same Apostle say: When Christ, your life, appears, then you also will appear with Him in glory. And he will exalt the power of his people.

They are this town. "Perhaps they come closer," someone tells me, "because every day they sing the psalms and sing the hymns of God." But did you not hear that the prophet said to them: This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me? If your heart is far from God, ours is close, because we believe, because we hope, because we love each other, because we are united to Christ, because we were made his members. Are the members separated from the head? If they were separated and far away, would the Lord not say: See that I am with you until the end of the ages. If they had been separated from Him, He would not have said: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? If it were not in us, I would not say: I was hungry, and you gave me food; and when he replied: When did we see you hungry?, he would not have responded: When you did it to one of my little ones, you did it to me. Behold the people, behold the Israel that is approaching: now waiting for it, then possessing it.
[SINGING GOODBYE AND TO HIS PEOPLE, OF HIS DESIGNS]

1 [v.l]. Let us praise the Lord with word, mind and good deeds; and let us sing to him, as this psalm exhorts us, a new song. Well, this is how it begins: Sing to the Lord a new song. The old man sings an old song; the new, aliquis canticle: quotidie et ipsi cantant psalmum, et cantant hymnos Dei. Non auditis quid eis dixit propheta? Populus hic labiis me honorat; cor autem eorum longe est a me (Is 29:13). Si illorum cor longe est, nostrum autem cor proximum est; quia credimus, quia speramus, quia diligimus, quia Christo adiuncti sumus, quia membra ipsius facti sumus: numquid membra longe sunt a capite? Si essent longe, et divina essent, non diceret: Ecce ego vobiscum sum usque ad consummationem saeculi (Mt 28,20). Si separata essent, non de cáelo says: Saule, Saule, why are you after me? (Acts 9,4). Si non in nobis esset, non diceret, Esurivi, et dedistis mihi manducare: et cum dicerent illi, Quando te vidémus esurientem? respondit, Cum uni ex minimis meis fecistis, mihi fecistis (Mt 25,35. 37.45). Ecce populus, ecce appropinquans Israel; et cum illo moda spe, post re.

1 [v.l]. Laudemus Dominum et in voce, et in intellectu, et in opere bono; et sicut nos hortatur iste psalmus, cantemus ei canticum novum. Sic enim coepit: Cántate Domino canticum novum. Vetus homo, vetus canticum; novus homo, novum canticum. Vetus Testamentum, vetus
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

new. The Old Testament sings an old song; the New, new song. In the Old Testament there are temporal and earthly promises. Everyone who loves earthly things sings an old song. He who wants to sing a new song, let him love eternal things. Love itself is new and eternal; It is always new, because it never ages. But, if you consider it carefully, this is old. How is it new? By chance, my brothers, is eternal life now established? Christ is eternal Life, and as for divinity, he was not born now, because in the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was in God, and the Word was God, This existed in the beginning in God. All things were made by Him, and without Him nothing was made. If the things that were made by Him are old, how old is He by whom they were made? He is eternal and coeternal with the Father. We, by falling into sin, reach old age. Our voice is that of the psalm in which it is said groaningly: I have grown old in the midst of all my enemies. Man grew old through sin, but was renewed through grace. All those who are renewed in Christ in order to begin to belong to eternal life sing the new song. 2. This song is a song of peace, it is a song of charity. Anyone who departs from the congregation of saints does not sing a new song, since he follows in the footsteps of the old enmity, not those of the new charity. What is in the new charity? Peace, the bond of holy brotherhood, the spiritual bond, the building built of living stones. Where is this one? Throughout the canticum: Novum Testamentum, novum canticum. In Veteri Testament promissions sunt temporal et terrenae. Quisquís terrena diligit, vetus canticum cantat: qui vult cantore canticum novum, diligat aeterna. Ipsa dilectio nova est et aeterna: ideo semper nova, quia numquam veterascit. Nam si bene consideres, antiquum est hoc: quomodo ergo est novum? Numquid, fratres mei, vita aeterna moda nata est? Vita aeterna ipse Christus est, et secundum divinitatem non moda natus est: quia, In principle erat Verbum, et Verbum erat apud Deum, et Deus erat Verbum: hoc erat in principle apud Deum. Omnia per ipsum facta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil (lo 1,1-3). Si quae per ipsum facta sunt, antiqua sunt; quid est ipse, per quem facta sunt? Quid, nisi aeternus, et Patri coaeternus? Sed nos delapsi in peccatum, pervenimus ad vetustatem.

Nostra enim vox est in illo psalmo ubi dicitur cum gemitu: Inveteravi in ómnibus inimiás meis (Ps 6,8). Inveteravit homo per peccatum, innovatur per gratiam. Omnes ergo qui innovantur in Christo, ut ad vitam aeternam incipiant pertinere, canticum novum cantant. 2. Et hoc canticum pacis est, canticum hoc charitatis est. Quisquís se a coniunctione sanctorum separat, non cantat canticum novum. Secutus est enim veterem animosítatem, non novam chritatem. In nova charitate quid est? Pax, vinculum sanctae societatis, compago spiritualis, aedificium de lapidibus vivís. Ubi est hoc? Non in uno loco, sed per universum orbem terrarum. Audi hoc de alio psalmo: sic dicit, Cántate Do-

terrestrial orb, not in a certain place. Hear this from another psalm that goes like this: Sing to the Lord a new song; sing to the Lord all the earth. From this it follows that he who does not sing with the whole earth, sings the old song no matter how many words come out of his mouth. What do I pay attention to what he sounds, when I see what he thinks? But you will tell me: "Do you see what he thinks?" The facts prove it. Certainly the eye does not penetrate consciousness. But I see what he does, and from this I understand what he thinks. If someone, for example, catches a man in theft, murder, or adultery, he certainly does not see the thoughts of his heart, but he has the facts before him. There are certain things that remain hidden in the heart, but there are many others that are manifested in works and are also made evident to men. Well, when there are some who separate themselves from the bond of charity and the society of the holy Church, being evil within themselves, only God knows it; But, when temptation arises and separates them, it makes clear to men what only God knew. The fruits are only shown in the works; For this reason it was said: By the fruits you will know them. The Lord spoke of certain individuals who dress in sheepskins, and internally they are ravenous wolves; and so that it would not happen that human weakness would be incapable of knowing the wolf dressed in the sheep's skin, he said: By their fruits you will know them. We seek the fruit of charity, and find the thorns of dissension. By their fruits you will know them. Therefore their song is old. Let us sing the new song. I already said, brothers, that the whole earth sings a new song. The one with

The whole earth does not sing a new song, sing whatever it wants, let the tongue utter the Hallelujah, sing all day, sing all night; However, the voice of the one who sings will not drag my ear too much, since I pay attention to the customs of the one who acts. I ask him and say, "What do you sing?" He answers me: Hallelujah. What does hallelujah mean? Praise the Lord. Well come, let us praise the Lord together. Why do we disagree? Charity praises the Lord, discord outrages him. 3. Do you want to know where you should sing the new song? See where and how the things that the psalm is to say take place. See if they are carried out in all nations or in a specific part of the world, and from this you will understand perfectly to whom the new song belongs. What I commemorated from another psalm has already been declared: Sing to the Lord a new song; Well, to show that in the new song there is fruit of charity and unity, he added that psalm 95: And sing to the Lord all the earth. Nobody separates, nobody separates; You are wheat, endure the chaff until the fork. Do you want to leave the era? If you are wheat outside the threshing floor, the birds will find you and eat you. Add to this that, by the very fact that you move away and fly, you show that you are straw, since because you were weak the wind came and snatched you from under the feet of the oxen. Those who are wheat endure the threshing floor; They rejoice, and because they are grains they groan among the chaff, they wait for the winnower, whom they know as Redenror. Sing to the Lord a new song; his praise in the Church of the saints. The Church of the saints is the Church of wheat

mino canticum novum; sing Domino, omnis tena (Ps 95,1). Ex hoc intelligitur quia qui non cura omni terra cantat, canticum vetus cantat, quaelibet verba de ore eius proceedant. Quid enim attendo quid sonet, cum video quid cogitet? Et tu, inquis, vines quid cogitet? Indicative fact. Nam oculus in consciousiam non penetrat. Attendo quid agat, et ibi intelligo quid cogitet. Ñeque enim si quisque, verbi gratia, comprehenderit hominem in furto, in homicide, in adultery, cogitationes ipsius in corde videt, sed in factis. Sunt quaedam quae intus latent; sed sunt et fine quae proceedunt in opera, et manifesta fiunt etiam hominibus. Cum ergo essent illi qui se a compage Christi charitatis et societate sanctae Ecclesiae separaunt, mali intus apud se, non noverat nisi Deus. Venit tentatio; separavit illos, et patefecit hominibus quod noverat Deus. Non enim fructus ostenditur nisi in factis. Unde dictum est: Ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos (Mt 7,16). Dixit enim Dominus ad quosdam, qui ovium vestitu se induunt, intus autem sunt lupi rapacious; et ne forte ftagüitas humano dignitiescere non posset lupum sub ovina pelle, ait: Ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos. Quaerimus fructus charitatis, invenimus spinas dissensionis. Ex fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos. Ergo canticum eorum vetus est: cantemus nos canticum novum. Iam diximus, fratres, omnis terra cantat canticum novum. Qui cum omni terra non

cantat canticum novum, dicat quod vult, linguis sonet Alleluia, dicat tota die, dicat tota nocte; non valde aures meae inclinantur ad vocem cantantis, sed quaero mores operantis. I interrogate enim, et dico: Quid est, what are you singing? Answer: Alleluia. What is it, Alleluia? Praise Dominum. Come, simul laudemus Dominum. Si tu laudas Dominum et ego laudo Dominum; quare in discord sumus? Chantas laudat Dominum, discordia blasphemat Dominum. 3. Et vultis iam nosse ubi cantetis canticum novum? Quae dicturus est in ipso Psalmo, videte quomodo fiant, et ubi fiant; utrum per omnes gentes fiant ista, an in una aliqua parte terrarum: et hinc plenius intelligetis ad quem pertineat canticum novum. Iam quidem manifestum est illud quod de alio psalmo commemoravi, Cántate Domino canticum novum: Et ut ostenderet in cántico novo esse fructum charitatis et unitatis, addidit, Cántate Domino, omnis terra. Nemo se separet, nemo se disiungat: triticum es, ferto paleam quousque ventiletur. Of area vis excuti? Et si triticum esses foris abarea, invenírent te volatilia, et colligerent te (ib. 3,12). Adde quia eo ipso quo discedis et volas, paleam te esse indicas: et quia levis erat, venit ventus, et de sub pedibus boum ablatus es. Qui autem triticum sunt, ferunt tumbam; gaudent, quia grana sunt, gemunt Inter paleam, exspectant ventilatorem, quem cognoscunt redemptorem. Sing Domino canticum novum: laus eius in Ecclesia sanctorum.

spread throughout the entire earth, sown in the field of the Lord, which is this world, as the Lord himself explained when, speaking of the sower, he said that a man sowed good seed in his field, and that, when the enemy came, he sowed tares on top; Then his servants said to him, "Did you not sow good seed in your field? How come it has tares?" And he answered them: "The enemy man did this." When they wanted to uproot the tares, he prevented them, saying: Let them grow with the wheat until the harvest. At this time I will say to my reapers: "First gather up the tares and tie them in bundles to throw them into the fire, and put my wheat in the barn." Later his disciples said to him: Explain to us the parable of the tares. The Lord expounds all these things so that no man may expound at his whim what he has understood there, except in accordance with what was expounded by the heavenly Master. Let no one say: "He explained it as he wanted." If the Lord were to explain the parables of the prophets, since He spoke through them what they themselves said, who would dare to say that He should not explain them in this way? How much less will anyone dare to contradict the obvious truth when He explained what He Himself said? When the Lord explained this parable, he said: He who sows good seed is the Son of man, proving himself. The good seed is the children of the kingdom, that is, the Church of the saints. The tares are the children of the wicked, and the field is the world. See, brothers, how both good seed and tares were sown throughout the world. Perhaps wheat was sown in part of it and in Haec est Ecclesia sanctorum, Ecclesia frumentorum toto terrarum orbe diffusorum; per agrum Domini seminata, quod est hic mundus, ipso Domino exponente, cum de seminante diceret: Quia «homo seminavit bonum semen in agro suo, et venit inimicus, et superseminavit zizania; et dixerunt servi patrifamilias, Nonne bonum semen seminasti in agro tuo? unde hic sunt zizania? Respondit Ule, Inimicus homo hoc fecit. Voluerunt colligere zizania, et compescuit illos say: «Sinite utraque crescere usque ad messem; et in tempore messis dicam messoribus, Colligite primum zizania, et alligate fasciculus ad comburendum ea; triticum autem meum reponite in hórreo». Post interrogaverunt eum discipuli dicentes: Narra nobis parabolam zizaniorum. Et ipse exponit omnia, ut nullus homo cordi suo tribuat quod ibi intellexerit, sed Magistro caeli exponenti.

Nemo dicat: Exposuit sibi quomodo voluit. Si parabolam prophetae exposeet Dominus, quando ipse per eos loquebatur quod dicebant; quis auderet dicere, non sic shall I expose? Multo magis, quando ipse exposuit quod proposuit ipse, quis audet contradicere manifestae veritati? Cum ergo hanc parabolam Dominus exponeet, ait, Qui autem seminal bonum semen, est Filius hominis: se utique demonstrans. Bonum vero semen, filii sunt regni: ipsa est Ecclesia sanctorum. Zizania autem, filii sunt maligni. Ager est hic mundus (Mt 13,24-30,36-38). Iam videte, fratres, quia per mundum seminatum est bonum semen, et per
