part the tares? Wheat was sown all over the world and tares all over it. The Lord's field is the world, not Africa. This land is not the Lord's field, since Getulia produces sixty or a hundred times one, and Numidia ten times one. The Lord's produces fruit everywhere a hundredfold, sixtyfold, and thirtyfold. You see which one you want to be if you plan to belong to the fruit of the Lord. Therefore the Church of the saints is the Catholic Church. The Church of the saints is not that of heretics. The Church of the saints is that which God predicted before it appeared, since he presented it so that it would be known. The Church of the saints was previously found in the codices, but now it is found among the people. The Church of the Saints used to be only read, now it is read and seen. When it was only read, it was believed, and when it was seen, it was challenged! His praise is found in the Church of the saints. 4 [v.2]. Let Israel rejoice in its Maker. What does Israel mean? He who sees God. This means Israel. He who sees God rejoices in Him for whom he was made. But, brothers: is it because I said that we belong to the Church of the saints that we already see God? So how are we Israel if we don't see God? There is a vision appropriate to this time and there will be another to come. The current vision is given through faith; the future, for reality. Now, if we believe, we see; If we love, we see. What do we see? Bye bye. Where is God? Ask Saint John. God is charity. Let us bless his holy name; and we will rejoice in God if we rejoice in charity. What do we send mundum seminata sunt zizania. Numquid in parte triticum, et in parte zizania? Per totum triticum, et per totum zizania. Ager Domini mundus est, non Africa. Non quomodo terrae istae: Getulia fert sexagenum aut centenum, et Numidia fert denum: non sic est Deo ager suus. Locate illi fertur fructus, et centenus, et sexagenus, et tricenus: tu tantum vide quid velis esse, si cogitas ad Domini fructum pertinere. Ergo Ecclesia sanctorum, Ecclesia catholica est. Ecclesia sanctorum is not Ecclesia haereticorum. Ecclesia sanctorum illa est quam praesignavit Deus antequam videretur; et exhibituit, ut videretur. Ecclesia sanctorum erat antea in codicibus, moda in gentibus: Ecclesia sanctorum antea tantummodo legebatur, nunc et legitur, et videtur. Quando solum legebatur, credebatur: moda videtur, et contradicitur! Laus eius in Ecclesia sanctorum. 4 [v.2]. Laetetur Israel in eo qui fecit eum. Who is Israel?

Videns Deum: hoc enim interpretatur nomen Israel. Qui videt Deum, in ipso laetetur, a quo factus est. What is this, brothers? quia diximus nos ad Ecclesiam pertinere sanctorum, numquid iam videmus Deum? Quomodo sumus Israel, si non videmus? Est quaedam visio huius temporis; erit alters visio futuri temporis: visio quae moda est, per fidem est; visio quae future est, per speciem erit. If credimus, videmus; yes amamus, videmus. Quid videomus? Deum. Ubi est ipse Deus? Interrogate Ioannem: Deus charitas est (1 lo 4,16). Benedicamus nomen eius sanctum; et gaudeamus in Deo, si gaudemus in charitate. Quisquís habet charitatem, utquid illum mittimus longe, ut videat Deum? Conscientiam suam atten-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

far away, to see God, who has charity? Look at your conscience, and there you will see God. If you do not have charity, God does not dwell there; If charity dwells in him, God also dwells in him. Maybe he wants to see him sitting in heaven; have charity, and you will dwell in it as in heaven. Then let us be Israel and rejoice in our Maker. Let Israel rejoice in its Maker. Be glad in your Maker, not in Arius, not in Donatus, not in Caecilian, not in Proculian, not in Augustine. Be glad in your Maker. I, brothers, do not recommend myself to you, but I recommend you to God, because I recommend you to Him. Why do I recommend you to God? So that you love him for your own good, not for his good; because, if you do not love him, you do not love him for your harm, not for his harm. God will not diminish in his divinity because man does not love him. You grow for God; He does not grow because of you; and yet he so loved us before we loved him that he sent his only Son to die for us. He who made us, became among us. How did he make us? All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made. How did it happen between us? And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. Therefore He is the one in whom we must rejoice, from Him comes the joy that makes us blessed. Let Israel rejoice in its Maker. 5. And the children of Zion rejoice in their King. Israel are the children of the Church. As Zion was a city already destroyed, the saints temporarily dwell in its ruins; but the true Zion and the true Jerusalem, because Zion is Jerusalem, is found dat, et ibi videt Deum. Si charitas ibi non habitat, non ibi habitat Deus: si autem charitas ibi habitat, Deus ibi habitat. Vult illum forte videre sedentem in cáelo; habeat charitatem, et in eo habitat sicut in cáelo. Ergo simus Israel, et laetemur in eo qui fecit nos: Laetetur Israel in eo qui fecit eum. In eo qui fecit cum laetetur, non in Ario, non in Donato, non in Caeciliano; non in Proculiano, non in Augustino: In eo laetetur qui fecit eum. Nos, fratres, non vobis commendamus; sed commendamus vobis Deum, quia commendamus vos Deo. Quomodo vobis Deum commendamus? Ut diligatis eum bono vestro, non bono ipsius: quia malo vestro eum non diligítis, non malo ipsius. Non enim minus habebit Deus divinitatem, si homo in illum non habeat charitatem. Tu crescis ex Deo, non ille ex te: et tamen tantum nos dilexit prior (1 lo 4,19), antequam eum diligeremus, ut Filium suum unicum mitteret moti pro nobis (lo 3,16).

Qui fecit nos, factus est Inter nos. How do we ipse fecit? Omnia per ipsum facta sunt, et sine ipso factum est nihil. Quomodo factus est inter nos? Et Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (ib. 1,3.14). Ergo ipse est in quo debenmus laetari. Nemo homo sibi arroget parts ipsius; ab ipso est laetitia quae facit us happy: Laetetur Israel in eo qui fecit eum. 5. Et filii Sion exsultent in rege suo. Ipse Israel, filii Ecclesiae sunt. Quia Sion fuet quidem una civitas, quae cecidit: in eius reliquiis inhabitant quidem sancti temporaliter; thirst Sion vera et Ierusalem vera (quia ipsa Sion, quae Ierusalem), aeterna est in caelis, quae est mater nostra
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

in heaven, who is our mother. She begot us, she is the Church of the saints, she nourished us; partly pilgrim and mostly residing in the heavens. The part that is in heaven is made up of the blessed angels, and the part that is a pilgrim in the world is made up of the hopeful saints. Of the first it was said: Glory to God in the highest; of the second: and on earth peace to men of good will. Those who groan in this life and long for that country, run with love, not with bodily feet; do not look for ships, but for wings; take the two wings of charity. What are these two wings? The love of God and neighbor. We wander, we sigh, we groan; but we received letters from our homeland; we read them to you. 6. Let Israel rejoice in their Maker, and the children of Zion rejoice in their King. It is the same in its Maker as in its King. Israel is also the same as the children of Zion. The Son of God, who made us, was made among us and rules us by being our King, because he made us by being our Creator. He who made us is the same one who governs us; hence we are Christians, because He is Christ. Christ is derived from "chrism", that is, from "anointing". In ancient times, kings and priests were anointed. He was anointed king and priest. As king he fought for us; as a priest he offered himself for us. When he fought for us he appeared defeated, but he won. He was crucified, and from his cross, on which he was elevated, he killed the devil; hence he is our King. How is he a priest? Because he offered himself for us. Give the priest what he must offer. What will man find (Gal 4:26). Ipsa nos genuit, ipsa est Ecclesia sanctorum, ipsa nos nutrivit; ex parte peregrina, ex magna parte immanens in cáelo. Ex parte qua immanet in cáelo, beatitudo Angelorum est: ex parte qua peregrinatur in hoc saeculo, spes est iustorum. De illa dictum est, Gloria in excelsis Deo: de hac dictum est, Et in terra pax hominibus bonae voluntatis (Luke 2:14). Qui ergo in hac vita gemunt, et desiderant illam patriam, current dilectione, non pedibus corporis: non quaerant naves, sed pennas; duas alas charitatis apprehendant. Quae sunt duae alae charitatis? Dilectio Dei, et proximi. Peregrinamur enim, suspiramus, gemimus. Venerunt ad nos Litterae de patria nostra, ipsas vobis recitamus. 6. Laetetur Israel in eo qui fecit eum, et filii Sion exsultent in rege suo. Quod dixit, qui fecit eum; hoc dixit, in rege suo.

Quod audistis, Israel; id sunt, filii Sion: et quod audistis, in eo qui fecit eum; hoc est, in rege suo. Filius Dei qui fecit nos, factus est inter nos: et Rex noster regit nos, quia Creator noster fecit nos. Ipse est tamen per quem facti sumus, qui est per quem nos regimur: et ideo Christiani, quia ille Christus. Christus a gossip dictus est, id est, ab unctione. Reges autem ungebantur (1 Reg 10,1; et 16,13) et priests (Ex 30,30): iUe vero unctus est et Rex et Sacerdos. Rex pugnavit pro nobis, Sacerdos obtulit se pro nobis. Quando pro nobis pugnavit, quasi victus est; I will see autem vicit. Crucifixus est enim, et de cruz sua, in qua erat fixus, diabolum

What can I deliver as a pure victim? What victim will he find? What pure thing can the sinner present? Oh wicked one, oh wicked one! Unclean is whatever you contribute, and yet something pure must be offered for you. Look in yourself for what you must offer; you won't find it. Look among your possessions for what you should sacrifice: he does not like rams, goats, or bulls. All this is His, even if you don't offer it to Him. Offer him pure sacrifice. But you are a sinner, you are impious, your conscience is stained. You may be able to offer him something pure if you are purified; But to be so, something must be offered for you. What must you offer for yourself so that you can be purified? If you are pure, you will be able to offer what is pure. Then let the pure priest offer himself and purify. Well, this is what Christ did. He found nothing pure in men that he could offer for men; Then He offered Himself, a most pure victim. Oh happy victim, true victim, immaculate victim! Then he didn't offer what we gave him. What do I say? He offered what he took from us and offered it pure. He took the meat from us and offered it. But where did he take it from? From the womb of the Virgin Mary to offer her pure for the impure. He is King, he is Priest; let us rejoice in Him. 7 [v.3]. Praise his name in chorus. What is a choir? Many know what it is; Precisely, as I speak in the city, without a doubt, almost everyone knows it. Choir is a group of singers who sing together. If we sing in choir, let's sing harmoniously. Anyone who disagrees with the voice in the choir of singers offends the occidit: et inde Rex noster. Where are Priests? Quia se pro nobis obtulit. Date Priest quod offerat. Quid inveniret homo quod daret mundam victimam? Who victimized us? Quid mundum potest efferre peccator? Either inique, or impie! quidquid attuleris immundum est, et aliquid mundum pro te offerendum est. Quaere apud te quid offeras; do not invenies. Quaere ex te quod offeras; non delectatur arietibus, nec hircis, nec tauris. Omnia ipsius sunt, etsi non offeras. Offer ergo illi mundum sacrificium. Sed peccator es, impius es, sed inquinatam conscientiam habes. Poteris forte aliquid mundum offerre, purgatus; sed ut purgeris, aliquid pro te offerendum est. Quid ergo pro te oblaturus es, ut munderis? If mundatus es, poteris offerre quod mundum est. Offerat ergo seipsum mundus sacerdos, et mundet. Hoc est quod fecit Christus. Nihil mundum invenit in hominibus, quod offerret pro hominibus; seipsum obtulit mundam victiman.

Félix victim, vera victim, immaculata host! Non ergo hoc obtulit quod nos illi dedimus: imo hoc obtulit quod a nobis accepit, et mundum obtulit. Carnem enim a nobis accepit, hanc obtulit. Sed unde illam accepit? De uterus virginis Mariae, ut mundam offerret pro immundis. Ipse Rex, ipse Sacerdos; in eo laetemur. 7 [v.3]. Laudent nomen eius in choro. What chorus does it mean? Multi noverunt chorum; et quia in civitate loquimur, prope omnes norunt. Chorus est consensio cantantium. Si in choro cantamus, concorditer cantemus. In choro cantantium quisquís voce discrepuerit, offen-
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

heard and disturbs the choir. If the voice of the one who sings, out of tune, disturbs the harmonious song, how will the dissonant heresy not disturb the harmony of those who praise? The choir of Christ is now made up of the entire world. The choir of Christ resounds from the east to the west. For another psalm says: From the rising of the sun until the setting, praise the name of the Lord. Praise his name in chorus. 8. With tympanum and psaltery they praise him. Why does he reach for the tympanum and the psaltery? So that he not only praises the voice, but also the work. When the psaltery and the tympani are taken, the hands accompany the voice. This will happen to you if, when you sing the hallelujah, you give bread to the hungry, you clothe the naked and welcome the pilgrim, for then not only will the voice sound, but the hands will accompany it, because the works agree with the voices. You took the musical instrument, and the fingers accompany the tongue. Nor should the mystery that the psaltery and the tympanum contain remain silent. The leather is stretched on the tympanum or drum and the strings are stretched on the psaltery; In both instruments, therefore, the flesh is crucified. How well he sang with the psaltery and the tympanum who said: The world is crucified for me, and I for the world! The one who loves the new song, the one who teaches you when he says: Whoever wants to be my disciple, let him deny himself, take up his cross and follow me, wants you to take up the psaltery along with the timpani. Do not abandon your psaltery, do not abandon your tympanum or drum; let it spread on the log and dry up as for the lust of the flesh, for the more the nerves are stretched, dit auditum, et perturbat chorum. Si vox inconvenience cantantis disturbat concentum cantantium, quomodo disturbat haeresis dissonans concentum laudantium? Chorus Christi iam totus mundus est. Chorus Christi ab oriente in occidentem consonat. Videamus si tantum extenditur chorus Christi. Dicit psalmus alius: A solis ortu usque ad occasum laúdate nomen Bomini (Ps 112,3). Laudent nomen eius in choro. 8. In tympano et psalterio psallant ei. Quare assumeit tympanum et psalterium? Ut non sola vox laudet, sed et opera. Quando assumitur tympanum et psalterium, manus concinunt voci. Sic et tu, si when Alleluia you sing, porrigas et panem esurienti, you were wearing nudum, suscipias peregrinum; non sola vox sonat, sed et manus consonat, quia verbis facta concordant. Assumpsisti organum, et consentiunt digiti linguae. Et ipsum mysterium tympani et psalterii non est tacendum.

In tympano corium extenditur, in psalterio chordae extenduntur: in utroque organ caro crucifigitur. Quam bene psallebat in tympano et psalterio, qui dicebat: Mihi mundus crucifixus est, et ego mundo! (Gal 6:14). Ipsum psalterium, velut tympanum tollere te vult, qui amat canticum novum, qui te docet quando tibi dicit: Qui vult esse meus discipulus, abneget semetipsum, et tollat ​​cruzem suam, et sequatur me (Mt 16:24). Non dimittat psalterium suum, non dimittat tympanum: extendatur in ligno, et siccetur a concupiscentia carnis. Nervi quanto plus fuerint ex-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

the sharper they sound. So that the psaltery of the apostle Saint Paul sounded sharp, what did he say? Forgetting what is behind and reaching out to what is ahead, I continue running towards the goal of the supreme vocation. He spread out; Christ touched him, and the sweetness of the truth resounded. With the tympanum and the psaltery they praise him. 9 [v.4]. Because the Lord benefited his people. What greater benefit than dying for the wicked? What greater benefit could he do than to erase with the blood of the Just the decree of condemnation of the sinner? What greater benefit than to say: "I am not interested in what you were; be what you were not?" The Lord benefited his people by forgiving their sins and promising them eternal life. He does good by converting the section, helping the combatant, crowning the winner. The Lord benefited his people. And he will exalt the meek to health. The proud are also exalted, but not for health. The meek are for health; the proud, to death; That is, the proud exalt themselves, but the Lord humbles them; The meek, on the other hand, humble themselves, but God exalts them. And he will exalt the meek for health. 10 [v.5-6]. And the saints will rejoice in glory. I want to tell you something. Hear carefully about the glory of the saints. There is no one who does not love glory. But the glory of fools, that which is called popular or worldly, carries with it the attraction of deception; so that, an individual, moved by the praise of vain men, wants to live in such a way that he se tenti, tan acutus sonant. Ut ergo acute sonaret Pauli apostoli psalterium, quid dixit? Quae retro oblitus, in ea quae ante sunt extentus, sequor ad palmam supernae vocationis (Phil 3:13-14). Extendit se ipse; tetigit Christus, et sonavit dulcedo veritatis. In tympano et psalterio psallant ei. 9 [v.4]. Quoniam benefecit Dominus in populo suo. Quid tam beneficum, quam morí pro impiis? quid tam beneficum, quam sanguine iusto delere chirographum peccatoris? quid tam beneficum, quam dicere: Non ad me pertinet quod fuestis; This is what you were not? Benefecit Dominus in populo suo, resigning peccata, promittendo vitam aeternam. Benefacit aversum convertere, pugnantem adiuvare, vincentem coronare: Benefecit Dominus in populo suo. And exaltabit mansuetos in salute. Exaltantur enim et superbi, sed non in salute.

Mansueti in salute, superbi in morte: id est, superbi ipsi se exaltant, et Dominus eos humiliat; mansueti autem ipsi se humiliant, et Deus eos exaltat. And exaltabit mansuetos in salute. 10 [v.5.6]. Exsultabunt sancti in gloria. Aliquid flew dicere; audite attentius de gloria sanctorum. Nemo est enim qui non amet gloriam. Sed gloria stultorum, popularis illa quae dicitur, habet illecebram deceptionis, ut ad laudes vanorum hominum quisque commotus, velit sic vivere, ut praedicetur ab hominibus quibuscumque, quornodocumque.
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

speak of him in any way and by any kind of men. Hence, men becoming foolish and inflated with vanity, empty inside and swollen outside, they dare to lose their property, giving it to comedians, comedians, gladiators, charioteers. How many goods they donate, how many goods they spend! They squander their assets, not so much the patrimonial ones as the spiritual ones. These despise the poor, because the populace does not shout for the poor to receive; However, the populace shouts for the gladiator to receive. These, then, when they do not cry out for the poor, do not want to give; and, when people cry out for the foolish, they go crazy, and in this way they all become foolish: the gladiator, the spectator, and the giver. The Lord reproaches this crazy glory; it is reproved in the presence of the Almighty. However, my brothers, Christ, citing the similarity of this fact, reproaches his people in such a way that he says to them: "I did not receive from you as much as the gladiators received, even though you gave them what was mine to reward them; but I was naked, and you did not clothe me." They will say to him: When did we see you naked and not clothe you? And He will answer them: When you did not do this to my little ones, you did not do it to me. You want to dress the one you like. Who do you dislike Christ in? Do you want to dress the gladiator, for whom perhaps, defeated, you will be ashamed? Christ is never defeated; defeat the devil; and conquers him for you, for you and in you. Don't you want to dress such a winner? Because? Because they barely shout, they barely go crazy for Him. For this reason, those who delight in such glory have nothing on their conscience. Just as Hinc nomines insani effecti, et inflati typho, inanes intus, foris tumidi, etiam res suas will lose volunt, donando scenicis, histrionibus, venatoribus, aurigis. How much donation! quanta impendunt! Effundunt vires, non patrimonii tantum, sed etiam animi sui. Isti fastidiunt pauperem, quia non clamat populus, ut pauper accipiat; clamat autem populus, ut venator accipiat. lili ergo ubi eis non clamatur, nolunt erogare: ubi clamatur ab insanis, insaniunt; et fiunt omnes insani, et qui spectatur, et qui spectat, et qui donat. Insane this glory reprehenditur Domino, improbatur ante oculos Omnipotentis. Et tamen, fratres mei, Christus sic imptoperat suis, et dicit: Non a vobis accepi tantum, quantum acceperunt venatores; et lilis ut donaretis, de meo donasüs: ego autem nudus eram, et non vestistis me.

Et illi: Et quando te vidimus nudum, et non vestimus te? Et ille: Cum uni ex minimis meis non fecistis, nec mibi fecistis (Mt 25,43-45). Sed eum vis ropa, qui tibi placet: in quo tibi Christus displicet? I will dress vis venatorem, quo forte victo erubescas: Christus nunquam vincitur; et diabolum vicit, et pro te vicit, et tibi vicit, et in te vicit. Talem victorem I will dress non vis. Quare? Quia minus clamatur, quia minus insanitur. Propterea isti qui tali gloria delectantur, in conscientia sua nihil habent. Quomodo exhauriunt arcas, ut vestes

They leave the coffers empty to deliver the clothes, thus leaving the conscience exhausted, so that there is nothing of value in it. 11. It is not necessary for me to say how the saints who rejoice in glory rejoice. Listen to the following verse of the psalm: The saints will rejoice in glory; They will rejoice in their homes. Not in the theaters or amphitheatres, not in the circuses, in the frivolities, in the forum, but in their dwellings. What does it mean in their homes? In their hearts. Hear the apostle Saint Paul rejoice in his dwelling: Our glory consists in the testimony of our conscience. On the other hand, it is to be feared that someone may take pleasure in himself and, as if conceited, may boast. Therefore each one should rejoice with fear, since it is due to the gift of God, not his desert, to rejoice. Indeed there are many who please themselves and consider themselves righteous. These are met by another passage of Scripture, saying: Who will glory in having a pure heart or who will glory in being clean from sin? There is a certain standard for boasting about conscience. It consists of knowing that your faith is sincere; your hope, certain, and your charity, without fiction. But since there are still many things that may perhaps offend God's children, praise God who gave you these things, and then you will perfect what he gave you. Therefore, after having said: They will rejoice in their dwellings, so that some might not think that they pleased themselves, he added immediately: The rejoicings of God (are) in their mouth. They rejoice so much in their homes that they do not claim to be good, but rather that they are mittant; sic exinaniunt ipsam conscientiam, ut nihil ibi habeant pretiosum. 11. Sancti autem qui exsultant in gloria, quomodo exsultent, non opus est ut nos dicamus; ipsius Psalmi audite sequentem versum: Exsultabunt sancti in gloria: laetabuntur in cubilibus suis. Non in theatris, non in amphitheaters, non in circis, non in nugis, non in foris; thirst, in cubilibus suis. Quid est, in cubilibus suis? In cordibus suis. Audi apostolum Paulum exsultantem in cubili suo: Nam gloria nostra haec est, testimonium conscientiae nostrae (2 Cor 1:12). Rursum timendum est ne quisque apud seipsum fiat sibi placens, et quasi superbus de conscientia sua glorietur. Debet enim quisque cum tremore exsultare (Ps 2:11); quia donum Dei est unde exsultat, non meritum suum.

Etenim sunt multi sibi pleasantes, et iustos se esse arbitrantes; et proceedit adversus they on the page say: Quis gloriabitur castum se habere cor; aut quis gloriabitur mundum se esse a sin? (Prov 20:9). Est ergo quidam modus in conscientia gloriandi, ut noveris fidem tuam esse sinceram, noveris esse spem tuam certam, noveris charitatem tuam esse sine simulatíone. Sed quoniam fines sunt adhuc forte quae possunt offendere oculos Dei, lauda Deum qui tibí ista donavit; tune perficiet quod donavit. Propterea cum dixisset, Laetabuntur in cubilibus suis; ne quasi sibi pleasurentes viderentur, adiunxit statim, Exsultationes Dei
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

they praise Him from whom they received what they are; to Him by whom they are called to achieve what they are not yet and from whom they expect perfection, to whom they give thanks because he initiated (this perfection). The joys of God (are) in his mouth. Look now at the saints; see his glory throughout the world; see, finally, that the joys of God are in his mouth. 12. And a two-stranded sword in his hands. What the common people call a rapier is called a two-edged sword. There are single-edged swords; These are the sabers. But the two-edged sword is also the spear, it is the rapier. These types of weapons, which are sharp on both sides, contain a great mystery. This two-edged sword is in his hands. The word of the Lord is a two-edged sword. It is one sword, but at the same time there are many swords, because there are many mouths and tongues of the saints. The word of God, says Saint Paul, is a two-edged sword. How is it a two-edged sword? Because he speaks of temporal and eternal things, and in both cases he proves what he says; and he who hurts is separated from the world. Is this sword of which the Lord says: I did not come to bring peace, but a sword? See how he came to separate, to separate. Remove the saints, remove the wicked, remove from you what makes you pregnant. The son wants to serve God, the father does not: the sword came, the word of God came, and separated the son from the father. The daughter longs to love God, the mother does not want to: the sword separates the two. The daughter-in-law wants to serve God, the mother-in-law does not want to. In short, let the two-edged sword approach and offer the promise of the present and future life, the consolation of in faucibus eorum. Sic laetabuntur in cubilibus suis, ut non sibi tribuant quod boni sunt, sed illum laudent a quo acceperunt quod sunt, a quo vocantur ut perveniant ad id quod nondum sunt, et a quo sperant perfectionem; cui gratias agunt, quia inchoavit: Exsultationes Dei in faucibus eorum. Iam videte sanctos, videte gloriam eorum, videte per universum mundum, videte quod exsultationes Dei sint in faucibus eorum. 12. Et frameae bis acutae in manibus eorum. Framea appellatur quam vulgo spatham dicunt. Sunt enim gladii ex una parte acutí, ipsae sunt machaereae. Ipsae autem frameae, ípsae et romphaeae, ipsae etiam spathae appellantur. Magnum mysterium habet hoc genus ferramenti, quod ex utraque parte acutum est. Ipsae frameae sunt bis acutae in manibus eorum.

Frameas bis acutas intelligimus sermonem Domini: et una framea est; sed ideo munal dicuntur, quia mula ora sunt, et mulae linguae sanctorum. Sermo ergo Dei, gladius bis acutus (Hebr 4:12). Unde bis acutus? Dicit de temporalibus, dicit de aeternis. In utroque probat quod dicit, et eum quem ferit, separate the world. Nonne ipse est gladius, de quo Dominus dicit: Non veni pacem mittere in terram sed gladium? (Mt 10,34). Attende quomodo venit disiungere, quomovenit separare. Disiungit holy, disiungit impios, separate you or impedit you. Filius vult I serve Deo, pater non vult: venit gladius, sermo Dei; dividet filium a patre. Filia vult, mater non vult;

temporal things, and the joy of eternal things: here you have the two-edged sword promising the temporal and the eternal. How did he deceive us? Isn't the Church of God spread throughout the world? See that it is so. Before it was read and not seen; Now, as it is read, it is seen. Everything temporal that we were promised belongs to one edge of the sword, and everything eternal to the other. You have, therefore, the hope of future things and the consolation of present things; Do not let yourself be seduced by the one who wants to separate you. Whether it is the father, the mother, the mother-in-law, the wife or the friend who wishes to separate you, do not separate yourself, and the two-edged sword will serve you well. She usefully separates you; you join badly. Then the Lord came bringing the two-edged sword: promising eternal things and fulfilling temporal things. That is why there are also two Testaments. What also symbolizes the two-edged sword in his hands? The two Testaments. To them belongs the two-edged sword. The Old promises earthly things, and the New promises eternal things. In both the word of God was shown to be true, like a two-edged sword. Why in the hands and not in the tongues, since it says: and a two-edged sword in his hands? He said in his hands as if he had said in power. Then they received the word of God in power so that wherever they wanted and to whom they wanted they could speak without fearing human powers, without despising the helpless. In their hands, then, they had the sword with which they prepared, agitated, drove and wounded, since all this was in the power of the preachers. If the word had not been in his possession, wouldn't someone perhaps say: dividuntur ab invicem. Nurus vult, socrus non vult; veniat gladius bis acutus, affetat promissionem vitae praesentis etfuturae, consolátionem temporalium, aeternorum perfruitionem. Ecce gladius ex utraque parte acutus, promittens temporalia et aeterna. In what do we feel? Nonne Ecclesia Dei per totum mundum non erat? Ecce est. Antea legebatur, et non videbatur: moda sicut legitur, ita cernitur. Quidquid temporaliter nobis promissum est, ad unam partem gladií pertinet: quidquid in sempiternum, ad alteram partem gladii pertinet. Habes spemfuturarum rerum, habes consolationem praesentium; noli retrahi ab eo qui vult retrahere: pater, mater, sóror, uxor sit, amicus sit, non te retrahat; et utilis tibi crit gladius bis acutus. Utiliter te Ule separat, male te tu conglutinas.

Venit ergo Dominus noster ferens gladium bis acutum, promittens aeterna, implens temporalia. Nam ideo et duo Testamenta dicuntur. Quae erant ergo frameae bis acutae in manibus eorum? Duo Testamenta ad gladium bis acutum pertinent: Vetus Testamentum terrena promittit, Novum aeterna. In utroque sermo Dei verax inventus est, ut gladius bis acutus. Quare ergo in manibus, et non in linguis? Et frameae bis acutae, inquít, in manibus eorum. In manibus dixit, in poJ testate. Acceperunt ergo sermonem Dei in potestate, ut ubi vellent dicerent, cui vellent dicerent; non timerent potestatem, non contemnerent paupertatem. In manibus enim habebant gladium, qua volebant, vibrabant, versabant, percutiebant: et hoc totum erat in potestate praedi-

"How the word is a two-edged sword and how it is found in the hand"? If the word had not been in the hands, why was it written: The word of the Lord became in the hands of Haggai the prophet? Did God, my brothers, place his word in the hands of Haggai? What does it mean he made a word in his hands? That he was given power to preach the word of the Lord. Anyway, we can also understand these hands in another way; namely: those who spoke had the word of the Lord on their tongues, and those who wrote had it in their hands. And the two-edged sword (is) in his hands. 13 [v.7]. You see, brothers, the saints are armed; See the carnage, see the glorious battles. If there is an emperor, there are also soldiers; If there are soldiers, there are also enemies; and, if there is war, there is also victory. Why do these who have two-edged swords in their hands fight? Will avenge the nations. See if vengeance was not taken among the nations. Every day this takes place; I also do this when speaking. See how the people of Babylon are destroyed and a double is given to her, for thus it was written of this Babylon: And a double was given to her, according to her works. How do you double it? The saints fight, wield their two-edged swords, and carry out ruin, death, separation. How was it given to you? She persecuted Christians, killed the flesh, but did not put down God. Now they pay him back twice as much, since they kill the pagans and break the idols. "How, you say, do pagans die?" Becoming Christians. I look for the pagan and I don't find him; He is already a Christian. Then cantium. Nam si non est in manibus sermo: ne forte aliquis dicat, Quomodo sermo est gladius bis acutus, et quomodo in manibus? si ergo sermo non est in manibus, quare scriptum est, Factus est sermo Domini in manu Aggaei prophetae? (Agg 1,1). Numquid, fratres, sermonem suum Deus in digitis ipsius fecit? Quid est, in manu ipsius Cactus est? In potestate illi datum est praedicare sermonem Domini. Postremo possumus etiam has manus aliter intelligere. Nam qui locuti sunt, in lingua habuerunt sermonem Dei; qui scripserunt, in manibus: Et frameae bis acutae in manibus eorum. 13 [v.7]. Iam, fratres, videtis sanctos armatos; attendite strages, attendite gloriosa praelia. Si enim imperator, et miles; yes thousands, et hostis; yes bellum, et victory. Quid fecerunt isti habentes in manibus frameas bis acutas? Ad faciendam vindictam in gentibus. Videte si non est vindicta facta in gentibus.

Quotidie ipsa fit; hoc agimus et nos loquendo. Attendite quomodo caesae sunt gentes Babyloniae. lili tedditur duplum: sic enim de illa scriptum est, Reddite illi duplum, ad quod fecit (Rev 18:6). How do redditur duplum? Bellant sancti, educunt frameas bis acutas; fiunt strages, fiunt occisions, separations: quomodo illi duplum redditur? Illa quando poterat persequi Christianos, carnem occidebat, Deum non confringebat: moda illi duplum redditur; et Pagani exstinguuntur, et idola franguntur. Quomodo, inquies, Pagani occiduntur? Quomodo, nisi cum Christiani fiunt? Quaero paganum, non invenio;

the pagan died. If they did not kill each other, how is it that he said to Saint Peter: Kill and eat? Hence Saul was killed as a persecutor and was raised up as a preacher. I look for Saul the pursuer and I don't find him; was killed. As? With the two-edged sword. But since he was killed in himself, as to what he was, and was made alive in Christ, therefore, full of confidence, he says: I live, but no longer I, but Christ lives in me. As it happened to him, so it will be done for him. In fact, upon being made a preacher, he also received the two-edged sword into his hands to execute vengeance on the nations. But lest you think that men were wounded by the sword, in such a way that they shed blood and received wounds in the flesh, the psalmist continues and says: Reproofs among the people. What is rebuke? Correction. Wield the two-edged sword, do not give up; God gave it to you according to your ability. What man are you that you worship idols? Tell your friend, if there is still any, to whom you say: "What man are you that you abandoned Him by whom you were created and worship what you made? Better is the craftsman than what the craftsman makes." You are ashamed to worship the craftsman, and are you not ashamed to worship what the craftsman made? When he begins to blush, when he begins to repent, then you strike with the sword; He reached the heart, and he will die to live. The two-edged sword in his hands, to avenge the nations and rebuke the people. 14 [v.8]. To imprison their kings with fetters, and their nobles with iron handcuffs. So that they may carry out with them the christianus est: ergo mortuus est paganus. Nam si non occiduntur, unde dictum est Petro: Macta et manduca? (Acts 10,13). Unde ipse Saulus occisus est persecutor, et Paulus erectus est praedicator? Quaero Saulum persecutorem, et non invenio; occisus est. Where? De framea bis acuta. Sed quia occisus est in se, et vivificatus est in Christo, ideo confidens dicit: Vivo autem iam non ego; vivit autem in me Christus (Gal 2:20). Quomodo illi fit, sic per illum. Etenim cum factus esset praedicator, accepit et ipse in manibus frameam bis acutam, ad faciendam vindictam in gentibus. Et ne veré tu putares homines ferro percutí, sanguinem fundi, vulnera in carne fieri, sequitur, et exponit: Obiurgationes in populis.' Obiurgatio quae est? Correptio. Procedat ex vobis framea bis acuta nolite cessare; dedít illam vobis Deus pro module vestro. Qualis homo' es, qui idola colis?

Dic amico tuo, si tamen remansit cuidicas: Qualis homo es, qu dimisisti eum a quo factus es, et adoras quod fecisti? Melior est faber, quam quod fabricat faber. Si fabrum adorare erubescis, quod faber fecit, non erubescis? Cum coeperit erubescere, cum coeperit compungí, fecisti vulnus de framea; pervenit ad cor, monturas est ut vívat: Frameae bis acutae in manibus eorum, ad faciendam vindictam in gentibus, obiurgationes in populis. 14 [v.3]. Ut alligent reges eorum in compedibus, et nobiles eorum in vinculis ferréis. Ut faciant in eis iudicium conscriptum. Easy expo-
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

judgment decreed. I easily explained how with the two-edged sword they fall to rise, they are separated to be gathered, they are wounded to heal and they are killed to live. But what will I do? How will I explain: To imprison their kings with fetters? The kings of the nations must be imprisoned with chains, and their nobles with wives, and also with iron. Pay attention so that you understand what you know. These little verses that I began to expound are obscure, but what I have to say about them is not something new; you already know it. Now you do not need to learn, but only to remember. The Lord wanted to present certain obscure verses, not in order to extract something new from them, but to innovate with an obscure exposition what was already known. We know that kings and Gentile nobles became Christians. They are today, they were and they will be, because the two-edged sword from the hand of the saints does not fail. But how do we understand that they are tied with iron shackles and handcuffs? Your charity and erudition know, since you have been nurtured in the Church and are accustomed to hearing the divine lesson, that God chose the weakness of the world to confuse the strong; and the foolish things of the world, to shame the wise; and what is not, as if it were, to destroy what is. For thus says the Apostle: See, brothers, your vocation or calling; There are not many wise according to the flesh, nor many powerful, nor many noble; Rather, God chose the foolish and the weak in the world to confound the strong; and he also chose what is ignoble and despicable and what is not, as if it were, to destroy what is. Christ God came to take advantage of tosuimus quomodo de frameis cadant ut exsurgant, separentur ut congregentur, vulnerentur ut sanentur, moriantur ut vivant: sed quid faciemus? quomodo exponemus, Ad alligandos reges eorum in compedibus? Reges gentium alligandi in compedibus; et nobiles eorum in vinculis, addidit ferris. Adestote, ut agnoscatis quod nostis. Isti enim versus quos coepimus exposed, obscuri sunt; sed illud quod ex illis dicturus sum, non est novum. Iam notum est vobis; moda non discere opus habetis, sed commemorari. Ad hoc autem voluit Deus obscure will pone quosdam versus suos, non ut aliquid novum de illis eruatur; sed ut quod iam usitatum erat, obscuris expositis innovetur. Novimus reges factos christianos, novimus nobiles gentium factos christianos. Sunt today, et fuerunt, et erunt; et non cessant frameae bis acutae in manibus sanctorum.

Quomodo ergo ligatos compedibus et vinculis ferréis intelligimus? Scit Chantas vestra et eruditio (quia in Ecclesia nutriti estis, et soletis audire divinas lectiones), quoniam infirma mundi elegit Deus, ut confunderet fortia; et stulta mundi elegit Deus, ad confusing sapientes; et ea quae non sunt tanquam ea quae sunt, ut quae sunt evacuentur. Sic enim ait Apostolus: Videre enim vocationem vestram, fratres, quia non multi sapientes secundum carnem, non multi potentes, non multi nobles; sed stulta mundi elegit Deus, et infirma mundi, ut confunderet fortia; et ignobilia et contemptibilia elegit Deus, et ea quae non sunt tanquam ea

two, but he chose the Fisherman to benefit the Emperor, not the Emperor to be useful to the Fisherman; and so he chose what was considered nothing in the world. He filled these with his Spirit, gave them the two-edged sword, commanded them to preach the Gospel and go throughout the world. The world roared, the lion confronted the lamb, and it was seen that the lamb was stronger than the lion. The lion was defeated by being angry, and the lamb conquered by suffering; The hearts of men were converted to the fear of Christ, and the kings and nobles began to be moved by the miracles, to be disturbed by the fulfillment of the prophecies, to see the human race flocking towards a single name. And what did they do? Many chose lowliness or humility, and, abandoning their homes and distributing their property to the poor, they headed toward perfection. For to a certain imperfect man the Lord said: If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have and give it to the poor; and come and follow me, and you will have treasure in heaven. Many nobles did this; but, for the same reason, they stopped being noble among people, since they chose poverty in the world and nobility in Christ. On the contrary, many others retain nobility, royal power, and yet they are Christians. These are the ones who are found tied with fetters and tied with iron handcuffs. And why this? So that, having received the shackles of wisdom, the shackles of the word of God, they do not head towards what is illicit. 15. And why are they tied with iron chains and not gold? They are iron when they fear; love and you will be golden. quae sunt, ut ea quae sunt evacuentur (1 Cor 1:26-28). Venit Deus Christus prodesse omnibus: sed elegit prodesse imperatori de piscatore, non piscatori de imperatore; et elegit ea quae nullius moments weret in mundo. Ipsos implevit Spiritu suo, dedit eis frameas bis acutas, praedicare praecepit Evangelium, et iré per totum orbem terrarum (Mt 28,19). Fremuit mundus, erexit se leo adversus agnum: sed fortior leone inventus est agnus. Leo victus is saeviendo, agnus vicit patiendo. Conversa sunt corda homkmm ad timorem Christi; coeperunt reges, coeperunt nobiles miraculis commoveri, prophetiae adimpletione turbari, videre in unum nomen concurrere genus humanum. Et quid facerent? Multi elegerunt ignobilitatem, et resignientes domos suas, substantias suas distribuentes pauperibus, cucurrerunt ad perfectionem.

Tali enim imperfecto dicitur to Domino: Si vis Perfectas esse, vade, vende omnia quae habes, et da pauperibus; et veni, sequere me, et habebis thesarurum in caelis (ib. 19,21). Multi ex nobilibus fecerunt hoc: sed cessaverunt isti nobiles esse gentium; elegerunt paupertatem in saeculo, nobilitatem in Christo. Multi autem tenent ipsam nobilitatem, tenent regias potestates, et sic sunt christiani. Ipsi sunt tanquam in compedibus, et tanquam in vinculis ferréis. Unde hoc? Ne progrederentur ad illicita, compedes acceperunt; compedes sapientiae, compedes verbi Dei. 15. Quare ergo iron bond, et non golden bond? Ferrea sunt quamdiu timent; ament, et aurea erunt. Attendat Charitas vestra quid
I sing to God and his people, executor of his designs

Let your charity pay attention to what I say. You recently heard the apostle Saint John say: There is no fear in love, because perfect charity casts out fear, since fear has its punishment. This fear is the iron chain; and yet, unless man begins to revere God out of fear, he will not come to love. For the beginning of wisdom is the fear of God. The voice of Christ's justice in the elect is: Mercy and judgment I will sing to you, O Lord!; I will salme and understand on the immaculate path when you come to me. Indeed, through mercy he helps us to carry out justice so that we may present ourselves safely to the judgment, where all those who evangelize wildebeest are exterminated from the city of the Lord, Agite poenitentiam; appropinquavit enim regnum caelorum (Mt 3,2; et 4,17). Iustificamur in vocatione mercye, et timore iudicii: hinc est quod dicitur, Deus, in nomine tuo salvum me fac, et in virtute tua indica me (Ps 53,3). Non timet judicari, qui impetraverit ante salvari. Vocati, renuntiamus diabolo per poenitentiam, ne sub iugo eius remaneamus: iustificati, sanamur per misericordiam, ne iudicium timeamus: glorificad, transimus in vitam aeternam, ubi Deum sine fine laudamus. Ad hoc pertinere arbitror quod Dominus ait: Ecce eiicio daemonia, et sanitates perfido hodie et eras, et tertia consummor (Luke 13:32). Quod etiam in triduo suae passionis et dormitionis et evigilationis ostendit. Crucifixus est enim, et sepultus, et resurrexit.

In the intersection of principibus et potestatibus triumphavit, in sepulcher requievit, in resurrectione exsultavit. Poenitentia cruciat, iustitia tranquillat, vita aeterna glorificat. Poenitentiae vox est: Miserere mei, Deus, secundum magnam misericordiam tuam; et secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum dele iniquitatem meam. Haec offert sacrificium Deo spiritum contribulatum, cor contritum et humiliatum (Ps 50,3.19). Iustitiae Christi vox est in electis suis: Misericordiam et iudicium cantabo tibi, Domine; psallam, et intelligam in via immaculata, quando venies ad me. Per misericordiam quippe adiuvamur ad faciendam iustitiam, ut securi ad iudicium ^veniamus; ubi disperduntur de civitate Domini omnes qui opera-

they work iniquity. The verse with which this psalm concludes (100) is the voice of eternal life. 4 {v.1-2}. Praise the Lord in his saints: certainly in those whom he glorified. Praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him in his powers, or as others recorded: in his potentates. Praise him according to the immensity of his greatness, All these things are his saints, for, as the Apostle says, we are the righteousness of God through Christ. Therefore, if they are the righteousness of God, which He worked in them, why should they not also be the power of God, which He made in them so that they might rise from the dead, since power also stands out in a special way in the resurrection of Christ, since, even when weakness appeared in the passion, according to the Apostle says: If he was crucified in regard to weakness, yet he lives by virtue or the power of God; and in another place it also says: In order to know Him, and the power of His resurrection? Admirably he therefore said: In the firmament of his power, for it is a firmament of power, because he no longer dies and death will no longer have dominion over him from now on. But why then is it not said: To those whom he made in them, when naming the powers of God? Without a doubt, they are His powers, just as we are the righteousness of God in Him, as was said. For what is more powerful than to reign eternally after having defeated all the enemies under your feet? And why should they not also be the immensity of his greatness? But not that by which He is great, but that by which He made them great, and so many, that is, thousands of thousands, just as justice is understood in a way by tur iniquitatem (Ps 100,1-2.8). Quo versu psalmus iste concluditur, vitae aeternae vox est. 4 [v.1.2]. Laúdate Dominum in sanctis eius: utique in eis quos glorificavit. Laúdate eum in firmamento virtutis eius. Praise eum in virtutibus eius; vel, ut alii interpretati sunt, in potentatibus eius. Laúdate eum secundum multitudinem magnitudeinis eius. Omnia ista ipsi sunt sancti eius; quomodo dicit Apostolus: Ut nos simus iustitia Dei in ipso (2 Cor 5,21). Si ergo iustitia Dei quam fecit in eis, cur non et virtus Dei quam fecit in eis, ut resurgerent a mortuis? Nam et in Christi resurrectione virtus máxime commendatur; quia in passione infirmitas Fuit, dicente Apostólo, Etsi crucifixus est ex infirmitate, sed vivit ex virtute Dei (ib. 13,4): et alio loco, Ad cognoscendum, inquit, eum, et virtutem resurrectionis eius (Phil 3,10).

Optime autem ait, In firmamento virtutis eius. Firmamentum est enim virtutis, quia iam non morietur, et mors ei ultra non dominabitur (Rom 6:9). Cur non et potentatus Dei dicantur, quos in eis fecit? Imo ipsi sint potentatus eius; quomodo dictum est, Nos sumus iustitia Dei in ipso. Quid enim potentius, quam regnare in aeternum, sub pedibus positis omnibus inimicis? Cur non ipsi sint etiam muítitudo magnitudeinis eius? Non qua ipse magnus est, sed qua magnos eos fecit, tam multos, hoc est, millia

which He is righteous, and from another what He does in us so that we may be His righteousness. 5. These same saints are symbolized below in all the musical instruments that praise God. For what he recorded in advance saying: Praise the Lord in his saints, he declares immediately, symbolizing his own saints in various ways. 6 [v.3]. Praise him with the sound of a trumpet; This is due to the very clear clarity of the praise. Praise him with the psaltery and the zither. The psaltery praises God in the upper part, and the zither in the lower part, as if God were praised for the heavenly and the terrestrial, as if he were praised because he made heaven and earth. I already said in the exposition of another psalm that the psaltery has the sound box in the upper part, in which the series of strings are fixed so that it produces a stronger and sweeter sound; and the zither has this sound box at the bottom. 7 [v.4]. Praise him with tympanum and dance. The tympanum, atabal or drum praises God when there is no longer any weakness of earthly corruption in the changed flesh, since the drum is made of dried and consolidated skin. The dance or choir praises God when the peaceful society praises Him. Praise Him with strings and organ. The psaltery and the zither that I previously commemorated have strings. The word organ is a generic name for all musical instruments, although the custom is already being acquired of calling musical instruments that are inflated with bellows an organ, but I do not believe that it is designated a solamillium here. Sicut aliter intelligitur iustitia qua est ipse iustus; aliter quam in nobis facit, ut nos simus iustitia eius. 5. Iidem ipsi sancti sunt in ómnibus musicis organis deinceps significad, ad laudandum Deum. Quod enim proposuit says, Laúdate Dominum in sanctis eius, hoc exsequitur, varié significans eosdem ipsos sanctos eius. 6 [v.3]. Laúdate eum in rang tubae: propter laudis excellentissimam claritatem. Laúdate eum in psalterio et cithara. Psalterium est de superioribus laudans Deum, cithara de inferioribus laudans Deum; tanquam de caelestibus et terrestribus, tanquam eum qui fecit caelum et terram. Iam quippe in allio psalmo exposuimus psalterium desuper habere sonorum illud lignum, cui nervorum series, ut meliorem sonum reddat, incumbit: quod lignum cithara inferius habet. 7 [v.4]. Laúdate eum in tympano et choro. Tympanum laudat Deum, eum iam in carne mutata nulla est terrenae corruptionis infirmitas.

De corio quippe fit tympanum exsiccato atque firmato. Chorus laudat Deum, quando laudat eum pacata societas. Laúdate eum in chordis et organ. Chordas habet et psalterium et cithara, quae superius commemorata sunt. Organum autem generale nomen est omnium vasorum musicorum; quamvis iam obtinuerit consuetudo, ut organa proprie dicantur ea quae inflantur follibus: quod genus significatum hic esse non arbitrar. Nam eum organum vocabulum graecum sit, ut dixí, generale omni-

mind this class of musical instruments. Well, the word organ is a Greek word, which, as I said, is a common name that applies to all musical instruments; and the Greeks call those who inflate themselves with bellows by another name. Calling only this type of musical instrument an organ is rather a Latin and popular custom. From what he says: with strings and organ, it seems to me that he meant some other musical instrument that has strings, since not only the psaltery and the zither have strings; But since in the psaltery and in the zither, due to the sound produced, in one in the upper part and in the other in the lower part, something was discovered that can be understood according to this distinction, for the same reason it incites us to look for something else in the same strings, because they are also flesh, but now exempt from corruption. Perhaps he added organ to the word strings so that it would not sound like each one on its own, but so that they would sound together in harmonious diversity, as they are coupled in the organ. For the saints of God will then also have their own consonant differences, not dissonant ones; that is, concordant, not discrepant, just as a very sweet song is produced with various sounds, but without disagreeing with each other. One star differs from another in clarity; so will be the resurrection of the dead. 8 [v.5-6]. Praise him with loud cymbals, praise him with cymbals of joy. Cymbals or cymbals are struck together to make sound; hence by some they were compared to our lips. But I think it should be better understood: that in a certain way God is praised with the cymbals when each one honors his bus musicis instrumentis; hoc cui folies adhibentur, alio Graeci nomine appellant. Ut autem organum dicatur, magis latina et ea vulgaris est consuetudo. Quod ergo ait, in chordis et organ, videtur mihi aliquod organum quod chordas habeat, significare voluíse. Non enim sola psalteria et citharae chordas habent: sed quia in psalterio et cithara, propter sonum ab inferioribus et superioribus, inventum est aliquid quod secundum hance distinctionem possit intelligi, aliud nos in ipsis chordis quaerere admonuit; quia et ipsae sunt caro, sed iam a corruptione liberata. Quibus fortasse ideo addidit organum, non ut singulae sonent, sed ut diversitate concordissima consonent, sicut ordinantur in organ.

Habebunt enim etiam tune sancti Dei differentias suas consonantes, non dissonantes, id est, consentientes, non dissentientes; sicut fit suavissimus concentus ex diversis quidem, sed non inter se adversis sonis. Stella enim a stella differt in claritate; sic et resurrectio mortuorum (1 Cor 15:41-42). 8 [v.5.6]. Laúdate eum in cymbalis bene sonantibus, laúdate eum in cymbalis iubilationis. Cymbala invicem tangunt ut sonent; ideo a quibusdam labiis nostris comparata sunt. Sed melius intelligi puto in cymbalis quodammodo laudare Deum, dum quisque honoratur a proxima suo, non a seipso; et invicem honorantes dant laudem Deo. Ne quis S.Ag. 22

neighbor and not self; and in this way, honoring each other, they praise God. But so that no one would understand that cymbals are instruments that sound without spirit, I think it was added with cymbals of rejoicing. Rejoicing, that is, ineffable praise, only springs from the soul. Nor do I think that what musicians say should be ignored, and it is obvious that there are three kinds of sounds, namely: those produced by the voice, by the breath, and by the pulsation. The one produced by the voice is what is done through the jaws and throat, without any instrument, of the man who sings. The one produced by the breath is the one that is played by the flute or some similar instrument. The one produced by the pulsation is the one that is carried out using the zither or some similar instrument. No kind of sound was omitted here in the psalm. Because the voice is given in the choir; the breath, in the trumpet, and the pulsation, in the zither, as if they were the mind, the spirit and the body, but comparing, not equalizing. What he recorded in advance: Praise the Lord in his saints, to whom did he say it but to them? And in whom was praising God carried out if not in themselves? You, he says, are his saints and his strength, but what he made in you; You are also His power and the immensity of His greatness, but that which He made and manifested in you. You are the trumpet, the psaltery, the zither, the drum, the choir, the strings, the organ, the sonorous cymbal of joy of things that sound good, because they are harmonious. Don't think here of anything vile, anything fleeting, anything comical. And since perceiving according to the flesh is death, let every spirit praise the Lord. autem cymbala intelligeret, quae sine anima sonant, ideo puto additum, in cymbalis iubilationis. Iubilatio namque, id est ineffabilis laus, nonnisi ab anima proficiscitur. Nec praetereundum existimo quod musici dicunt, et res ipsa manifesta est, tria esse genera sonorum; voce, flatu, pulsu: voce, ut est per fauces et arteries, sine organ aliquo cantantis hominis; flatu, sicut per tibiam, vel quid eiusmodi; pulsu, sicut per citharam, vel quid eiusmodi. NuUum itaque genus hic praetermissum est: nam vox est in choro, fiatus in tuba, pulsus in cithara; tanquam mens, spiritus, corpus; thirst per similarities, not per proprietates. Quod ergo proposuit, Laúdate Dominion in sanctis eius, quibus hoc dixit, nisi eis ipsis? Et in quibus ut Deum laudent, nisi in seipsis?

Vos enim sancti eius, inquit, virtus eius estis, sed quam fecit in vobis; et potentatus eius, et multitudo magnitudeinis eius, quam fecit et ostendit in vobis. Vos estis tuba, psalterium, cithara, tympanum, chorus, chordae, et organum, et cymbala iubilationis bene sonantia, quia consonantia. Vos estis haec omnia: nihil hic vile, nihil hic transitorium, nihil ludicrum cogitetur. Et quia sapere secundum carnem mors est, Omnis spiritus laudet Dominum.
PRAYER THAT SAINT AUGUSTINE USED TO RECITE AT THE END OF EVERY SERMON AND EXHIBITION, AS WARNED TO BE INCHORED IN SOME PSALM

Returning to the Lord, God the omnipotent Father, let us give him with a pure heart, as far as our littleness allows us, the most heartfelt and sincere thanks, asking his particular goodness, with all our strength, to deign to hear our prayers according to his good pleasure and to also remove with his power the enemy from all our thoughts and works; May he increase our faith, govern our mind, give us spiritual thoughts and lead us to his blessedness through his Son Jesus Christ, our Lord, who lives and reigns with Him, God, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, forever and ever. Amen. So be it. SANCTI AURELII AUGUSTINI ORATIO QUAM POS SINGULES SERMONS ATQUE TRACTATUS DICERE CONSUEVIT
